meta.source: PL-300 Practice Question Bank (300 original questions, 6 sets, 5 case studies)
meta.notes: id is s<set>q<number in set>. Every option carries its own explanation; 'reference' holds the Concept line.

cases.title: Contoso Retail
cases.text:
Contoso Retail sells products through physical stores and an online shop. The company is building a Power BI semantic model that must use a star schema.
Data sources
• Orders: an on-premises SQL Server table that has about 200 million rows. The OrderDateTime column is a datetime value with second precision. Reports analyze orders by day only.
• Products and Categories: two tables in the same SQL Server database. Products has the columns ProductID, ProductName, and CategoryID. Categories has the columns CategoryID and CategoryName.
• Deliveries: a partner uploads one CSV file every day to a SharePoint Online folder. All files have the columns DeliveryID, OrderID, DeliveredOn, and Status.
• Budget: an Excel workbook in OneDrive for Business that contains one table with the columns Category, Jan, Feb, Mar, and so on up to Dec, followed by a Total column.
Requirements
• The model must refresh daily without any manual file handling.
• The size of the model must be minimized.
• Only orders from the last three years are required.
• Budgets must be analyzable by month and by category.

cases.title: Fabrikam Logistics
cases.text:
Fabrikam Logistics ships goods between warehouses around the world. You are designing a semantic model in Power BI Desktop.
Tables
• Shipments (fact): ShipmentID, OriginKey, DestinationKey, ShipDate, DeliveryDate, WeightKg, Cost.
• Locations (dimension): LocationKey, City, Country. Both OriginKey and DestinationKey in Shipments contain LocationKey values.
• Date (dimension): Date, Year, MonthName, MonthNumber. The model must use this single Date table.
Requirements
• Report authors must analyze shipments by origin location and by destination location independently in the same visual, for example a matrix that shows origin country on the rows and destination country on the columns.
• All date-based visuals must use ShipDate by default. Some measures must use DeliveryDate.
• Users must be able to choose, in one visual, whether the visual shows Total Cost, Total Weight, or Shipment Count.
• Users must be able to enter a fuel surcharge percentage and see how Total Cost changes.
• The values in the Country column must plot correctly on map visuals.

cases.title: Wingtip Toys performance
cases.text:
Wingtip Toys uses a Power BI Import model. The Sales table has 120 million rows at transaction level.
Reports use only month and product for analysis. You run Performance Analyzer on the Overview page, which has 20 visuals. The relevant results, in milliseconds, are shown below.
Sales by Product matrix: DAX query 4,200 / Visual display 90 / Other 30
Orders scatter plot (150,000 data points): DAX query 120 / Visual display 3,900 / Other 60
Twelve Region KPI cards: DAX query 80 each / Visual display 20 each / Other 2,800 each
After you change a measure, repeated tests are faster than the first run. You suspect that the data engine cache affects your results.

cases.title: Northwind Outfitters
cases.text:
Northwind Outfitters sells outdoor equipment through stores and online. You are building a Power BI report that uses a semantic model with the tables Sales, Product, Store, and Date. The Product table has the columns ProductName, Category, and Subcategory.
The report has two pages named Summary and Product Detail.
Requirements:
• Users must be able to right-click any product in a visual on the Summary page and open the Product Detail page filtered to that product only.
• Regional managers view the report in the Power BI mobile app on phones held in portrait orientation.
• Some report users depend on screen readers.
• The Region slicer on the Summary page must also filter the Product Detail page.
• When a user hovers over a product in the bar chart on the Summary page, a small line chart must show the monthly Total Sales of that product.

cases.title: Tailspin Wholesale
cases.text:
Tailspin Wholesale distributes goods to retailers. The company uses Power BI Pro licenses, and it has a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label named Confidential.
A Sales semantic model in Import mode loads data from a SQL Server instance that is hosted in the company's data center. The semantic model is published to a workspace named Sales Analytics. The data must be refreshed four times a day.
The model contains a table named SecurityMap that has the columns Email and Region. The table lists which region each of the 40 regional managers is responsible for. The assignments change several times a year. Regional managers must see only the data of their own region.
Six hundred employees need to consume the reports in read-only mode from one location. Executives must see an additional Executive Summary page that other employees must not see.
The data governance team must be the only group that can mark the Sales semantic model as an official, trusted source.
Every report that is created from the Sales semantic model must also be classified as Confidential.

questions.stem:
You need to create a small mapping table that has three rows and two columns directly in the model by using DAX. The table must not depend on any external source.
Which function should you use?

options.text: CALENDAR
options.explanation: CALENDAR creates a table of dates.

options.text: GENERATESERIES
options.explanation: GENERATESERIES creates one column of numbers or dates in steps.

options.text: ROW
options.explanation: ROW returns a single row, so it cannot create three rows directly.

options.text: DATATABLE
options.explanation: DATATABLE lets you define the columns, their data types, and a set of literal rows.

questions.stem:
The Products table has a column that contains the URLs of product pictures. You need the pictures to appear in a table visual instead of the URLs.
What should you do?

options.text: Set the data type of the column to Binary in Power Query
options.explanation: Binary is a data type for binary data. The URL is text and is rendered by using the data category.

options.text: Add a slicer for the column and display it as a gallery
options.explanation: A slicer filters data and does not display images in a table.

options.text: Set the data category of the column to Image URL
options.explanation: The Image URL data category tells Power BI to render the URL as an image in visuals that support images, such as a table.

options.text: Set the Summarize by property to Count in the model
options.explanation: Summarize by affects aggregation and does not display images.

questions.stem:
The Inventory table stores the units on hand for each product once per day. A report shows the units by month. Each month must show the units on hand on the last day of the month, not the sum of the daily values.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: AVERAGE(Inventory[Units])
options.explanation: AVERAGE returns the average daily balance and not the closing balance.

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Inventory[Units]), LASTDATE('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: LASTDATE returns the last date in the current filter context, which is the last day of each month. The measure is semi-additive across time.

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Inventory[Units]), FIRSTDATE('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: FIRSTDATE returns the opening balance of the month.

options.text: SUM(Inventory[Units])
options.explanation: SUM adds the daily balances of the month, which overstates the stock.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Your organization wants every user to select a sensitivity label before they publish content in Power BI, so that no content stays unlabeled.
What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A workspace app audience
options.explanation: Audiences control who sees content in an app and do not require labels.

options.text: A scheduled refresh on every semantic model
options.explanation: A scheduled refresh updates data and is not related to labels.

options.text: Row-level security on every semantic model
options.explanation: RLS restricts the rows that users see and does not classify content.

options.text: A mandatory labeling policy in Microsoft Purview
options.explanation: A label policy in Microsoft Purview can require users to apply a label to their content.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You need to restrict a semantic model so that users in the Sales West group see only the data of the West region, in every report that uses the model. You are working in Power BI Desktop.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a slicer for Region to each report page, and then hide the slicer from users
options.explanation: A hidden slicer is a report feature that users with edit permission can change, and it is not a security feature.

options.text: Create a calculated column that contains the value West in the Sales table
options.explanation: A calculated column does not restrict any data.

options.text: Create a role in Manage roles, and define a table filter DAX expression for West
options.explanation: A role with a table filter expression restricts the rows that members of the role can see, and it applies to every report that uses the model.

options.text: Add a report-level filter on Region in each of the reports that use the model
options.explanation: A report-level filter is not security. Users who can edit the report can remove it, and other reports are not affected.

questions.reference: Row-level security in Power BI Desktop

questions.stem:
A metric in a scorecard must change its status to At risk automatically when its value is lower than 90 percent of the target, and to On track when the value is at or above the target.
What should you configure?

options.text: Status rules on the metric
options.explanation: Status rules define conditions on the value or the target that set the status of the metric automatically.

options.text: A calculated column in the model
options.explanation: A calculated column is evaluated at refresh, and it cannot change the status of a metric in a scorecard.

options.text: A data alert on a dashboard tile
options.explanation: A data alert sends a notification when a tile value crosses a threshold and does not set the status of a metric.

options.text: Row-level security on the scorecard
options.explanation: Row-level security limits the data that users see and does not set a status.

questions.stem:
You create the first calculation group in Power BI Desktop. Desktop displays a message that implicit measures must be handled before you continue.
What does Power BI require for a model that has calculation groups?

options.text: Implicit measures must be discouraged in the model.
options.explanation: Calculation groups work with explicit measures. Power BI requires the model to discourage implicit measures so that visuals do not use implicit aggregations that calculation items cannot modify.

options.text: All relationships must be bidirectional.
options.explanation: Relationship direction is not a requirement for calculation groups.

options.text: Auto date/time must be enabled.
options.explanation: Auto date/time is unrelated to calculation groups.

options.text: Every table in the model must be marked as a date table first
options.explanation: Only a table that supplies dates can be marked as a date table, and this is not a requirement here.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the number of customers whose total sales are greater than 10,000. [Total Sales] is an existing measure.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: COUNTROWS(FILTER(Customers, [Total Sales] > 10000))
options.explanation: FILTER evaluates the measure for each customer, because the row context is converted into a filter context. COUNTROWS counts the customers that meet the condition.

options.text: CALCULATE(DISTINCTCOUNT(Sales[CustomerKey]), [Total Sales] > 10000)
options.explanation: A Boolean filter in CALCULATE cannot reference a measure, so this expression is not valid.

options.text: COUNTROWS(Customers) > 10000
options.explanation: This compares the number of customers with 10,000 and returns TRUE or FALSE.

options.text: COUNTROWS(FILTER(Sales, Sales[Amount] > 10000))
options.explanation: This counts order lines whose amount is greater than 10,000, not customers.

questions.stem:
You reduce the granularity of a fact table from transaction level to one row per product per month, to reduce the model size.
Which requirement can no longer be met after this change?

options.text: Filtering the sales by product category in a slicer
options.explanation: Product category filtering is available through the Product dimension.

options.text: Showing total sales by product and month on a dashboard
options.explanation: Sales by product and month is the grain that the aggregated table still supports.

options.text: Analyzing a single customer's individual transactions
options.explanation: After aggregation, individual transactions no longer exist in the model, so drilling down to a single customer's transactions is not possible.

options.text: Showing year-to-date sales by product and category
options.explanation: Year-to-date sales can still be computed by adding up the monthly values.

questions.stem:
A key influencers visual shows that customers with a month-to-month contract are more likely to churn. The marketing team now wants to see combinations of attributes, for example a month-to-month contract together with fiber internet, that describe groups of customers with a high churn rate.
What should you use in the visual?

options.text: The Key influencers tab
options.explanation: The Key influencers tab ranks the individual factors, and it does not show combinations of factors as segments.

options.text: A bookmark that filters on ContractType
options.explanation: A bookmark stores a state of the report and does not discover segments.

options.text: A reference line on the visual
options.explanation: A reference line marks a value on an axis and does not calculate segments.

options.text: The Top segments tab
options.explanation: The Top segments tab groups customers into segments that are defined by combinations of factors and shows which segments have the highest rate of the outcome.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model in Import mode gets its data from a SQL Server instance in your company's data center. The semantic model is published to the Power BI service and must refresh every night.
What must you do to enable the scheduled refresh?

options.text: Change the storage mode of the tables to Direct Lake in Power BI Desktop and republish
options.explanation: Direct Lake is for data in a Fabric lakehouse or warehouse, and it is not a way to reach an on-premises SQL Server.

options.text: Install an on-premises data gateway, and map the data source to it in the settings
options.explanation: The Power BI service cannot reach a data source on a private network. A gateway provides the connection so that the scheduled refresh can load the data.

options.text: Publish the semantic model to My workspace only, and set up the refresh there
options.explanation: The workspace does not remove the need for a gateway when the source is on-premises.

options.text: Enable the Q&A feature in the semantic model settings of the service
options.explanation: Q&A is a natural language feature and has no influence on refreshing data.

questions.stem:
The following measure is slow, and the expression that calculates the previous year's sales appears three times.

{{code}}

You need to improve the performance without changing the result.
What should you do?
questions.code:
YoY % =
IF(
    CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) = 0,
    BLANK(),
    ([Total Sales] - CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])))
    / CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))
)

options.text: Store the repeated expression in a variable, and reference the variable.
options.explanation: A variable is evaluated once and reused, so the previous year's sales are calculated one time instead of three times.

options.text: Set the relationship between Date and Sales to bidirectional to speed up the filtering
options.explanation: Bidirectional filters can reduce performance, and they do not remove the repeated calculation.

options.text: Wrap the whole expression in IFERROR.
options.explanation: IFERROR adds an extra evaluation and does not remove the repeated calculations.

options.text: Convert the measure to a calculated column.
options.explanation: A calculated column cannot respond to the filter context of the visual, so the result would change.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
You create two bookmarks that show or hide visuals on a page. Users must be able to switch between the bookmarks without losing the slicer selections that they have made.
What should you do?

options.text: Disable the Data option for each bookmark.
options.explanation: The Data option saves filters, slicers, sorting, and drill location. With it disabled, applying the bookmark does not reset those items, and only the visibility changes.

options.text: Enable the Current page option for each bookmark.
options.explanation: The Current page option controls whether the bookmark moves the user to the page where it was created, and it does not influence the slicer state.

options.text: Enable the All visuals option for each bookmark.
options.explanation: All visuals applies the saved state of every visual on the page, including the slicers. Together with the Data option, the saved slicer selections would be restored and the users' selections would be replaced.

options.text: Disable the Display option for each bookmark.
options.explanation: The Display option saves visibility and spotlight. Disabling it would stop the bookmark from showing and hiding the visuals.

questions.stem:
You create a calculation group named Time Intelligence. You add a calculation item named YTD that must work with any measure that the user places in a visual.
Which expression should you use for the YTD item?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESYTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: This expression always evaluates Total Sales, so the item would work with only one measure.

options.text: CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE(), DATESYTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: SELECTEDMEASURE returns the measure that is currently being evaluated, so the item applies the YTD filter to any measure.

options.text: SELECTEDMEASUREFORMATSTRING()
options.explanation: SELECTEDMEASUREFORMATSTRING returns the format string of the current measure and not a value.

options.text: SELECTEDMEASURENAME()
options.explanation: SELECTEDMEASURENAME returns the name of the measure as text and does not apply a date filter.

questions.stem:
A scatter chart plots each customer by Total Sales on the X axis and Total Profit on the Y axis. You need Power BI to find groups of customers that behave similarly and color the points by group.
What should you do?

options.text: Add an average line to the scatter chart from the Analytics pane
options.explanation: An average line marks the mean and does not form groups of points.

options.text: Turn on error bars for both axes from the Analytics pane
options.explanation: Error bars show the uncertainty of a value and do not create clusters.

options.text: Enable Automatically find clusters on the scatter chart.
options.explanation: Clustering algorithms find groups of similar data points and assign them to clusters. The clusters are displayed on a scatter chart in different colors.

options.text: Add the Customer field to the Legend well of the scatter chart
options.explanation: Using Customer as a legend would give each customer its own color, which does not group them by behavior.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: Before you publish a model, you need to check what a user in the West role sees in your report. What should you do in Power BI Desktop?

options.text: Add the user to the workspace as an Admin and ask them to check
options.explanation: An Admin is not restricted by RLS, so they would see all of the data.

options.text: On the Modeling tab, select View as and select the West role.
options.explanation: View as applies one or more roles to the report in Desktop so that you can see the restricted data.

options.text: Remove all roles from the model and republish it to the service
options.explanation: Removing roles removes security and does not test it.

options.text: Turn on Performance Analyzer and refresh the visuals of the page
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer measures visual load times, and it does not simulate a role.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You are the owner of a semantic model. You want to receive an email notification when a scheduled refresh fails, and you want a colleague to also be notified.
What should you configure?

options.text: Row-level security members that include the owner and the colleague
options.explanation: RLS members control which rows users see.

options.text: Set refresh failure notifications in the model settings, and add the colleague as a contact
options.explanation: The refresh settings let you send failure notifications to the owner and to other contacts.

options.text: A data alert on a dashboard tile that shows the status of the refresh
options.explanation: A data alert reacts to the value of a tile and not to a refresh failure.

options.text: An email subscription to the report for the owner and the colleague
options.explanation: A subscription sends snapshots of a report and does not report refresh failures.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem: A Year column in the Date table has a Whole Number data type. When you add it to a table visual, Power BI shows the sum of the years. The column must remain a whole number so that it sorts correctly. What should you do?

options.text: Hide the column in report view.
options.explanation: Hiding the column removes it from the field list. It does not change aggregation, and you want to use the column.

options.text: Change the data type to Text.
options.explanation: Changing to Text would break the requirement that the column remains a whole number.

options.text: Change the format of the column to Whole number.
options.explanation: The format only changes how values are displayed. It does not change how the column is aggregated.

options.text: Set Summarize by to Don't summarize.
options.explanation: Don't summarize prevents Power BI from aggregating the column automatically while keeping it as a whole number.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
The Sales table has one row for each order line, and it contains a CustomerKey column. You need a measure that returns the number of different customers who placed orders.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: COUNT(Sales[CustomerKey])
options.explanation: COUNT counts every non-blank CustomerKey value, including repeated values, so customers with several order lines are counted several times.

options.text: COUNTA(Sales[CustomerKey])
options.explanation: COUNTA also counts every non-blank row and does not remove duplicates.

options.text: DISTINCTCOUNT(Sales[CustomerKey])
options.explanation: DISTINCTCOUNT counts each customer once, regardless of the number of order lines.

options.text: COUNTROWS(Customers)
options.explanation: COUNTROWS(Customers) counts all customers, including those who never ordered.

questions.stem:
A CSV file contains a ZipCode column with values such as 02134. After import, Power Query shows 2134 because it automatically added a Changed Type step that converted the column to Whole Number. You need the five-digit zip codes with their leading zeros.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a custom column that adds a 0 before each value in ZipCode
options.explanation: Adding a fixed 0 would be wrong for zip codes that already have five digits.

options.text: Set the data category of ZipCode to Postal Code in the model
options.explanation: Data category affects how Power BI treats the field in visuals such as maps. It does not change the stored values.

options.text: Edit the Changed Type step so that ZipCode uses the Text type
options.explanation: Changing the type in the existing step keeps the original text from the file, so the leading zeros are never lost.

options.text: Add a new step after Changed Type that converts ZipCode to Text.
options.explanation: A later conversion to Text starts from the numbers that were already created, so the leading zeros are already gone.

questions.reference: Data type detection in Power Query

questions.stem:
A telecom company has a Customers table that has the columns Churned (Yes or No), ContractType, Tenure, InternetService, and MonthlyCharge. You need to identify which customer attributes are most strongly associated with customers who churn.
Which visual should you use, and what should you add to the Analyze field well?

options.text: Scatter chart, with Churned in the X Axis well
options.explanation: A scatter chart shows the relationship between numeric values and does not rank the factors that influence a category.

options.text: Smart narrative, with Churned in the Analyze well
options.explanation: A smart narrative summarizes the visuals of a page in text and does not analyze the drivers of an outcome.

options.text: Decomposition tree, with Churned in the Analyze well and the attributes in the Explain by well
options.explanation: The Analyze well of a decomposition tree expects a measure that is broken down by categories, and the visual does not rank influence on a categorical outcome.

options.text: Key influencers, with Churned in the Analyze well and the attributes in the Explain by well
options.explanation: The key influencers visual analyzes which fields influence a chosen outcome, such as Churned equal to Yes, based on the fields in Explain by.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You add a filter on the OrderDate column of the Sales table that uses the RangeStart and RangeEnd parameters for incremental refresh. You must ensure that no row is loaded twice in two consecutive partitions.
Which filter should you apply?

options.text: OrderDate is equal to RangeStart or OrderDate is equal to RangeEnd
options.explanation: This would return only rows that fall exactly on the boundaries.

options.text: OrderDate is greater than or equal to RangeStart and OrderDate is less than or equal to RangeEnd
options.explanation: Making both boundaries inclusive would load a row that equals RangeEnd in two adjacent partitions.

options.text: OrderDate is greater than or equal to RangeStart and OrderDate is less than RangeEnd
options.explanation: Using one inclusive boundary and one exclusive boundary guarantees that a row that falls exactly on a partition boundary belongs to only one partition. Microsoft documents this form, with RangeStart inclusive and RangeEnd exclusive.

options.text: OrderDate is greater than RangeStart and OrderDate is less than RangeEnd
options.explanation: Making both boundaries exclusive would skip the rows that fall exactly on a boundary, so they would not be loaded in any partition.

questions.stem:
A table visual shows Total Sales by month. You need to add a column that shows the running total of the monthly sales, without creating a measure in the semantic model.
Which function should you use in a visual calculation?

options.text: SUMX
options.explanation: SUMX is an iterator that requires a table and an expression, and it does not provide a running total across the visual.

options.text: RUNNINGSUM
options.explanation: RUNNINGSUM adds up the values in the visual cumulatively along an axis, for example [Total Sales] across the months.

options.text: DATESYTD
options.explanation: DATESYTD returns a table of dates for use in CALCULATE and does not calculate a running total.

options.text: TOTALYTD
options.explanation: TOTALYTD is a time intelligence function for model measures and resets each year.

questions.stem:
A Transactions table has one row per transaction with the columns CustomerID, OrderDate, and Amount. You need a query that returns one row per customer with the total Amount and the number of transactions.
What should you use in Power Query?

options.text: Remove Duplicates on CustomerID, and then add an index column
options.explanation: Remove Duplicates keeps one row per customer but discards the other rows instead of summarizing them.

options.text: Group By with two aggregations: Sum of Amount and Count Rows
options.explanation: Group By summarizes rows by CustomerID. The advanced option lets you add several aggregations, such as a sum and a row count, in the same step.

options.text: Pivot Column on CustomerID with Amount as the values column
options.explanation: Pivot Column would turn each customer into a column, which does not produce one row per customer.

options.text: Merge Queries with the table itself, and expand the Amount column
options.explanation: Merging a table with itself adds matching rows. It does not aggregate.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A regional manager wants to receive an email with a snapshot of a report page every morning at 7:00, without opening the Power BI service.
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Analyze in Excel connection that refreshes every morning
options.explanation: Analyze in Excel connects Excel to the semantic model and does not send emails.

options.text: Create a data alert on the report that triggers every morning
options.explanation: A data alert is triggered when a value reaches a threshold and does not follow a time schedule.

options.text: Publish the report to the web and send the link every morning
options.explanation: Publish to web makes the report public and does not send emails.

options.text: Create an email subscription for the report page.
options.explanation: A subscription emails a snapshot of the report page on a schedule that you define, and it includes a link to the report.

questions.stem: A scorecard has a Revenue metric for each of five regions. You need a company-level Revenue metric whose value is the sum of the five regional metrics and updates when the regional values change. What should you do?

options.text: Add a slicer to the scorecard and select all of the regions in the slicer
options.explanation: A scorecard does not use slicers, and a slicer would not aggregate the values.

options.text: Create five dashboards and pin each of the regional metrics to its own dashboard
options.explanation: Dashboards do not aggregate metric values.

options.text: Create a measure in the scorecard that uses SUMX over the five regions
options.explanation: A scorecard does not contain DAX measures. DAX belongs to the semantic model.

options.text: Create the regional metrics as submetrics of the company metric, and set a rollup
options.explanation: A metric can have submetrics, and rollups aggregate the values of the submetrics into the parent, for example as a sum.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
An intranet page in SharePoint Online must display a Power BI report. Only employees who already have permission to the report in Power BI should see the data on the page.
What should you use?

options.text: Publish to web, and copy the embed code into the page
options.explanation: Publish to web creates a public link without authentication.

options.text: An anonymous link to the report that is pasted into the page
options.explanation: An anonymous link does not check the identity or permissions of the user.

options.text: A screenshot of the report that is updated by hand
options.explanation: A screenshot is static and does not use permissions or live data.

options.text: The Power BI web part, or the embed option for SharePoint Online
options.explanation: The embed option for SharePoint Online shows the report to users who sign in, and the report permissions of each user are respected.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Three managers need access to a single report that is in a workspace. They must not be added to the workspace, and they do not need access to the other items in it.
What should you do?

options.text: Publish the workspace app.
options.explanation: An app is a distribution method for a curated set of content, and it would be unnecessary for sharing one report with three people.

options.text: Add the managers as Contributors of the workspace.
options.explanation: Contributors can edit all the items in the workspace.

options.text: Share the report directly with the three managers.
options.explanation: Sharing a report gives specific users access to that item only, without adding them to the workspace.

options.text: Add the managers as Viewers of the workspace.
options.explanation: Workspace Viewers can see all the content of the workspace, which is more than the requirement.

questions.stem:
While you author a report that has many visuals on a page, every change that you make causes all the visuals to refresh, and editing is slow.
Which feature should you use?

options.text: Pause visuals in the Optimize ribbon
options.explanation: Pause visuals stops visuals from refreshing queries while you make changes. You can resume them when you are ready.

options.text: Page navigation
options.explanation: Page navigation buttons move users between pages.

options.text: Persistent filters
options.explanation: Persistent filters keep user filter selections between sessions. They do not affect authoring speed.

options.text: Selection pane
options.explanation: The Selection pane controls the visibility and order of objects but does not stop queries.

questions.stem: You merge Orders and Customers on the Email column. The result contains no matches for customers whose email addresses differ only in letter case, such as Sam@Fabrikam.com and sam@fabrikam.com. What should you do?

options.text: Remove the Customers query from the model and use the Orders query only
options.explanation: Removing the query does not fix matching.

options.text: Change the data type of both Email columns to Any.
options.explanation: The Any data type does not change how values are compared.

options.text: Change the join kind to Full Outer so that the rows that do not match are kept
options.explanation: A different join kind changes which rows are returned but does not make the values match.

options.text: Convert both Email columns to lowercase before the merge.
options.explanation: Merge comparisons are case-sensitive. Standardizing the case in both tables makes equal addresses identical.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model is in a Power BI Pro workspace that is not on a Premium capacity. The business requires it to refresh every 30 minutes between 06:00 and 20:00, which is 29 refreshes a day.
What should you do?

options.text: Configure 29 scheduled refreshes in the settings of the semantic model in the Pro workspace
options.explanation: A Pro workspace on shared capacity cannot be configured for 29 scheduled refreshes.

options.text: Move the workspace to a Premium capacity or Premium Per User, which allows more daily refreshes
options.explanation: In shared capacity the number of scheduled refreshes is limited to 8 per day. Premium capacity and Premium Per User allow up to 48 refreshes per day.

options.text: Use the personal gateway instead of the standard gateway for the refresh
options.explanation: The type of gateway does not change the number of refreshes that are allowed.

options.text: Switch the semantic model to Import mode and publish it again to the workspace
options.explanation: The semantic model is already refreshed, so Import mode is implied, and republishing does not change the limit.

questions.stem:
A line chart shows the average monthly temperature reported by a sensor. The model contains a measure for the lowest reading and a measure for the highest reading of each month. You need to show the range of the readings around the average for each month.
What should you add from the Analytics pane?

options.text: Symmetry shading on the axis of the line chart for the readings
options.explanation: Symmetry shading is for scatter charts to show which side of the diagonal a point is on.

options.text: A percentile line at the 90th percentile
options.explanation: A percentile line draws a single line at a percentile of the values in the chart, and it does not show a range per data point.

options.text: A constant line at the average value of the monthly readings
options.explanation: A constant line draws one fixed value across the chart and does not show a range per month.

options.text: Error bars with upper bound and lower bound measures
options.explanation: Error bars show the range around a data point. You can set the upper and lower bounds to fields or measures.

questions.stem: In a Quantity column, null means that no units were sold, and the business wants those rows to count as zero in an average quantity per row. Currently AVERAGE ignores the null rows, and the result is too high. What should you do?

options.text: Replace null with -1.
options.explanation: A value of -1 would reduce the average below the correct value.

options.text: Replace null with 0 in the Quantity column.
options.explanation: Replacing null with 0 makes AVERAGE include those rows with a value of zero, which produces the intended result.

options.text: Remove the rows that have null in the Quantity column.
options.explanation: Removing the rows would exclude them from the average, which keeps the result too high.

options.text: Change the Quantity column data type to Text.
options.explanation: Text columns cannot be averaged.

questions.stem:
A City column in a customer table is typed by hand. You suspect that some entries are misspelled variants of valid cities, such as "Kuala Lumpr", that appear only once or twice.
You need to find these likely typos by using Power Query Editor profiling.
What should you review?

options.text: The Count value shown in Column statistics for the column
options.explanation: Count is the total number of rows. It does not identify unusual values.

options.text: The least frequent entries in the Value distribution chart
options.explanation: Misspelled entries occur rarely, so they appear at the bottom of the Value distribution chart. Sorting that chart by count surfaces them.

options.text: The percentage of Valid values in the Column quality bar
options.explanation: The typos are still valid text values, so Column quality does not flag them.

options.text: The Average and Standard deviation values in Column statistics
options.explanation: Average and standard deviation describe numeric data. They do not apply to a text column of city names.

questions.stem:
You need a grid of line charts, one for each sales region. All charts must use the same axes so that the trends can be compared.
What should you use?

options.text: A line chart with a legend
options.explanation: A legend puts all regions in one chart, which can become cluttered.

options.text: A scatter chart with a play axis
options.explanation: A play axis animates a scatter chart over time and does not create a grid of charts.

options.text: Small multiples on a line chart
options.explanation: Small multiples split a chart into a grid of similar charts, one for each value of a field, with consistent axes.

options.text: A funnel chart
options.explanation: A funnel chart displays stages and not trends over time.

questions.stem:
You create visual calculations in a report.
Which two statements about visual calculations are true? Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: A visual calculation can reference fields that are in the visual, including other visual calculations.
options.explanation: Visual calculations work with the data that is in the visual, so they can reference its fields and previously defined visual calculations.

options.text: A visual calculation can reference any column of the model, even if the column is not in the visual.
options.explanation: A visual calculation cannot reference model fields that are not in the visual.

options.text: A visual calculation is defined and stored on the visual, not in the semantic model.
options.explanation: A visual calculation belongs to the visual where it was created, and it is not added to the model.

options.text: A visual calculation can be reused in any other visual of the report.
options.explanation: A visual calculation exists only in its visual and cannot be used by other visuals.

options.text: A visual calculation must be created in the model view.
options.explanation: Visual calculations are created in the report view by using the visual's calculation editor.

questions.stem:
You want to write, test, and run DAX queries against your semantic model in Power BI Desktop, for example to evaluate a table expression or to verify a measure.
Which view should you use?

options.text: Report view
options.explanation: Report view is used for building report pages.

options.text: Table view
options.explanation: Table view displays the data of the loaded tables and does not run queries.

options.text: DAX query view
options.explanation: DAX query view lets you write and run DAX queries, including EVALUATE statements, and see the results in a grid.

options.text: Model view
options.explanation: Model view shows tables and relationships.

questions.stem:
You publish a report that has a report-level filter on Region. Report viewers must still be able to see the filter, but they must not be able to change or remove it.
What should you do?

options.text: Convert the filter to a slicer on the page
options.explanation: A slicer is meant for user interaction, so viewers could change it.

options.text: Lock the filter in the Filters pane
options.explanation: Locking a filter prevents viewers from changing or removing it, and the filter remains in effect.

options.text: Rename the filter to indicate that it is required
options.explanation: Renaming does not protect a filter.

options.text: Hide the Filters pane from the report viewers
options.explanation: Hiding the Filters pane removes the filters from the viewers' sight, so the filter would no longer be visible. Locking is the feature that keeps a filter visible but unchangeable.

questions.stem:
A bar chart shows sales by product. You need the chart to show only the five products with the highest Total Sales, even though Total Sales is not the field on the axis.
What should you do?

options.text: Sort the chart in descending order by Total Sales, without a filter
options.explanation: Sorting changes the order, but it still shows all the products.

options.text: Add a relative date filter that keeps only the most recent products
options.explanation: A relative date filter limits the dates and does not limit the number of products.

options.text: Apply a basic filter on the Product field and select the five products manually
options.explanation: A manual selection does not update when the top products change.

options.text: Apply a Top N filter to the Product field with the value 5, by Total Sales
options.explanation: A Top N filter keeps the top items of a field according to a measure that you choose, and it updates when the data changes.

questions.stem:
A source system occasionally adds new columns to a table. Your query must always load only the 12 columns that you selected, even when the source gains new columns.
Which two commands should you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Choose Columns
options.explanation: Choose Columns keeps an explicit list of columns, so new source columns are not loaded.

options.text: Remove Other Columns
options.explanation: Remove Other Columns also keeps only the selected columns and drops everything else, including columns added later.

options.text: Rename Columns
options.explanation: Renaming does not control which columns are loaded.

options.text: Hide in report view
options.explanation: Hiding a column only affects the report view. The column is still loaded into the model.

options.text: Remove Columns
options.explanation: Remove Columns lists the columns to delete. A new source column is not in that list, so it would be loaded.

questions.stem:
Your company's fiscal year ends on June 30. You need a measure that returns the fiscal year-to-date total of Total Sales.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: TOTALYTD([Total Sales], 'Date'[Date], "6/30")
options.explanation: The optional year-end date argument tells TOTALYTD that the year ends on June 30, so the accumulation restarts every July 1.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the current period back by one year. It does not accumulate the total.

options.text: TOTALYTD([Total Sales], 'Date'[Date])
options.explanation: Without the year-end argument, TOTALYTD uses a calendar year that ends on December 31.

options.text: TOTALMTD([Total Sales], 'Date'[Date])
options.explanation: TOTALMTD accumulates sales from the start of the month and not from the start of the fiscal year.

questions.stem:
You build a report on a shared semantic model that has a live connection. You need to add a local Excel table of regional sales targets so that visuals can combine it with the shared model's data. The original semantic model must remain unchanged.
What should you do?

options.text: Use Get data to add the Excel table while keeping the live connection to the shared semantic model
options.explanation: A pure live connection cannot be combined with additional data sources.

options.text: Select Make changes to this model to create a composite model, and then import the Excel table
options.explanation: Converting the live connection to a DirectQuery connection to the semantic model lets you add other sources such as an Excel file. Your changes are stored in your own composite model, and the original is untouched.

options.text: Ask the model owner to add the targets to the shared model, because a report that uses a live connection cannot be extended
options.explanation: Report authors can extend a shared model by using a composite model, so waiting for the owner is not required.

options.text: Export the semantic model to a .pbix file, import the Excel table, and publish it with the same name.
options.explanation: Re-publishing a copy with the same name creates a duplicate version of the model and defeats the single source of truth.

questions.reference: Composite models on Power BI semantic models

questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the sales from two years before the current period.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATEADD('Date'[Date], -2, YEAR))
options.explanation: DATEADD shifts the current dates back by two years.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATEADD('Date'[Date], 2, YEAR))
options.explanation: A positive interval moves the dates forward in time, so the result is two years in the future.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], PREVIOUSYEAR('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: PREVIOUSYEAR returns the entire previous year and not the same period two years earlier.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the dates by exactly one year.

questions.stem:
You add a custom column that converts a text column named Amount to a number by using Number.From. Some rows contain invalid text, and these rows return an error. You need the custom column to return 0 for those rows instead of an error.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: if Number.From([Amount]) = error then 0 else Number.From([Amount])
options.explanation: M cannot compare a value to error in this way. It has no error literal that can be used in a comparison.

options.text: Number.From(try [Amount] otherwise 0)
options.explanation: The try applies only to reading the Amount field, which does not fail. The conversion still raises the error.

options.text: Number.From([Amount]) otherwise 0
options.explanation: The otherwise keyword is only valid together with try, so this expression is a syntax error.

options.text: try Number.From([Amount]) otherwise 0
options.explanation: try evaluates the conversion and, if it raises an error, otherwise supplies the fallback value 0.

questions.reference: Error handling in Power Query M

questions.stem:
In a composite model, an imported Budget table is related to a DirectQuery Sales table on the Product key. The two tables belong to different source groups.
What is a consequence of this relationship?

options.text: It is treated as a many-to-many relationship that cannot be edited after it is created
options.explanation: The cardinality can be one-to-many. It is labeled limited because of the source groups, not because of many-to-many.

options.text: It is a limited relationship, so the RELATED function cannot be used across it
options.explanation: Relationships between tables from different source groups are limited (weak) relationships. They have restrictions such as not supporting RELATED across them.

options.text: It is a strong relationship that always enforces referential integrity between the tables
options.explanation: Power BI cannot enforce referential integrity across source groups, which is why the relationship is limited.

options.text: It automatically converts both tables to Dual storage mode to improve performance
options.explanation: Storage mode is not changed automatically. You choose it for each table.

questions.stem:
You need to load the partner delivery files so that new daily files are included automatically at each refresh.
What should you do?

options.text: Create one query for each daily file and append them.
options.explanation: One query per file needs a new query every day, and that is also manual work.

options.text: Use the SharePoint folder connector and combine the files.
options.explanation: The SharePoint folder connector reads all files in the folder, and combining them applies the same transformation to each file. New files are picked up at the next refresh.

options.text: Use the Text/CSV connector and change the file name in the query every day.
options.explanation: Changing the file name every day is a manual step, which the requirements forbid.

options.text: Use the SharePoint Online list connector.
options.explanation: The list connector reads SharePoint lists and not files in a document library.

questions.stem:
You need to shape the Budget table so that it can be analyzed by month and by category.
What should you do?

options.text: Transpose the table.
options.explanation: Transposing does not create attribute and value columns, and the months would not be in a single column.

options.text: Unpivot all columns except Category without removing any column.
options.explanation: Without removing Total, the unpivot treats Total as another month, which double counts the budget amounts.

options.text: Pivot the Category column by using the Sum of the values as the aggregate
options.explanation: Pivoting would turn the categories into columns, and it does not produce a month attribute.

options.text: Remove the Total column, and then unpivot all columns except Category.
options.explanation: Removing the Total column first keeps it from being treated as a month. Unpivoting the remaining month columns creates one row per category and month.

questions.stem: You need to minimize the size of the model by reducing the cardinality of the OrderDateTime column. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the datetime column and hide it in report view.
options.explanation: Hiding a column does not remove it from the model, so its size remains.

options.text: Change the data type of OrderDateTime to Text.
options.explanation: Text values are less efficient to store and would not reduce the number of distinct values.

options.text: Split the column into separate hour, minute, and second columns.
options.explanation: Splitting adds three columns and keeps the details that the reports never use.

options.text: Change the data type of OrderDateTime to Date.
options.explanation: Reports use the day only, so converting the datetime to a date removes the time part. This sharply reduces the number of distinct values.

questions.stem: You plan to publish the semantic model and schedule a daily refresh in the Power BI service. For which data sources is an on-premises data gateway required?

options.text: The SQL Server database only
options.explanation: The SQL Server database is on-premises, so the service needs a gateway to reach it. SharePoint Online and OneDrive for Business are cloud sources.

options.text: The SQL Server database, the SharePoint Online folder, and the OneDrive for Business workbook
options.explanation: Neither SharePoint Online nor OneDrive for Business needs a gateway.

options.text: The SQL Server database and the SharePoint Online folder
options.explanation: A SharePoint Online folder is a cloud source and does not need a gateway.

options.text: None of the data sources
options.explanation: The on-premises SQL Server cannot be reached by the service without a gateway.

questions.stem:
You need to make sure that only the orders from the last three years are read from SQL Server, and that the filtering runs at the source instead of in Power Query.
What should you do?

options.text: Load all orders into the model, and create a calculated table that contains only the last three years
options.explanation: A calculated table is built after all the orders have already been loaded, so it does not reduce the model size.

options.text: Apply Table.Buffer to the Orders query before the filtering steps so that they run faster in memory
options.explanation: Table.Buffer loads the table into memory and prevents later steps from folding.

options.text: Load all orders into the model, and apply a relative date filter on every report page and visual
options.explanation: A report-level filter does not reduce the data loaded into the model.

options.text: Filter the dates and remove columns first, and confirm that View Native Query works for the last step
options.explanation: Filter and column-removal steps usually fold into the native SQL query. Keeping them early, and checking View Native Query, confirms that SQL Server does the filtering.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
Customers is on the one side of a one-to-many relationship to Orders. You need a calculated column in Customers that returns the number of orders for each customer.
Which formula should you use?

options.text: COUNTROWS(Orders)
options.explanation: COUNTROWS(Orders) counts all rows in Orders and returns the same number for every customer.

options.text: RELATED(Orders[OrderID])
options.explanation: RELATED works from the many side to the one side. Used here, it does not return a count.

options.text: COUNTROWS(RELATEDTABLE(Orders))
options.explanation: RELATEDTABLE returns the Orders rows related to the current customer, and COUNTROWS counts them.

options.text: SUM(Orders[OrderID])
options.explanation: Summing the order IDs returns a meaningless total of the identifiers for all rows.

questions.stem:
In your star schema, the Sales fact table identifies a store by the two columns StoreID and RegionID. The Stores dimension identifies each store by the same two columns, and neither column is unique on its own. Power BI relationships can use only one column on each side.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a many-to-many relationship on StoreID only, and filter on RegionID in the visuals
options.explanation: A many-to-many relationship on StoreID would match stores from different regions that share the same ID, which produces incorrect results.

options.text: Create two active relationships, one for StoreID and one for RegionID
options.explanation: Only one relationship between two tables can be active, and two single-column relationships would not uniquely identify a store.

options.text: Create a bidirectional relationship on RegionID between the two tables
options.explanation: Cross-filter direction does not make a non-unique column valid as a key.

options.text: Add a column that combines StoreID and RegionID in each table, and relate on it
options.explanation: A concatenated key column in each table provides a single column that is unique on the dimension side, which allows a one-to-many relationship.

questions.stem:
You need a visual that shows the proportion of total sales by product category and subcategory, by using nested rectangles whose sizes are proportional to the sales.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Funnel chart
options.explanation: A funnel chart displays values across stages of a process.

options.text: Donut chart
options.explanation: A donut chart shows the share of one level of categories and does not nest subcategories as rectangles.

options.text: Gauge
options.explanation: A gauge shows a single value against a minimum, maximum, and target.

options.text: Treemap
options.explanation: A treemap displays hierarchical data as nested rectangles that are sized by value.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
Your scheduled refresh uses a standard gateway that is installed on one server. When the server is restarted for maintenance, the refresh fails. You need the refresh to continue when one gateway server is offline.
What should you do?

options.text: Add additional gateway members to create a gateway cluster.
options.explanation: A gateway cluster has several members. If one member is offline, requests are sent to another member, which provides high availability.

options.text: Disable the credentials of the data source to avoid the authentication failure
options.explanation: Removing the credentials makes the refresh fail.

options.text: Increase the refresh timeout of the semantic model to the maximum value
options.explanation: A longer timeout does not help if the gateway is not reachable.

options.text: Change the gateway to personal mode and install it on a second computer
options.explanation: A personal gateway runs on one user's computer and offers no high availability.

questions.stem:
A Segment Selector table contains the values Retail, Wholesale, and Online. The table has no relationship to the Customers table, which has a Segment column. You need a measure that returns Total Sales for the segments that the user selects in a slicer based on Segment Selector.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], KEEPFILTERS(VALUES('Segment Selector'[Segment])))
options.explanation: KEEPFILTERS on the selector values filters the Segment Selector table only, and that table has no relationship to Customers.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], USERELATIONSHIP('Segment Selector'[Segment], Customers[Segment]))
options.explanation: USERELATIONSHIP activates an existing inactive relationship. It cannot create one.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], TREATAS(VALUES('Segment Selector'[Segment]), Customers[Segment]))
options.explanation: TREATAS applies the selected values from the selector table as filters on the Customers[Segment] column, creating a virtual relationship without a physical relationship.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL('Segment Selector'))
options.explanation: ALL removes the filters from the selector table and does not apply the selection to Customers.

questions.stem:
You add a line chart that shows Total Sales by the Date column. In the Analytics pane, the Forecast option is not available. The X axis of the chart uses the Date column on a categorical axis.
What should you do?

options.text: Convert the chart to a stacked column chart.
options.explanation: Forecasting is for line charts, and a stacked column chart does not provide it.

options.text: Change the type of the X axis to Categorical in the Y axis settings.
options.explanation: The axis is already categorical, and changing the Y axis does not change the X axis type.

options.text: Add a second measure to the chart.
options.explanation: Adding more measures does not change the axis type, and a forecast is not available for several series anyway.

options.text: Change the type of the X axis to Continuous.
options.explanation: Forecasting requires a continuous date or time axis. Changing the axis type of a date field to Continuous makes the Forecast option available.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A sales director wants a notification when the value of the Total Sales card on a dashboard falls below 100,000.
What should you do?

options.text: Create an email subscription for the report.
options.explanation: A subscription sends snapshots on a schedule and is not triggered by a threshold.

options.text: Add a data alert to the dashboard tile.
options.explanation: Data alerts are set on dashboard tiles such as cards, gauges, and KPIs, and they notify users when the value crosses the threshold.

options.text: Add a data alert to the card in the report view.
options.explanation: Alerts are not configured on visuals in a report. The visual must be pinned to a dashboard first.

options.text: Create an RLS role with a DAX filter on Total Sales.
options.explanation: RLS filters the rows that users can see and does not send notifications.

questions.stem:
You need to exclude all test customers, where CustomerType equals Test, from every visual on every page of a report. Users must not have to apply any filter themselves.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a visual-level filter on CustomerType to each visual of every page
options.explanation: Visual-level filters would need to be maintained on every visual and could be missed.

options.text: Add a CustomerType filter in the Filters on all pages section of the Filters pane
options.explanation: A report-level filter applies to every page and every visual, and users do not need to do anything.

options.text: Create a bookmark that filters CustomerType, and add a button that applies it
options.explanation: A bookmark is applied only when users select it.

options.text: Add a slicer for CustomerType on each page, and select every value except Test
options.explanation: Slicers depend on user selections, and they must be added to every page.

questions.reference: Filter scopes in the Filters pane

questions.stem:
A CSV file begins with three lines of report title and export notes. The column names appear on the fourth line. You import the file and see Column1, Column2, and so on.
What should you do first to prepare the column names correctly?

options.text: Remove the top three rows.
options.explanation: Removing the top three rows moves the real header row to the first row. After that, you can promote it to headers.

options.text: Transpose the table.
options.explanation: Transposing swaps rows and columns and does not remove the note lines.

options.text: Use First Row as Headers.
options.explanation: Promoting the first row now would turn the title line into the column names.

options.text: Unpivot all columns.
options.explanation: Unpivoting would restructure the data and mix the notes with the data.

questions.reference: Promote headers and remove top rows

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A manager wants to put a link to a Power BI report on the company's public website for anyone on the internet to see. The report uses internal sales data, and the manager says the website visitors do not have Power BI accounts.
What should you recommend?

options.text: Use Publish to web, because only the people who know the link will be able to see the data
options.explanation: A link can be shared or found, and it is not a security control.

options.text: Do not use Publish to web, because anyone with the link can see all of the report's data
options.explanation: Publish to web makes the report and its data accessible to anyone on the internet, and it should not be used for confidential information.

options.text: Use the Viewer role, and ask the visitors to sign in to the workspace
options.explanation: The visitors do not have accounts, so they cannot sign in and be assigned a role.

options.text: Use Publish to web, and enable row-level security to limit what the visitors see
options.explanation: Row-level security is not supported for Publish to web, so it could not limit what visitors see.

questions.stem:
Your finance team needs to produce invoices that are printed or exported to PDF. Each invoice must have a fixed layout, a repeating header row on every page, and must continue across multiple pages when it has many lines.
Which type of report should you create?

options.text: A dashboard
options.explanation: A dashboard is a single page of tiles and is not a printable document.

options.text: A Power BI report with drillthrough pages
options.explanation: Drillthrough pages support navigation to details but not page-based printing.

options.text: A Power BI report with bookmarks
options.explanation: Interactive reports are designed for exploration on screen, not for controlled page breaks.

options.text: A paginated report
options.explanation: Paginated reports are designed for pixel-perfect, printable documents that flow across pages and can repeat headers.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
An organization uses Power BI Pro licenses. Employees who have only a free license must be able to view the reports of a workspace app.
What should you do?

options.text: Move the workspace to a Premium capacity, or to a large enough Fabric capacity
options.explanation: Content in a workspace on a Premium capacity, or on a large enough Fabric capacity, can be viewed by users who have a free license.

options.text: Enable the Build permission on the semantic model for the employees
options.explanation: The Build permission concerns creating content from a semantic model and has no relationship to the license of the viewer.

options.text: Share each report with the employees by using a link that is sent by email
options.explanation: Sharing a report by using a link still requires a Pro license for the viewer when the content is not on a capacity that supports free users.

options.text: Assign the employees the Viewer role in the existing Pro workspace
options.explanation: The Viewer role in a Pro workspace does not remove the license requirement.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem: A workspace app contains a Sales report and a Finance report. Sales staff must see only the Sales report, finance staff must see only the Finance report, and managers must see both. You want to publish one app. What should you do?

options.text: Create audiences in the app, and assign the content for each audience
options.explanation: Audiences let you publish one app and decide which content each group of users can see.

options.text: Create three workspaces, and publish one app from each of the workspaces
options.explanation: Three workspaces and apps would duplicate the content and the maintenance effort.

options.text: Create a bookmark for each group of users in each report of the app
options.explanation: A bookmark stores a view of a report. It does not control which items a user can open.

options.text: Create an RLS role for each group, and add the groups as members
options.explanation: RLS restricts rows of data in a semantic model, and it does not decide which reports are visible in an app.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
You need to add a text summary of the key takeaways of the visuals on a page. The text must update when users change slicers, and it must be generated without a Copilot license.
Which feature should you use?

options.text: A smart narrative visual
options.explanation: A smart narrative visual generates text that summarizes the visuals and updates dynamically as the filters change.

options.text: A Q&A visual
options.explanation: A Q&A visual answers a typed question with a visual and does not summarize the page.

options.text: A text box with the numbers typed in
options.explanation: A text box is static, so the numbers would not follow the slicers.

options.text: A decomposition tree
options.explanation: A decomposition tree visualizes how a measure breaks down by categories and does not write a summary.

questions.stem:
A card visual shows Total Sales. You need its title to read Sales for West when the Region slicer has West selected, and Sales for Multiple regions otherwise.
What should you do?

options.text: Type the title manually, and update it every time that the slicer selection changes
options.explanation: A manual title does not change when users select a different region.

options.text: Set the data category of the Region column to Title in the model view
options.explanation: Data categories do not control visual titles.

options.text: Add a text box next to the card that contains the name of the selected region
options.explanation: A static text box does not update with the slicer unless it is bound to a measure.

options.text: Create a measure for the title text, and use it in the title as a field value
options.explanation: A DAX measure can build text from the selected value, for example by using SELECTEDVALUE. Applying it with conditional formatting makes the title dynamic.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need to calculate the sample standard deviation of the Sales[Amount] column. The data is a sample of a larger population.
Which function should you use?

options.text: VAR.P
options.explanation: VAR.P returns the population variance, not the standard deviation of a sample.

options.text: MEDIAN
options.explanation: MEDIAN returns the middle value and not a standard deviation.

options.text: STDEV.S
options.explanation: STDEV.S calculates the standard deviation of a sample.

options.text: STDEV.P
options.explanation: STDEV.P assumes that the data is the entire population.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A data steward has reviewed a Sales semantic model for quality and wants to indicate to all users in the organization that it is the trusted, official source for sales data. Only authorized reviewers designated by the administrator can do this.
Which endorsement should be applied?

options.text: Shared
options.explanation: Shared is not an endorsement. It describes granting access to others.

options.text: Featured
options.explanation: Featured is a way to highlight content, for example in a workspace or app. It does not indicate a quality review.

options.text: Certified
options.explanation: Certification is applied by authorized reviewers who are designated by the Power BI administrator and indicates that the content meets the organization's quality standards.

options.text: Promoted
options.explanation: Promotion can be applied by content owners and users who have write permission, without a review by designated reviewers.

questions.stem:
Your Import model is larger than expected. You need to identify which tables and columns use the most memory.
Which tool should you use?

options.text: Column profile in Power Query Editor
options.explanation: Column profile shows statistics of the data in a query, not the memory usage of the loaded model.

options.text: Query Dependencies view
options.explanation: Query Dependencies shows relationships between queries and does not show memory.

options.text: Performance Analyzer
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer measures how long visuals take to render and not how much memory the model uses.

options.text: VertiPaq Analyzer in DAX Studio
options.explanation: VertiPaq Analyzer shows the memory that each table, column, and relationship uses in the model.

questions.reference: Model size analysis with VertiPaq Analyzer

questions.stem:
In an Age column, the value 999 is used when the age is unknown. You must calculate the average customer age in reports, and the unknown ages must not influence the result.
What should you do in Power Query?

options.text: Replace 999 with null.
options.explanation: Aggregations such as AVERAGE ignore null values, so replacing the placeholder with null excludes unknown ages from the calculation.

options.text: Leave the values unchanged and create a DAX measure that uses AVERAGE.
options.explanation: AVERAGE would include the value 999 and overstate the average.

options.text: Change the data type to Text.
options.explanation: Text values cannot be averaged.

options.text: Replace 999 with 0.
options.explanation: Zero would be included in the average and would lower the result.

questions.reference: Replace values and handle placeholder values

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A sales manager is a Contributor in the workspace and is a member of the RLS role West. The manager still sees the sales of all regions in the reports.
What should you do to enforce the RLS role for the manager?

options.text: Switch the semantic model to DirectQuery so that the role is applied.
options.explanation: The storage mode does not change that users with edit rights are not restricted by RLS.

options.text: Change the workspace role of the manager to Viewer.
options.explanation: RLS applies to users with the Viewer role. Users who have edit permission in the workspace, such as Admin, Member, and Contributor, are not restricted by RLS.

options.text: Change the manager's workspace role to Admin so that the role applies.
options.explanation: Admins are not restricted by RLS either.

options.text: Add the manager to the role a second time so that the role is applied again.
options.explanation: Adding the member again does not change the effect of the workspace role.

questions.stem:
A table has three whole number columns: Year, Month, and Day. You need to add a custom column of type Date.
Which M expression should you use?

options.text: #date([Year], [Month], [Day])
options.explanation: #date takes a year, a month, and a day and returns a date value.

options.text: Date.AddDays([Year], [Day])
options.explanation: Date.AddDays expects a date as its first argument, not a year number.

options.text: Date.From([Year], [Month], [Day])
options.explanation: Date.From converts a single value to a date and does not accept three arguments.

options.text: Date.FromText(Text.From([Year]) & Text.From([Month]) & Text.From([Day]))
options.explanation: Joining the text parts without separators produces ambiguous strings such as 202515, which cannot be reliably parsed as a date.

questions.reference: Date functions in Power Query M

questions.stem:
A column chart shows product sales that range from 10 to 10,000,000. The columns of the small products are almost invisible. You must keep all products on the same chart.
What should you configure on the value axis?

options.text: A secondary axis
options.explanation: A secondary axis is for a second series, and it does not solve a wide range within one series.

options.text: A reverse scale
options.explanation: A reverse scale flips the axis direction and does not change the visibility of small values.

options.text: A logarithmic scale
options.explanation: A logarithmic scale compresses large values and makes small values visible on the same axis.

options.text: A minimum value of 5,000,000
options.explanation: A minimum of 5,000,000 would remove the columns of the small products from the view.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A KPI table uses red and green font colors to show whether each region is below or above target. Some users are red-green color blind and cannot tell the values apart.
What should you do?

options.text: Use a color-blind-safe palette, and add icons or text to the formatting
options.explanation: Information should not depend on color only. Icons or text carry the meaning, and a color-blind-safe palette keeps the colors distinguishable.

options.text: Remove the target from the table so that no comparison is shown
options.explanation: Removing the target removes the information that users need.

options.text: Replace the colors with a larger font size for the values in the table
options.explanation: Font size does not indicate whether a region is above or below the target.

options.text: Make the red and green fonts darker so that they have more contrast
options.explanation: Darker versions of red and green can still look the same to a person with red-green color blindness.

questions.stem:
A table has the columns Employee, Skill, and Level. You pivot the Skill column by using the values in Level and select Don't Aggregate. The operation fails with the error: There were too many elements in the enumeration to complete the operation.
What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The Level column has a Text data type
options.explanation: Text values can be pivoted. A text data type is not the cause.

options.text: Privacy levels are not configured for the data source of the query
options.explanation: Privacy levels apply to combining data sources and not to a pivot operation.

options.text: Some employees have more than one row for the same skill
options.explanation: Without aggregation, each employee and skill combination must have a single value. Several rows for the same combination cause the error. Choose an aggregation or remove the duplicates.

options.text: The table contains null values in the Employee column of the pivoted data
options.explanation: Null values would appear as a group but would not cause this error.

questions.stem:
Five report authors each maintain their own copy of the same Power Query steps that clean the Customer table. Differences between the copies cause inconsistent numbers. You need to maintain the transformation logic in one place and let all authors reuse the cleaned table.
What should you create?

options.text: A Power BI template (.pbit) file
options.explanation: A template distributes the report structure and queries, but each author still has an independent copy of the logic.

options.text: A Power Query parameter
options.explanation: A parameter holds a value, not a set of transformation steps.

options.text: A dataflow
options.explanation: A dataflow centralizes Power Query logic in the service. Authors connect to the dataflow's output tables instead of repeating the transformations.

options.text: A calculated table in each report
options.explanation: Calculated tables are created in each report, so the logic is duplicated again.

questions.stem: Your solution contains these queries: RawSales (loads all columns from a SQL table), FactSales (a reference to RawSales with columns removed), DimProduct (a reference to RawSales with duplicates removed), and DimDate (generated in M). The model must contain only the fact table and the dimensions. Which query should you configure so that it is not loaded into the model?
