options.text: FactSales
options.explanation: FactSales is the fact table and must be loaded.

options.text: RawSales
options.explanation: RawSales is only a staging query. Disabling its load keeps it available to other queries but removes it from the model.

options.text: DimProduct
options.explanation: DimProduct is a dimension table and must be loaded.

options.text: DimDate
options.explanation: DimDate is a dimension table and must be loaded.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A report page contains a column chart and a table that show the same data. You need to give users two buttons that switch the page between the chart view and the table view, and only one of the two visuals can be visible at a time.
What should you do?

options.text: Apply a visual-level filter to each visual that hides the table when the chart is selected
options.explanation: Filters change the data that a visual shows and not the visibility of the visual.

options.text: Create two report pages, one for each view, and add a page navigator to switch between them
options.explanation: Two pages would navigate away from the page, and the requirement is to switch views on the same page.

options.text: Create two bookmarks that show one visual and hide the other, and assign them to buttons
options.explanation: Bookmarks can save the visibility of objects. Buttons with a bookmark action let users switch between the saved states of the same page.

options.text: Create two drillthrough pages, one for each view, and add a Back button to each page
options.explanation: Drillthrough pages carry a filter context to another page and are not meant to toggle between views on one page.

questions.stem:
A report uses DirectQuery against an Azure SQL database that applies row-level permissions based on the identity of the signed-in user. Each report viewer must see only the rows that the database allows for that person.
What should you configure in the semantic model settings in the Power BI service?

options.text: Single sign-on (SSO) for DirectQuery with the viewers' own OAuth2 credentials
options.explanation: Single sign-on passes each viewer's identity to the source, so the database's own permissions determine what each user sees.

options.text: A scheduled refresh that uses the database owner's credentials for all viewers
options.explanation: Scheduled refresh applies to Import models. A single stored credential would run every query as the same identity.

options.text: Row-level security roles in the model that map the viewers' emails to database users
options.explanation: Model RLS filters data inside Power BI. It would not apply the database's own row-level permissions, and it requires maintaining separate roles.

options.text: A personal-mode on-premises data gateway that is shared by all of the report viewers
options.explanation: A personal gateway is designed for personal use and does not pass individual viewer identities to the source.

questions.stem:
You are reviewing a new table in the Power Query Editor. You need to quickly see, for every column, the percentage of values that are valid, in error, or empty.
Which view should you enable?

options.text: Column profile
options.explanation: Column profile shows detailed statistics and the value distribution for one selected column, not a summary of valid, error, and empty values for all columns at once.

options.text: Column distribution
options.explanation: Column distribution shows a small histogram together with the counts of distinct and unique values. It does not show error and empty percentages.

options.text: Column quality
options.explanation: Column quality displays the percentage of valid, error, and empty values for each column right under the column header.

options.text: Query Dependencies
options.explanation: Query Dependencies shows how queries relate to one another. It does not profile column data.

questions.reference: Data profiling tools in Power Query

questions.stem:
A column chart shows monthly Total Sales. The sales target is 500,000 per month for every month, and you need a horizontal line at that level.
What should you add from the Analytics pane?

options.text: A forecast that extends the monthly sales
options.explanation: A forecast predicts future values.

options.text: An average line that shows the mean of the sales
options.explanation: An average line draws the average of the values in the chart, which changes with the data and is not 500,000.

options.text: A constant line with the value 500000
options.explanation: A constant line draws a horizontal line at the value that you specify, which is suitable for a fixed target.

options.text: A trend line that follows the monthly sales
options.explanation: A trend line shows the direction of the data points.

questions.reference: Reference lines in the Analytics pane

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem: You develop a set of three reports and a dashboard for 400 employees. The employees only need to consume the content. The content must be released as a curated, versioned set, and further edits that you make to the reports must not be visible to the employees until you decide to release them. Which distribution method should you use?

options.text: Publish a workspace app
options.explanation: A workspace app is a curated package of content for consumers. Changes made in the workspace are not visible to app users until you update the app.

options.text: Publish each report to the web
options.explanation: Publish to web makes a report public to anyone, which is inappropriate for internal business data.

options.text: Share each report by email with the employees
options.explanation: Sharing each report separately does not give a curated set and is difficult to manage for 400 users.

options.text: Add all the employees as Viewers of the workspace
options.explanation: Viewers of the workspace see the workspace content as it is edited, so unfinished changes would be visible to them.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
The Sales table contains one row per order line. You need a measure that returns the median order total, not the median order line amount.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: MEDIANX(Sales, Sales[Amount])
options.explanation: Iterating over Sales rows returns the median of line amounts, which is the same result as MEDIAN(Sales[Amount]).

options.text: AVERAGEX(VALUES(Sales[OrderID]), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount])))
options.explanation: AVERAGEX returns the average of the order totals and not the median.

options.text: MEDIANX(VALUES(Sales[OrderID]), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount])))
options.explanation: The iterator computes the total for each distinct order, and MEDIANX returns the median of those totals.

options.text: MEDIAN(Sales[Amount])
options.explanation: MEDIAN returns the median of the individual order line amounts.

questions.stem:
A table has a Payload column in which each cell contains JSON text such as {"Id":1,"City":"Oslo"}. You need separate columns for Id and City.
What should you do?

options.text: Use Pivot Column on the Payload column with Id as the values
options.explanation: Pivot Column needs attribute and value columns, and it does not read JSON.

options.text: Use Transpose on the Payload column and promote the headers
options.explanation: Transpose swaps rows and columns, and it does not interpret JSON text.

options.text: Change the data type of Payload to Whole number
options.explanation: JSON text cannot be converted to a number.

options.text: Use Transform > Parse > JSON, and expand the record column
options.explanation: Parse JSON converts the text into a record. Expanding that record column creates the Id and City columns.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem: You need a measure that returns the sales of Red products, but it must also respect any selection that users make in a slicer on Products[Color]. When Blue is selected, the measure must return a blank value. Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS(Products[Color]))
options.explanation: REMOVEFILTERS removes the color filter and returns sales for all colors.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL(Products[Color]), Products[Color] = "Red")
options.explanation: ALL removes the slicer filter, and then Red is applied, so the slicer selection is ignored.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], KEEPFILTERS(Products[Color] = "Red"))
options.explanation: KEEPFILTERS adds the Red filter to the existing filters instead of replacing them. With Blue selected, the intersection is empty and the measure returns blank.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], Products[Color] = "Red")
options.explanation: Without KEEPFILTERS, the Red filter replaces the slicer selection, so it returns the sales of Red products.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
The scheduled refresh of a semantic model that imports data from an Azure SQL Database fails with an error that says that the credentials are not valid, because the password of the database account was changed.
What should you do?

options.text: Increase the refresh frequency so that the refresh is retried more often
options.explanation: Refreshing more often repeats the same failure.

options.text: Edit the data source credentials in the semantic model settings of the service
options.explanation: Credentials of the data source are stored in the settings of the semantic model. Updating them lets the next refresh authenticate.

options.text: Install a new gateway and add the Azure SQL Database to it
options.explanation: Azure SQL Database is a cloud source and does not need a gateway for refresh. The failure is caused by the credentials.

options.text: Delete the semantic model and publish it again to the workspace with a different name
options.explanation: Deleting the semantic model is not necessary and would break the reports that depend on it.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem: The Sales table contains one row per order line with the columns OrderID and Amount. You need a measure that returns the average total value of an order, not the average value of an order line. Which expression should you use?

options.text: AVERAGEX(Sales, Sales[Amount])
options.explanation: This also returns the average of order lines because it iterates over Sales rows.

options.text: AVERAGE(Sales[Amount])
options.explanation: This returns the average amount of an order line.

options.text: AVERAGEX(VALUES(Sales[OrderID]), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount])))
options.explanation: The iterator runs over each distinct order. CALCULATE turns each OrderID into a filter, so SUM returns the order total, and AVERAGEX averages these totals.

options.text: DIVIDE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), COUNTROWS(Sales))
options.explanation: Dividing the total by the number of lines is the same as the average line amount.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
The Sales table has the columns Quantity and UnitPrice. You need a measure that returns the total revenue, which is the sum of Quantity multiplied by UnitPrice for every row.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: SUMX(Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: SUMX evaluates the expression for each row and then adds the results, which gives the correct revenue.

options.text: SUM(Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: SUM accepts only a column reference, and it cannot evaluate a row-level expression, so this formula is not valid.

options.text: SUM(Sales[Quantity]) * SUM(Sales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: This multiplies the total quantity by the total of the unit prices, which does not equal the sum of row-level revenue.

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Quantity]), Sales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: The second argument of CALCULATE must be a filter, so a plain column reference is not valid.

questions.stem:
You want Copilot to generate a text summary of the data on a report page, and the summary must be placed on the page as a visual that you can refresh.
Which visual should you add?

options.text: Narrative visual with Copilot
options.explanation: The narrative visual with Copilot generates a text summary of the report content and displays it as a visual on the page.

options.text: Decomposition tree with the sales fields
options.explanation: A decomposition tree lets users break a measure into categories interactively.

options.text: Key influencers visual on the Total Sales measure
options.explanation: Key influencers analyzes which factors affect a metric and does not write a summary of the page.

options.text: A Q&A visual with the question summarize this page
options.explanation: A Q&A visual answers a typed question with a visual and does not summarize the page.

questions.stem: Your model has 18 date columns in different tables. Power BI Desktop has created a hidden date table and hierarchy for each date column, which increases the model size. You already have a dedicated Date table. What should you do?

options.text: Set the cross-filter direction of the date relationships to Both.
options.explanation: Cross-filter direction has no effect on the automatic date tables.

options.text: Mark every date column as a key column.
options.explanation: Marking a column as a key does not affect the automatic date tables.

options.text: Disable the Auto date/time option in the Data Load options.
options.explanation: Auto date/time creates a hidden table for each date column. Turning it off removes them, and your Date table supports time intelligence.

options.text: Delete the Date table.
options.explanation: Deleting the dedicated Date table would remove the tool that provides the date analysis.

questions.reference: Auto date/time in Power BI Desktop

questions.stem:
When you convert the Amount column to Decimal Number, a small number of rows show errors. You need to inspect only the rows that contain errors in this column to find the cause.
What should you do?

options.text: Use Keep Errors on the Amount column.
options.explanation: Keep Errors filters the table to the rows that have an error in the selected column, which makes the problem values easy to inspect.

options.text: Use Remove Errors on the Amount column.
options.explanation: Remove Errors does the opposite and hides the rows you want to analyze.

options.text: Use Replace Errors on the Amount column.
options.explanation: Replace Errors overwrites the error cells, so the problem values are no longer visible.

options.text: Filter the Amount column to remove null values.
options.explanation: Null values and errors are different. Filtering nulls does not isolate the errors.

questions.reference: Keep or remove rows with errors

questions.stem: A bar chart shows the average order value per customer. A few customers have extremely large orders, and the average line on the chart is pulled up so that most customers appear to be below it. You need a reference line that represents a typical customer and is not influenced by the extreme values. What should you add from the Analytics pane?

options.text: An additional average line
options.explanation: A second average line has the same sensitivity to extreme values.

options.text: A min line
options.explanation: The min line marks the lowest value, and it does not describe a typical customer.

options.text: A max line
options.explanation: The max line marks the highest value, which is the extreme value itself.

options.text: A median line
options.explanation: The median is the middle value of the distribution. Extreme values do not move it much.

questions.reference: Reference lines in the Analytics pane

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem: A page contains a bar chart of sales by category, a table of sales by product, and a map of sales by store. When a user selects a bar, the table must be filtered to that category, but the map must not change. What should you do?

options.text: Remove the Category field from the map, so that the map ignores the selection
options.explanation: Removing a field changes what the map displays and does not control how the visual reacts to selections.

options.text: Select the bar chart, use Edit interactions, and set the table to Filter and the map to None
options.explanation: Edit interactions lets you choose, for each target visual, whether a selection in the source visual filters, highlights, or has no effect.

options.text: Add a page-level filter on Category that applies to the table and the map
options.explanation: A page-level filter would apply to all the visuals and would not react to the bar selection.

options.text: Select the map, use Edit interactions, and set the interaction for the bar chart to None.
options.explanation: This changes how the map affects the bar chart. The requirement concerns how the bar chart affects the map.

questions.stem: You need to add a custom column that returns the first three characters of the ProductCode column. Which formula should you use?

options.text: Text.End([ProductCode], 3)
options.explanation: Text.End returns the last three characters.

options.text: Text.Middle([ProductCode], 1, 3)
options.explanation: Text.Middle starts at a zero-based offset, so starting at 1 skips the first character and returns characters two through four.

options.text: Text.Start([ProductCode], 1)
options.explanation: Text.Start with a count of 1 returns only the first character.

options.text: Text.Start([ProductCode], 3)
options.explanation: Text.Start returns the specified number of characters from the beginning of the text.

questions.reference: Text functions in Power Query M

questions.stem:
A table is in long format with the columns Product, Month, and Sales. You need a table that has one row per product and one column for each month that contains the sales amount. Some products have several rows for the same month.
What should you do?

options.text: Unpivot the Month column
options.explanation: Unpivot does the opposite. It turns columns into attribute and value rows.

options.text: Pivot the Month column by using the Sum of Sales as the aggregate
options.explanation: Pivoting Month with Sum as the aggregate creates a column per month and adds up multiple rows for the same product and month.

options.text: Transpose the table
options.explanation: Transposing swaps rows and columns but does not group values by product and month.

options.text: Pivot the Month column by using the Don't Aggregate option, with Sales as the values
options.explanation: Don't Aggregate fails when a product has several rows for the same month because a cell cannot hold more than one value.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A dashboard has tiles that come from reports that use a DirectQuery semantic model. The tiles are cached, and the business needs the tiles to be updated every 15 minutes.
What should you configure?

options.text: The incremental refresh policy of the semantic model and its parameters
options.explanation: Incremental refresh applies to imported tables, not to DirectQuery.

options.text: The data category of the date column
options.explanation: The data category affects how the field is treated in visuals and not how often tiles are updated.

options.text: The page size of the reports
options.explanation: The page size has no influence on the update of tiles.

options.text: The scheduled cache refresh frequency of the semantic model
options.explanation: For DirectQuery and live connections, the service caches the tile data. The cache refresh frequency in the semantic model settings decides how often the tiles are updated.

questions.stem:
You need to model locations so that report authors can use origin and destination independently in the same visual without writing DAX.
What should you do?

options.text: Create two location tables named Origin and Destination, for example by referencing the Locations query, and relate each table to Shipments.
options.explanation: Two role-playing dimension tables allow origin and destination to be placed on different axes of the same visual because each table has its own active relationship.

options.text: Create a many-to-many relationship between Locations and Shipments on both keys.
options.explanation: A relationship connects one column to one column. A relationship on both keys is not possible, and many-to-many would not fix the single-active-relationship limit.

options.text: Merge the Locations columns into Shipments twice, and remove the Locations table.
options.explanation: Merging attributes into the fact table makes it wide, repeats text values on every row, and breaks the star schema.

options.text: Create one active relationship on OriginKey and one inactive relationship on DestinationKey, and then create measures that use USERELATIONSHIP.
options.explanation: Only one relationship can be active, so authors would need measures to see destination data. Inactive relationships cannot supply a separate axis to the same visual.

questions.stem:
You need to meet the requirement for ShipDate and DeliveryDate.
What should you do?

options.text: Keep the ShipDate relationship active, make the DeliveryDate relationship inactive, and use USERELATIONSHIP in the delivery measures
options.explanation: ShipDate stays the default through the active relationship. Measures that call USERELATIONSHIP activate the inactive DeliveryDate relationship only for their calculation.

options.text: Keep both relationships active, and set the cross-filter direction of the DeliveryDate relationship to Both
options.explanation: Cross-filter direction does not activate a relationship.

options.text: Create both relationships as active, and let the report users choose the date column in a slicer
options.explanation: Only one relationship between two tables can be active at a time.

options.text: Create a relationship from Date to ShipDate only, and calculate delivery analysis by using DAX filters on the Date table without a relationship.
options.explanation: Without a second relationship, the Date table cannot filter DeliveryDate. A DAX workaround is possible, but it is more complex than the relationship approach that meets the requirement.

questions.stem: You need to let users choose Total Cost, Total Weight, or Shipment Count in a single visual. What should you create?

options.text: A numeric range what-if parameter
options.explanation: A what-if parameter provides a numeric input value. It does not switch between measures.

options.text: A field parameter that contains the three measures
options.explanation: A field parameter lets users select which field or measure is shown in a visual, typically through a slicer, so one visual can switch between the three measures.

options.text: Three visuals that are switched by bookmarks
options.explanation: Bookmarks would switch between three separate visuals, and the requirement is to use one visual.

options.text: A calculation group that contains three calculation items
options.explanation: A calculation group modifies how existing measures are calculated, for example to apply time intelligence. It is not designed to choose which measure is displayed.

questions.stem:
You need to let users enter a fuel surcharge percentage and see Total Cost change.
What should you create?

options.text: A calculated column in Shipments
options.explanation: A calculated column is computed at refresh time and cannot respond to a value that a user selects in a report.

options.text: A numeric range what-if parameter
options.explanation: A what-if parameter creates a table of values and a measure that returns the selected value. You use that measure inside a Total Cost measure to simulate the surcharge.

options.text: A calculation group
options.explanation: A calculation group changes the evaluation of measures, and it does not collect an input from users.

options.text: A field parameter
options.explanation: A field parameter switches fields in visuals and does not provide a numeric input for calculations.

questions.stem:
You need to make sure that the Country values plot correctly on map visuals.
What should you do?

options.text: Set the data category of the Country column to Country/Region.
options.explanation: Setting the data category gives Power BI a hint about how to interpret the values, which improves geocoding on map visuals.

options.text: Set the data category of the Country column to Text.
options.explanation: Text is a data type, and it gives no geographic hint to the map.

options.text: Set the sort by column of the Country column to City.
options.explanation: Sorting changes the display order of values. It does not help the map interpret them.

options.text: Set the Summarize by property of the Country column to Count.
options.explanation: Summarize by changes how numeric values are aggregated and has no effect on geocoding.

questions.stem:
You need a visual calculation that shows the average of the Total Sales of the current row and the two rows before it.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: MOVINGAVERAGE([Total Sales], 3)
options.explanation: MOVINGAVERAGE averages the values over a window of rows. A window of 3 covers the current row and the two rows before it.

options.text: RUNNINGSUM([Total Sales]) / 3
options.explanation: Dividing the running total by 3 does not produce a three-row average.

options.text: PREVIOUS([Total Sales], 3)
options.explanation: PREVIOUS returns the value of a single row that is a number of steps back, not an average of rows.

options.text: AVERAGE([Total Sales])
options.explanation: AVERAGE over the visual's field would return a single average and not a moving window.

questions.stem:
You add a conditional column named Size with these rules, in this order:
1. If Sales is greater than or equal to 500, then Medium.
2. If Sales is greater than or equal to 1000, then Large.
3. Otherwise, Small.
After applying the step, no row contains the value Large.
What is the cause?

options.text: Rules run from top to bottom, so a value of at least 1000 already matches the first rule
options.explanation: The first rule that evaluates to true is used. Values of 1000 or more also meet the first rule, so the Large rule is never reached. Put the more restrictive rule first.

options.text: The Otherwise value is applied first and replaces the results of the other rules
options.explanation: The Otherwise value can be any value, including text such as Small.

options.text: Conditional columns cannot use the greater than or equal to operator in a rule
options.explanation: Conditional columns support comparison operators including greater than or equal to.

options.text: The Sales column has a Text data type, so the comparison with 1000 fails for every row
options.explanation: If Sales were text, the step would raise a comparison error or use text comparison. It would not simply skip one rule.

questions.stem:
Managers want to explore Total Sales by Region, Category, and Product, and they want to choose the order of the dimensions themselves as they explore.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Decomposition tree
options.explanation: In a decomposition tree, users add a level at a time and select the dimension for each level, so they control the order of the breakdown.

options.text: Treemap
options.explanation: A treemap shows a fixed hierarchy of rectangles, and users cannot add levels in an order of their choice.

options.text: Ribbon chart
options.explanation: A ribbon chart shows rank changes of categories across a time axis.

options.text: Key influencers
options.explanation: Key influencers analyzes the drivers of an outcome and is not a free breakdown of a measure.

questions.stem:
A fuzzy merge of a Customers query with a master list returns many incorrect matches, such as different companies with similar names. You need the merge to return only very close matches.
What should you change in the fuzzy matching options?

options.text: Select Ignore case
options.explanation: Ignore case treats uppercase and lowercase letters as equal, so it makes matching looser, not stricter.

options.text: Increase the similarity threshold
options.explanation: A higher similarity threshold (closer to 1) requires names to be more alike before they match.

options.text: Increase the maximum number of matches
options.explanation: The maximum number of matches limits how many matches each row can return, and it does not make matching stricter.

options.text: Decrease the similarity threshold
options.explanation: A lower threshold accepts less similar names, which causes more incorrect matches.

questions.stem: A Readings table stores a ReadingTime column that is a datetime value with second precision. Reports must show readings by date and by hour of the day. You need to reduce the cardinality of the table. What should you do?

options.text: Split the column into a Date column and an hourly Time column, and remove the original
options.explanation: A date column and an hour column have few distinct values, so they compress well. Removing the original datetime column eliminates the high-cardinality column.

options.text: Create a calculated table of the distinct datetime values and relate it to the readings
options.explanation: A calculated table adds more data and does not change the original column.

options.text: Change the data type of ReadingTime to Text to reduce the number of distinct values
options.explanation: Text does not reduce the number of distinct values and stores them less efficiently.

options.text: Keep the datetime column, and add a calculated column that returns the hour of each value
options.explanation: Keeping the original datetime column keeps the high cardinality and adds another column.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
The Order Detail page of a report is a drillthrough target. You need to keep the page from appearing as a tab for report consumers, who must still reach it by right-clicking an order.
What should you do?

options.text: Hide the page.
options.explanation: A hidden page does not show as a tab for consumers, but it remains available as a drillthrough target.

options.text: Turn off the drillthrough filters on the page.
options.explanation: Without drillthrough fields, the page would no longer be a drillthrough target.

options.text: Lock the page filters.
options.explanation: Locking filters prevents users from changing a filter, and it does not hide the page.

options.text: Delete the page and re-create it as a bookmark.
options.explanation: A bookmark is not a page, and it does not support drillthrough from a visual.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A column chart has the hierarchy Year, Quarter, and Month on its axis. Users want to select the 2025 column and see only the quarters of 2025 in the same visual.
What should they do?

options.text: Use Expand all down one level in the hierarchy of the visual.
options.explanation: Expanding all down one level shows the current level and the next level together for all items.

options.text: Use Go to the next level in the hierarchy.
options.explanation: Going to the next level changes the whole visual to the next level for all years, and it does not limit it to 2025.

options.text: Use drillthrough from the 2025 column.
options.explanation: Drillthrough navigates to another page and does not change the level of the visual.

options.text: Turn on drill mode, and then select the 2025 column.
options.explanation: In drill mode, selecting a column moves to the next level for that column only, so the visual shows the quarters of 2025.

questions.stem:
The query OnlineSales has the columns OrderID, Amount, and ShippingCost. The query StoreSales has only OrderID and Amount. You append StoreSales to OnlineSales.
What is the result?

options.text: A table in which ShippingCost is 0 for the rows that came from StoreSales
options.explanation: The missing values are null, not zero.

options.text: A table that contains only the columns that exist in both of the queries
options.explanation: Append does not drop columns that exist in only one table.

options.text: One table with all three columns, with null in ShippingCost for the StoreSales rows
options.explanation: Append returns all columns from both queries. Cells for columns that a source lacks are filled with null.

options.text: An error because the two queries do not have the same set of columns, so the append fails
options.explanation: Append does not require identical column sets, so no error occurs.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A workspace owner wants to know which reports in the workspace are used the least and how many people viewed each report during the last 30 days.
What should the owner use?

options.text: The lineage view of the workspace and its items
options.explanation: The lineage view shows dependencies between items and not how many people use them.

options.text: The Selection pane of each report
options.explanation: The Selection pane controls visibility and order of the objects on a page.

options.text: The Performance Analyzer pane in Power BI Desktop
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer shows the load time of visuals, not who views the report.

options.text: The usage metrics report of the workspace
options.explanation: Usage metrics reports show the number of views and viewers of reports and dashboards over time.

questions.stem:
Users of a decomposition tree want Power BI to choose the next dimension automatically, so that the split is made on the dimension where Total Sales is the highest.
What should the users select when they add a level?

options.text: High value
options.explanation: The High value AI split finds the dimension that has the item with the highest value of the analyzed measure, and splits the tree on it.

options.text: Low value
options.explanation: Low value finds the dimension that has the lowest value, which is the opposite of the requirement.

options.text: Expand all
options.explanation: Expand all is a drill mode of other visuals, and it is not an AI split option in a decomposition tree.

options.text: Show as percent of total
options.explanation: Showing a percent of total changes how the values are displayed and does not choose a dimension.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
Users who use the Q&A visual type the question show revenue by region, but the visual returns an error because the model has no field called revenue. The measure that they mean is Total Sales.
What should you do?

options.text: Add revenue as a synonym of the Total Sales measure in the model.
options.explanation: Synonyms let Q&A map alternative words to model fields, so revenue is understood as Total Sales.

options.text: Create a calculated table named revenue that stores the Total Sales values
options.explanation: A new table would not help Q&A to understand the word as the measure.

options.text: Hide the Total Sales measure so that Q&A uses a different field
options.explanation: Hiding the measure would remove it from the report view and from Q&A.

options.text: Rename the Region column to revenue in the Region table
options.explanation: Renaming Region to revenue would break the field and would not map revenue to Total Sales.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model uses a Power Query parameter named ServerName for the database server. The report was published to the service with the value of the development server. You need to change the parameter to the production server without republishing the file.
What should you do?

options.text: Edit the parameter in the report view of the report in the service
options.explanation: Parameters are part of the semantic model queries, and they are not edited in the report view.

options.text: Create a new workspace app that contains the report with the production server
options.explanation: An app is a distribution method and does not change parameter values.

options.text: Edit the parameters in the semantic model settings in the Power BI service
options.explanation: Parameters that are used in queries can be changed in the settings of the semantic model in the service, and the next refresh uses the new value.

options.text: Change the RLS role so that it points to the production server of the data
options.explanation: RLS filters rows for users and does not change the source server.

questions.reference: Parameters in the Power BI service

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Finance analysts want to build PivotTables in Excel that connect directly to the published Sales semantic model, so that they use the same measures as the Power BI reports.
What is required for the analysts?

options.text: Use Publish to web and open the link in Excel for the analysts
options.explanation: Publish to web creates a public link to a report and is not a connection for Excel.

options.text: Use Analyze in Excel, with the Build permission on the semantic model
options.explanation: Analyze in Excel connects Excel to the semantic model, so PivotTables use its measures and relationships. It requires the Build permission on the semantic model.

options.text: Install a gateway on each analyst's computer to connect to the model
options.explanation: A gateway is for refresh and DirectQuery of on-premises sources, and it is not needed for analysts to connect to the model.

options.text: Export the report to CSV, and import the file into Excel.
options.explanation: A CSV file is a static copy of the data and does not contain the measures.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem: A table visual that shows sales by product includes a row with a blank product name that has a significant sales amount. The Sales table contains ProductKey 9999, but the Products table has no row for that key. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Assume referential integrity on the relationship between the tables
options.explanation: Assume referential integrity tells Power BI that the data has no orphans. The data does contain a missing key, so the setting would be incorrect.

options.text: Change the relationship between Sales and Products to bidirectional
options.explanation: Cross-filter direction does not create missing dimension rows.

options.text: Add a row for an Unknown product with key 9999 to the Products table.
options.explanation: Adding a dimension row for the unknown key gives the sales a meaningful product label, so they are no longer reported under blank.

options.text: Filter out the blank product in the visual by using a visual-level filter
options.explanation: Filtering hides the sales amount, so totals no longer match the source.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A workspace already contains a report named Sales Overview and its semantic model, which was published last week. You publish a new version of Sales Overview.pbix from Power BI Desktop to the same workspace.
What is the result?

options.text: The existing report and semantic model are replaced by the new versions.
options.explanation: When you publish a file that has the same name as an existing report and semantic model in the workspace, the existing items are overwritten. Changes that were made in the service to the report are lost.

options.text: A second report named Sales Overview is created next to the first one
options.explanation: A new report with the same name is not created. The existing items are replaced.

options.text: Only the report is replaced, and the existing semantic model is kept
options.explanation: The semantic model is replaced together with the report when it is part of the file you publish.

options.text: The publish operation fails because the names already exist in the workspace
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop asks you to confirm the replacement, and the operation does not fail.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
Sales is on the many side of a one-to-many relationship from Products. You need a calculated column in Sales that returns the Category of each product.
Which formula should you use?

options.text: VALUES(Products[Category])
options.explanation: VALUES depends on filter context, and a row context in a calculated column does not filter Products. It would return all categories, which is not a scalar value.

options.text: RELATEDTABLE(Products)
options.explanation: RELATEDTABLE returns a table and is used from the one side to reach the many-side rows.

options.text: SELECTEDVALUE(Products[Category])
options.explanation: SELECTEDVALUE also depends on filter context, so without a filter it returns a blank value.

options.text: RELATED(Products[Category])
options.explanation: RELATED follows the relationship from the many side to the one side and returns the value for the current row.

questions.stem: Users will print a report on Letter-size paper. You need the report pages to match the paper proportions. What should you configure?

options.text: The Selection pane order of the objects on the page
options.explanation: The Selection pane controls the visibility and order of objects.

options.text: The report theme that is applied to all the pages
options.explanation: A theme controls colors and fonts, not the dimensions of the page.

options.text: The page size in the canvas settings, set to Letter
options.explanation: The canvas settings let you select a page size such as 16:9, 4:3, Letter, or a custom size.

options.text: The page alignment of the visuals on the canvas
options.explanation: Alignment places visuals within the page and does not change the page size.

questions.stem:
A UnitPrice column contains prices with two decimal places. You must avoid floating-point rounding issues in totals and keep the model small.
Which data type should you use?

options.text: Text
options.explanation: Text cannot be aggregated and stores values inefficiently.

options.text: Fixed decimal number
options.explanation: Fixed decimal number (currency) stores values with fixed precision, so it avoids floating-point rounding problems and uses efficient storage.

options.text: Whole number
options.explanation: Whole number would remove the decimal part of each price.

options.text: Decimal number
options.explanation: Decimal number is a floating-point type that can produce small rounding differences in sums.

questions.reference: Data types in Power BI Desktop

questions.stem:
You need to display a small horizontal bar inside each cell of a Sales column in a table, so that readers can compare the relative size of the values.
Which formatting should you apply?

options.text: Gradient background color
options.explanation: A gradient changes the cell color and does not draw bars.

options.text: Data bars
options.explanation: Data bars draw a bar in each cell whose length is proportional to the value.

options.text: Icons
options.explanation: Icons show symbols based on rules and do not show relative magnitude through bar length.

options.text: Web URL
options.explanation: Web URL turns the value into a link and does not draw anything.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A bar chart shows Total Sales by category. When users hover over a bar, the default tooltip shows the category and the Total Sales. You need the tooltip to show the Profit Margin measure as well, without changing the bar chart or its axis.
What should you do?

options.text: Turn on cross-highlighting for the visual.
options.explanation: Cross-highlighting changes how other visuals react to a selection, and it does not add fields to a tooltip.

options.text: Add the Profit Margin measure to the Tooltips field well of the visual.
options.explanation: Fields in the Tooltips well appear in the default tooltip and do not change the visual.

options.text: Add the Profit Margin measure to the Values field well of the visual.
options.explanation: A second measure in Values would draw a second bar series and change the chart.

options.text: Add the Profit Margin measure to the Legend field well of the visual.
options.explanation: Legend takes a categorical field that splits the series, and a measure cannot be used there.

questions.stem: A line chart shows Total Sales by day. You need a measure that returns the cumulative total of sales from the first selected date up to the date of each point, and that does not reset at the start of each year. Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], FILTER('Date', 'Date'[Date] <= MAX('Date'[Date])))
options.explanation: FILTER over Date is evaluated in the current filter context, in which only the current day is visible. The result is the same as the daily sales.

options.text: TOTALYTD([Total Sales], 'Date'[Date])
options.explanation: TOTALYTD restarts the accumulation at the start of each year.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], FILTER(ALLSELECTED('Date'[Date]), 'Date'[Date] <= MAX('Date'[Date])))
options.explanation: ALLSELECTED returns all dates that are selected outside the chart, and FILTER keeps the dates up to the current date, so the total accumulates across the whole selected range.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESMTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: DATESMTD restarts the accumulation at the start of each month.

questions.stem:
Your organization uses Microsoft Fabric. Sales data is stored as Delta tables in a lakehouse. You are building a semantic model and need query performance similar to Import mode, without copying the data into the model through scheduled import refreshes.
Which storage mode should you choose?

options.text: Direct Lake
options.explanation: Direct Lake loads Delta table data from OneLake directly into memory on demand, which gives Import-like performance without a separate import copy and scheduled import refresh.

options.text: DirectQuery
options.explanation: DirectQuery translates every visual query into a query against the source. It avoids copying data but is generally slower than in-memory access.

options.text: Import
options.explanation: Import creates its own copy of the data inside the model and relies on scheduled refreshes.

options.text: Live connection
options.explanation: A live connection attaches a report to an existing semantic model. It is not a storage mode for a new model's tables.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
Users report that the data in a report has not changed for two weeks. In the semantic model settings, you see that scheduled refresh is turned off, and a message states that it was disabled because of repeated failures. You have fixed the cause of the failures, which was an expired password.
What should you do next?

options.text: Delete the semantic model and publish it again.
options.explanation: Deleting the model is unnecessary and would break the reports that use it.

options.text: Turn the scheduled refresh back on.
options.explanation: The service disables the schedule after consecutive failures. Once the cause is fixed, you must turn the schedule on again, and it is a good idea to run a manual refresh to verify.

options.text: Change the storage mode to DirectQuery.
options.explanation: Changing the storage mode changes the architecture and was not required to fix an expired password.

options.text: Assign the users the Contributor role.
options.explanation: The roles of the users have no effect on whether the refresh runs.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A report developer must be able to publish reports to a workspace, and edit and delete existing reports and semantic models in it. The developer must not be able to publish or update the workspace app, and must not be able to add users to the workspace.
Which workspace role should you assign to the developer?

options.text: Member
options.explanation: A Member can additionally publish and update the app and add users with lower roles, which the requirement does not allow.

options.text: Admin
options.explanation: An Admin has full control of the workspace, including access management and deleting the workspace.

options.text: Viewer
options.explanation: A Viewer can only view and interact with content, so the developer could not publish or edit.

options.text: Contributor
options.explanation: A Contributor can publish, edit, and delete content in the workspace, but cannot publish or update the app and cannot manage workspace access.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Your company uses Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels. A semantic model that contains salary data has the label Highly Confidential. Employees export visuals from reports that are based on this semantic model to Excel.
What happens to the exported Excel files?

options.text: The sensitivity label and its protection settings are applied to the exported files.
options.explanation: When data is exported from labeled content to supported formats such as Excel, the sensitivity label and its protection settings travel with the file.

options.text: The exported files are always unlabeled, because the label applies only to Power BI items.
options.explanation: Labels are applied to exported files, so they are not left unlabeled.

options.text: The export is blocked for all labels.
options.explanation: Export is not blocked by a label alone. The label protects the exported file. Blocking export is configured separately.

options.text: The exported files are encrypted with a key that only the report owner has.
options.explanation: The protection comes from the label's policy, and access is not tied to one key owned by the report owner.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem: In a chart, the MonthName column sorts alphabetically as April, August, December, and so on. The Date table also has a MonthNumber column. You need the months to appear in calendar order in every visual. What should you do?

options.text: Select MonthName, and set Sort by column to MonthNumber.
options.explanation: Sort by column makes MonthName follow the order of MonthNumber wherever it is used in the model.

options.text: Change the data type of MonthName to Date.
options.explanation: Month names are text values and cannot be converted to a Date by changing the data type.

options.text: Create a hierarchy that contains MonthName.
options.explanation: A hierarchy defines drill levels and does not change the sort order of a column.

options.text: Sort the visual in ascending order by MonthName in the More options menu of the visual
options.explanation: Sorting by MonthName in a visual still sorts alphabetically.

questions.stem:
A relationship between Products and Sales filters in one direction only. You need one specific measure to filter Products from the Sales side, but you do not want to change the relationship setting for the whole model.
Which function should you use in the measure?

options.text: TREATAS
options.explanation: TREATAS applies filters from one set of values to the columns of another table, and it does not change the relationship direction.

options.text: USERELATIONSHIP
options.explanation: USERELATIONSHIP activates an inactive relationship, and it does not change the filter direction.

options.text: CROSSFILTER
options.explanation: CROSSFILTER changes the cross-filter direction of a relationship for the duration of a CALCULATE expression, for example to Both.

options.text: ALLEXCEPT
options.explanation: ALLEXCEPT removes filters and does not change the filter direction.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
You share a report with a group of colleagues. They should be able to view the report, but they must not be able to share it with other people, and they must not be able to build their own reports from its semantic model.
What should you do in the Share dialog?

options.text: Select only the option that allows recipients to share this report
options.explanation: Allowing sharing would let the recipients give the report to others.

options.text: Select both options, for sharing and for building content with the data
options.explanation: Selecting both options would allow resharing and building, which the requirement forbids.

options.text: Select only the option that allows recipients to build content with the data associated with the report
options.explanation: Allowing building gives the recipients Build permission on the semantic model, which the requirement forbids.

options.text: Clear both Allow recipients to share this report and Allow recipients to build content
options.explanation: Clearing both options gives the recipients access to view the report only, without resharing and without Build permission on the semantic model.

questions.stem:
A sales table includes rows where OrderID is null, but the Notes column of those rows contains text. You need to remove these rows.
What should you do?

options.text: Apply Remove Duplicates to the table.
options.explanation: Remove Duplicates removes repeated rows, not rows with a missing key.

options.text: Apply Remove Bottom Rows to the table
options.explanation: Remove Bottom Rows removes a fixed number of rows from the end of the table and does not target rows by their content.

options.text: Apply Remove Blank Rows to the table
options.explanation: Remove Blank Rows removes only rows where every column is empty. These rows contain Notes text, so they would remain.

options.text: Filter OrderID to exclude null values
options.explanation: Filtering OrderID to exclude null removes exactly the rows where the key is missing, even if other columns contain data.

questions.reference: Filter and remove rows in Power Query

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Dashboard users want to see the Sales page of a report on a dashboard tile that stays interactive and that updates automatically when you change the page in the report.
What should you pin to the dashboard?

options.text: A static image of the page
options.explanation: A static image does not update when the report changes and is not interactive.

options.text: A single visual from the page
options.explanation: A single visual does not include the other visuals of the page, and later changes to the page layout are not reflected.

options.text: The live report page
options.explanation: Pinning a live page adds a tile of the whole page that is interactive and stays in sync with the report.

options.text: The semantic model
options.explanation: A semantic model cannot be pinned as a tile.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A report has twelve pages. You need a row of buttons that lets users jump to any page, and the buttons must be created without configuring each button separately.
Which visual should you add?

options.text: Bookmark navigator
options.explanation: A bookmark navigator creates buttons for bookmarks and not for pages.

options.text: Page navigator
options.explanation: The page navigator creates a button for each page automatically and can show or hide pages.

options.text: Back button
options.explanation: A Back button returns to the previous page and cannot reach arbitrary pages.

options.text: Slicer
options.explanation: A slicer filters data and does not navigate between pages.

questions.stem:
You add a custom column by using this formula:

{{code}}

Power Query returns an error that a token is not valid.
What is the cause?

options.text: The column name Sales must be enclosed in parentheses, as in DAX
options.explanation: Column references use square brackets, which the formula already has.

options.text: The formula must start with an equal sign, as in Excel
options.explanation: The custom column dialog does not require a leading equal sign for the expression.

options.text: M is case-sensitive, so if, then, and else must be lowercase
options.explanation: The M language is case-sensitive. The expression must be written as if [Sales] > 100 then "High" else "Low".

options.text: Text values must be enclosed in single quotation marks in M
options.explanation: Text literals in M use double quotation marks.

questions.stem:
You need a visual that shows how the rank of each product category by sales changes from month to month. The visual must connect the categories across months and always show the highest-ranked category at the top of each month.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Ribbon chart
options.explanation: A ribbon chart ranks the categories in each period, with the highest value at the top, and connects the ribbons between periods to show rank changes.

options.text: 100% stacked column chart
options.explanation: A 100% stacked column chart shows the share of each category but does not connect categories across periods or sort them by rank.

options.text: Stacked area chart
options.explanation: A stacked area chart shows the cumulative size of categories and does not rank them in each period.

options.text: Waterfall chart
options.explanation: A waterfall chart shows how positive and negative changes build a total.

questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the seven-day moving average of Total Sales, which is the average of the daily Total Sales over the seven days that end at the current date.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: AVERAGEX(DATESINPERIOD('Date'[Date], MAX('Date'[Date]), -7, DAY), [Total Sales])
options.explanation: DATESINPERIOD returns the seven days that end at the current date, and AVERAGEX evaluates the measure for each day and averages the results.

options.text: AVERAGE([Total Sales])
options.explanation: AVERAGE requires a column, and it cannot take a measure.

options.text: CALCULATE(AVERAGE(Sales[Amount]), DATESMTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: This calculates the average line amount from the start of the month, not a moving average of daily totals.

options.text: AVERAGEX('Date', [Total Sales])
options.explanation: AVERAGEX over Date iterates the dates that are visible in the current context and not the previous seven days.

questions.stem: In the Power Query Editor, you want a bar chart above each column that shows the count of distinct values and the count of unique values, so that you can spot columns that are candidates for relationship keys. Which view should you enable?

options.text: Column quality
options.explanation: Column quality shows valid, error, and empty percentages, not distinct and unique counts.

options.text: Column distribution
options.explanation: Column distribution shows a frequency chart for each column and lists the number of distinct and unique values.

options.text: Column profile
options.explanation: Column profile focuses on one selected column. It is not displayed above every column.

options.text: Query Settings
options.explanation: Query Settings shows the applied steps and the query properties, not profiling information.

questions.reference: Data profiling tools in Power Query

questions.stem:
You create a Product dimension by referencing the Sales query, keeping the product columns, and removing duplicate rows. The result has no numeric key. You need to add an integer surrogate key that starts at 1.
Which command should you use?

options.text: Add Column > Conditional Column
options.explanation: A conditional column returns values based on rules, not a sequence of unique integers.

options.text: Transform > Count Rows
options.explanation: Count Rows returns a single number for the table.

options.text: Add Column > Duplicate Column
options.explanation: Duplicate Column copies an existing column, so it would repeat the existing values.

options.text: Add Column > Index Column
options.explanation: Index Column adds a sequence of integers. When you apply it after removing duplicates, it gives each product a unique key.

questions.stem: You need a visual that shows Total Sales by product category on the rows and by year on the columns. The visual must show subtotals for each category and let users expand and collapse the category rows. Which visual should you use?

options.text: Matrix
options.explanation: A matrix supports row and column groups, subtotals, and expanding and collapsing in a hierarchy.

options.text: Clustered bar chart
options.explanation: A clustered bar chart shows bars rather than a grid of values with subtotals.

options.text: Table
options.explanation: A table shows data in rows and columns, but it does not pivot a field onto the column headers.

options.text: Card
options.explanation: A card displays a single value.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model imports data from Azure SQL Database, which can be reached over the internet. The semantic model is published to the Power BI service, and a nightly refresh is required.
What is required for the scheduled refresh?

options.text: A personal gateway that is installed on the computer of the report author
options.explanation: A personal gateway is for scenarios with on-premises or private data and depends on the author's computer.

options.text: Cloud credentials for the data source in the model settings, without a gateway
options.explanation: The service can connect directly to a cloud source that is reachable over the internet, so only the credentials are needed.

options.text: A Premium capacity that is assigned to the workspace of the semantic model
options.explanation: Scheduled refresh is available without Premium capacity, subject to the usual limits.

options.text: An on-premises data gateway in standard mode that is mapped to the source
options.explanation: A standard gateway is needed for sources that the service cannot reach, such as on-premises sources.

questions.stem:
You must load data from a SQL Server database. The database administrator is willing to create objects in the database. You need to apply filters and column removals in Power Query that are pushed down to the source (query folding) and keep the solution easy to maintain.
What should you do?

options.text: Paste a hand-written SQL statement in the Advanced options of the connector.
options.explanation: Entering a native SQL statement generally stops folding for the steps that follow it, so later steps run locally.

options.text: Apply Table.Buffer to the source table before filtering.
options.explanation: Table.Buffer loads the table into memory and prevents later steps from folding.

options.text: Ask the administrator to create a view, and connect to the view.
options.explanation: Connecting to a view lets later steps such as filtering and removing columns fold into the source query, and the logic is maintained in one place in the database.

options.text: Import all tables, and then reduce the data by using calculated tables.
options.explanation: Importing everything and reducing afterward loads all the data and does not use query folding.

questions.stem:
You import a folder of CSV files by selecting Combine and Transform Data. Power Query creates a sample file query, a parameter, a Transform Sample File query, a function, and a combined table. You need to remove an unwanted column from every file's data before the files are combined.
Where should you apply this change?

options.text: In the parameter query
options.explanation: The parameter only identifies which sample file is used. It does not contain transformation steps.

options.text: In each file's source query manually
options.explanation: The individual files do not have separate queries. They are processed by the function.

options.text: In the Transform Sample File query
options.explanation: The Transform Sample File query defines the steps that the function applies to each file in the folder. Steps added to it run on every file before the results are combined.

options.text: In the combined table query only, after the files are combined
options.explanation: Editing only the combined table after the combine can also remove the column, but it does not change the transformations that are applied to each file.

questions.stem:
You need to create a calculated table named Discount that contains the values 0, 0.05, 0.1, and so on up to 1, in steps of 0.05.
Which function should you use?

options.text: CALENDAR(0, 1)
options.explanation: CALENDAR creates a table of dates and expects start and end dates.

options.text: ROW("Value", 0.05)
options.explanation: ROW returns a table that has only one row.

options.text: DISTINCT(0.05)
options.explanation: DISTINCT requires a table or a column as its argument, not a constant value.

options.text: GENERATESERIES(0, 1, 0.05)
options.explanation: GENERATESERIES creates a single-column table of values from a start value to an end value in a specified increment.

questions.stem: A scheduled refresh fails with the message The column 'Region' of the table wasn't found. The source team renamed the column from Region to SalesRegion. You cannot ask them to revert the change. What should you do?

options.text: Install an on-premises data gateway to reach the source team's server
options.explanation: A gateway affects connectivity. The service already reached the source because it found the table.

options.text: Increase the refresh timeout in the semantic model settings of the service so that the refresh can finish
options.explanation: The failure is caused by a missing column and not by a timeout.

options.text: Update the steps that reference Region to use SalesRegion, and republish the report
options.explanation: The query still refers to the old column name. Updating those steps to the new name fixes the error, and republishing applies the fix to the service.

options.text: Change the privacy level of the data source to Public and refresh again
options.explanation: Privacy levels control data sharing between sources and do not fix a missing column.

questions.stem:
A matrix shows Total Sales for each product in a row. You need to show a small line chart in each row that illustrates the monthly sales trend of that product.
What should you add?

options.text: A sparkline
options.explanation: Sparklines are mini charts that you can add to the rows of a table or matrix to show a trend.

options.text: A small multiples visual
options.explanation: Small multiples repeat a whole chart for each category, and they are not embedded in matrix rows.

options.text: Data bars
options.explanation: Data bars show a bar in each cell for a single value and not a trend over time.

options.text: A reference line
options.explanation: A reference line is a constant or calculated line on a chart, not a trend in each table row.

questions.stem:
A pie chart shows five product categories. You need each slice to display its category name together with its percentage of the total sales.
What should you configure?

options.text: A reference line at the percent of total for each category
options.explanation: A reference line applies to charts that have an axis.

options.text: A secondary axis that shows the percent of total for each category
options.explanation: A pie chart has no axes.

options.text: Data labels set to show the category and the percent of total
options.explanation: The data labels settings let you choose the content of labels, including the category name and the percent of the total.

options.text: A tooltip page that shows the percent of total for each slice
options.explanation: A tooltip page appears on hover and is not displayed on the slice.

questions.stem:
Your model combines an Excel workbook, a CSV file, and an Azure SQL table. Report users need the full set of DAX functions, including time intelligence, and fast visuals. Data only needs to be refreshed once per day.
Which storage mode should you use?

options.text: DirectQuery for all tables
options.explanation: DirectQuery cannot combine an Excel file and a CSV file in a single-source DirectQuery model. It also restricts some Power Query transformations and DAX functions.

options.text: Direct Lake
options.explanation: Direct Lake reads Delta tables from OneLake in Fabric. It cannot read directly from Excel, CSV, and Azure SQL sources.

options.text: Live connection
options.explanation: A live connection connects a report to an existing semantic model or Analysis Services model. It does not combine new sources.

options.text: Import
options.explanation: Import supports multiple source types, the full DAX function set, and the fastest query performance. A daily refresh satisfies the freshness requirement.

questions.reference: Choose between Import, DirectQuery, and Direct Lake

questions.stem:
You need to find out why the Sales by Product matrix is slow and test changes to its measure without modifying the model.
What should you do?

options.text: Replace the matrix with a table visual that has the same fields and the same filters
options.explanation: Changing the visual type does not change the slow DAX query that it sends.

options.text: Enable the Pause visuals option in the Optimize ribbon while you test the measure changes
options.explanation: Pause visuals stops visuals from refreshing while you edit. It does not make a query faster.

options.text: Copy the visual query from Performance Analyzer into DAX query view, and test with DEFINE MEASURE
options.explanation: The matrix spends its time in the DAX query. Running the copied query in DAX query view lets you test a modified measure definition with DEFINE MEASURE, without changing the model.

options.text: Reduce the number of data points that the matrix displays by using a Top N filter on the products
options.explanation: The matrix's display time is only 90 ms, so rendering is not the problem.

questions.reference: Performance Analyzer and DAX query view

questions.stem:
You need to improve the performance of the Orders scatter plot.
What should you do?

options.text: Change the storage mode of the Sales table to DirectQuery to reduce the memory used
options.explanation: DirectQuery would add source latency and does not reduce the rendering time.

options.text: Rewrite the measure of the visual to use variables to avoid repeated work
options.explanation: The DAX query takes only 120 ms, so optimizing the measure will not solve the problem.

options.text: Reduce the data points that the visual renders, for example with a Top N filter
options.explanation: Most of the time is spent in Visual display, which depends on the number of data points that the visual must draw. Fewer points reduce the rendering time.

options.text: Enable the query reduction options in the report settings of Power BI Desktop
options.explanation: Query reduction options reduce the number of queries that are sent, and the DAX query here is already fast.

questions.stem:
Each of the twelve KPI cards shows a high Other time and a low DAX query time.
What should you do?

options.text: Reduce the number of data points in each card by adding a Top N filter to every card
options.explanation: A card has a single value, so there are no data points to reduce.

options.text: Optimize the measures that the cards use by rewriting them to use variables and DIVIDE
options.explanation: The DAX query time of the cards is only 80 ms, so the measures are not the cause.

options.text: Disable Auto date/time in the data load settings so that the hidden date tables are removed from the model
options.explanation: Auto date/time affects the model size and has no effect on the waiting time of visuals.

options.text: Reduce the number of visuals on the page, for example by combining the cards in one multi-row card
options.explanation: The Other category includes time that a visual waits for other visuals' operations to complete. A page that has many visuals causes waiting, so you should have fewer visuals.

questions.stem:
You need to make sure that the data engine cache does not influence your Performance Analyzer results. You must not restart Power BI Desktop.
What should you do first?

options.text: Select Refresh visuals in the Performance Analyzer pane.
options.explanation: Refresh visuals reruns the queries, and the engine can answer them from its cache.

options.text: Select Start recording again.
options.explanation: Starting a new recording captures new results but does not clear any cache.

options.text: Add a blank report page, and select it.
options.explanation: Switching to a blank page clears the visual cache, not the data engine cache.

options.text: Connect DAX Studio to the model, and run Clear Cache.
options.explanation: DAX Studio can clear the data engine cache of the model that Desktop hosts, so the next test runs with a cold cache.

questions.stem:
You need to reduce the size of the model. The solution must not remove the ability to analyze sales by month and product.
What should you do?

options.text: Hide the transaction-level columns in report view.
options.explanation: Hidden columns remain in the model and still use memory.

options.text: Change the relationships of the Sales table to bidirectional.
options.explanation: Relationship direction does not reduce the size of the data.

options.text: Group the Sales table by month and product in Power Query, and sum the numeric columns.
options.explanation: Reducing the granularity of the fact table to month and product removes most of its rows, which reduces the model size substantially, and it still supports the required analysis.

options.text: Create a calculated table that summarizes Sales by month and product, and keep the transaction table loaded.
options.explanation: The transaction table would still be loaded, so the model would get larger, not smaller.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You add the following calculated column to the Customers table. Every customer row shows the same value, which equals the total of the Amount column in the Sales table. Customers has a one-to-many relationship to Sales.

{{code}}

You need each row to show the sales of that customer only.
What should you do?

options.text: Change the formula to SUMX(Sales, Sales[Amount])
options.explanation: SUMX over the whole Sales table has no filter from the current customer row, so it still returns the total.

options.text: Change the formula to CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]))
options.explanation: CALCULATE converts the row context of the current customer into a filter context. The filter flows through the relationship to Sales, so SUM adds up only that customer's rows.

options.text: Change the formula to RELATED(Sales[Amount])
options.explanation: RELATED works from the many side to the one side. From Customers to Sales it is not valid and would not aggregate.

options.text: Change the relationship to bidirectional
options.explanation: A row context does not filter other tables, regardless of the relationship direction.

questions.stem:
You need to see, for one selected column, the detailed statistics (such as count, minimum, and maximum) together with a value distribution chart in a pane beside the data preview.
What should you enable on the View tab of the Power Query Editor?

options.text: Column distribution
options.explanation: Column distribution shows a small frequency chart under each header but not the detailed statistics pane.

options.text: Column quality
options.explanation: Column quality shows percentages of valid, error, and empty values under each column header.

options.text: Monospaced
options.explanation: Monospaced changes the font used in the preview and is not a profiling feature.

options.text: Column profile
options.explanation: Column profile shows column statistics and the value distribution for the selected column in its own pane.

questions.reference: Data profiling tools in Power Query

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
You plan to mark a table as the date table in your model.
Which three requirements must the date column meet? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: It must include a time component.
options.explanation: A date column should have the Date data type without a time component for a standard date table.

options.text: It must be sorted in descending order.
options.explanation: The row order of the table does not matter for a date table.

options.text: It must contain unique values.
options.explanation: A date table needs one row for each date, so the date column must be unique.

options.text: It must contain contiguous dates with no gaps.
options.explanation: Time intelligence functions rely on a continuous range of dates. Missing dates cause incorrect results.

options.text: It must contain no blank values.
options.explanation: Blank values are not valid in the date column of a date table.

questions.reference: Set and use date tables in Power BI Desktop

questions.stem: A column named ContactInfo contains values such as Anna Lee (anna.lee@contoso.com). You do not know the M language and need a new column that contains only the email domain, for example contoso.com. What should you use?

options.text: Fill Down
options.explanation: Fill Down copies values into null cells, so it does not extract text.

options.text: Conditional Column
options.explanation: A conditional column returns different values based on rules and does not extract text patterns.

options.text: Group By
options.explanation: Group By summarizes rows. It does not extract part of a text value.

options.text: Column From Examples
options.explanation: Column From Examples lets you type the expected result for some rows, and Power Query generates the transformation for the rest.

questions.stem:
You need to compare how the sales of three product categories contribute to the total in each year, by showing the percentage share of each category as segments of equal-height columns.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Line chart
options.explanation: A line chart shows trends and not the composition of a total.

options.text: Clustered column chart
options.explanation: A clustered column chart places categories side by side and does not show shares of a total.

options.text: Stacked column chart
options.explanation: A stacked column chart shows absolute values, so the columns have different heights.

options.text: 100% stacked column chart
options.explanation: A 100% stacked column chart scales every column to the same height and shows each category's percentage share.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
The Sales table and the Targets table both contain a MonthKey column. In each table, MonthKey contains repeated values. Report users need a single month slicer that filters both tables. You must follow star schema best practices.
What should you do?

options.text: Merge the Targets table into the Sales table on MonthKey, and expand the target columns
options.explanation: Merging on a non-unique key repeats rows and produces incorrect totals.

options.text: Create a Month dimension table with one row per month, and relate it one-to-many to both tables
options.explanation: A shared dimension that has unique keys filters both fact tables through standard one-to-many relationships.

options.text: Append the Targets table to the Sales table and add a column that identifies the source
