options.explanation: Appending the tables mixes two facts that have different grains and meanings.

options.text: Create a direct many-to-many relationship between Sales[MonthKey] and Targets[MonthKey], and use it for the slicer
options.explanation: A direct many-to-many relationship works for some scenarios, but it is not the star schema best practice when a shared dimension can be created.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A central BI team owns a Sales semantic model in Workspace A. Analysts in Workspace B must create their own reports from this semantic model. The analysts must not be able to edit the semantic model and must not be added to Workspace A.
What should you do?

options.text: Copy the semantic model to Workspace B and give the analysts access to the copy.
options.explanation: A copy creates a second model that must be maintained and refreshed, and the analysts would no longer use the central model.

options.text: Add the analysts as Members of Workspace A so that they can use its semantic model.
options.explanation: Members can edit all the content of Workspace A, including the semantic model.

options.text: Share the reports of Workspace A with the analysts so that they can see the data.
options.explanation: Sharing reports lets the analysts view those reports, and they could not create new reports from the semantic model.

options.text: Grant the analysts the Build permission on the semantic model.
options.explanation: The Build permission lets users create new content, such as reports, from the semantic model without being able to edit the semantic model.

questions.stem:
Your model has 10 base measures. Report authors need a current-period, a year-to-date, and a prior-year version of every measure. You want to avoid creating 30 additional measures.
Which feature should you use?

options.text: A calculation group
options.explanation: A calculation group applies time intelligence logic to any measure through calculation items, so the three versions do not need separate measures.

options.text: A field parameter
options.explanation: A field parameter lets users switch which field appears in a visual. It does not change how measures are calculated.

options.text: Quick measures
options.explanation: A quick measure creates one new measure for each use and does not reduce the number of measures.

options.text: A what-if parameter
options.explanation: A what-if parameter provides an input value for scenarios and does not generate time variations of measures.

questions.stem:
An Excel sheet lists a region name once, on the first row of each group of stores. The rows below each region name show null in the Region column. You need every store row to carry the region name that appears above it.
Which transformation should you use on the Region column?

options.text: Fill Down
options.explanation: Fill Down copies the last non-null value downward to the null cells that follow it.

options.text: Unpivot Columns
options.explanation: Unpivot Columns rotates columns into rows. It does not fill missing values.

options.text: Replace Values
options.explanation: Replace Values can replace a fixed value with another fixed value, not a different value for each group.

options.text: Fill Up
options.explanation: Fill Up copies values upward, so rows would receive the region name from the group below them.

questions.stem:
In a visual calculation, you need to show the difference between the Total Sales of each row and the Total Sales of the previous row.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: [Total Sales] - FIRST([Total Sales])
options.explanation: FIRST returns the value of the first row, so all rows are compared with the first one.

options.text: [Total Sales] - PREVIOUS([Total Sales])
options.explanation: PREVIOUS returns the value from the previous row of the visual, so the difference compares each row with the one before it.

options.text: [Total Sales] - NEXT([Total Sales])
options.explanation: NEXT returns the value from the following row.

options.text: [Total Sales] - LAST([Total Sales])
options.explanation: LAST returns the value of the last row, so all rows are compared with the last one.

questions.stem:
A Sensors table stores a Temperature column that has 12 decimal places. Reports show the temperature with one decimal place only. The table has 300 million rows, and the model is too large.
What should you do?

options.text: Change the column to Text so that fewer distinct values are stored
options.explanation: Text values use more space and do not reduce the number of distinct values.

options.text: Hide the column in report view so that it is excluded from the model
options.explanation: Hiding does not reduce the memory used by the column.

options.text: Round the Temperature column to one decimal place in Power Query
options.explanation: Rounding reduces the number of distinct values that the engine must store, which improves compression and lowers the model size.

options.text: Change the format of the column to one decimal place in the model
options.explanation: The format changes only the display. The stored values keep all 12 decimal places.

questions.stem:
You apply several steps to a SQL Server query. For the step named Added Custom, the View Native Query option is unavailable, but it is available for the step before it.
What does this indicate?

options.text: The Added Custom step contains an error that prevents the query from loading
options.explanation: An error would be shown in the step or preview. The unavailable option indicates that folding stopped.

options.text: Query folding stops at the Added Custom step, so the later steps run in the Power Query engine
options.explanation: When View Native Query is unavailable for a step, that step could not be translated into a native query. Folding stops there, and the later steps run locally.

options.text: The data source does not accept native SQL for steps that add columns
options.explanation: The option was available for the earlier step, which shows the source does support native queries.

options.text: The query uses DirectQuery mode, so no native query can be shown for steps that add custom columns
options.explanation: DirectQuery is not what disables the option. DirectQuery models may still run foldable steps.

questions.stem: Two queries, Sales and Returns, reference a staging query named RawOrders. You delete RawOrders. What is the effect on Sales and Returns?

options.text: They keep their data because each stores its own copy of the RawOrders output.
options.explanation: A referencing query does not store its own copy of the source data. It reads the output of the query that it references.

options.text: They return errors because the query that they use as their source no longer exists.
options.explanation: Referencing queries use the output of RawOrders as their source. When it is deleted, their first step cannot be evaluated and they return errors.

options.text: They are automatically converted to duplicate queries that contain the steps of RawOrders.
options.explanation: Power Query does not convert referencing queries to duplicates when you delete the query that they use.

options.text: They are deleted together with RawOrders.
options.explanation: Deleting a query does not delete the queries that reference it.

questions.stem:
You have the latitude and longitude of each store. You need a map that places a bubble on each store location, with the size of each bubble determined by the store's sales.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Map
options.explanation: The Map visual plots locations as bubbles and uses a size field to represent a measure.

options.text: Funnel chart
options.explanation: A funnel chart shows stages of a process, not locations.

options.text: Filled map
options.explanation: A filled map shades whole regions such as countries or states, and it does not place bubbles on locations.

options.text: Ribbon chart
options.explanation: A ribbon chart shows rank changes over time.

questions.stem:
You are starting a new report page and do not know which content would be useful. You want Copilot to propose ideas for the page that are based on the semantic model.
What should you ask Copilot to do?

options.text: Create a drillthrough page
options.explanation: Creating a drillthrough page builds a navigation target for a specific field and is not a suggestion of content.

options.text: Apply the current theme to every page
options.explanation: Applying a theme changes formatting and does not suggest content.

options.text: Summarize the semantic model into a narrative visual
options.explanation: A narrative summarizes data that is already in the report and does not propose a new page.

options.text: Suggest content for a new report page
options.explanation: Copilot can suggest page topics based on the semantic model, and then it can create a page from the suggestion that you select.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You define an RLS role named West in Power BI Desktop and publish the model to the service. Users who should be restricted still see all of the data in the reports.
You verify that the users have the Viewer role in the workspace.
What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The semantic model must be published as a paginated report.
options.explanation: A semantic model is not published as a paginated report.

options.text: The reports use bar charts instead of tables to show the data of the model
options.explanation: The type of visual does not influence RLS.

options.text: The role must be defined in the service by using DAX Studio.
options.explanation: Roles are defined in Power BI Desktop, and DAX Studio is not required.

options.text: The users were not added as members of the West role in the service
options.explanation: Defining a role in Desktop does not assign anyone to it. You must add the users or groups as members of the role in the security settings of the semantic model in the service.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Before you change a column name in a shared semantic model, you want to know which reports and dashboards, including those in other workspaces, depend on it.
What should you use?

options.text: Impact analysis in the lineage view
options.explanation: The lineage view and its impact analysis show the downstream items, such as reports and dashboards, that use a semantic model, including items in other workspaces.

options.text: Usage metrics report
options.explanation: A usage metrics report shows how items are used by viewers, and it does not show which items depend on a semantic model.

options.text: Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer measures the time that visuals need to load in a report.

options.text: The Query Dependencies view in Power Query Editor
options.explanation: Query Dependencies shows the relationships between queries within one Power BI Desktop file.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Executives want a single page in the Power BI service that shows a few key visuals from three different reports, each from a separate semantic model.
What should you create?

options.text: A Power BI app that includes the three reports as separate items
options.explanation: An app is a container for content and does not combine visuals.

options.text: A dashboard that contains tiles pinned from the three reports
options.explanation: A dashboard is a single page of tiles. You can pin visuals from several reports and semantic models to the same dashboard.

options.text: A new report that has three pages, one for each source report
options.explanation: A report uses one semantic model and cannot combine visuals from separate semantic models that way.

options.text: A paginated report that combines the three source reports
options.explanation: A paginated report is meant for printable output.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
Report consumers want to change the visual type of a chart and swap the fields on its axis on their own, without opening the report in edit mode and without affecting other users.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a field parameter to every visual.
options.explanation: A field parameter lets users switch fields with a slicer, but the author must set it up, and it does not let users change the visual type.

options.text: Give the consumers the Contributor role in the workspace of the report.
options.explanation: The Contributor role would allow users to edit and publish content, which is far more than the requirement and affects the shared report.

options.text: Enable personalized visuals for the report and for the visual.
options.explanation: Personalize visuals lets consumers change the visual type, fields, and other options for their own view, and saves it for them only.

options.text: Publish a separate copy of the report for each consumer.
options.explanation: Separate copies create unnecessary maintenance.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: A Sales table has data for the last 10 years. The business needs 5 years of history in the report. Only the data of the last 10 days changes in the source system, and the full refresh takes too long. What should you configure in the incremental refresh policy?

options.text: Store rows in the last 5 years, and refresh rows in the last 10 days.
options.explanation: The first setting defines how much history is kept in the model, and the second defines the window of recent data that is refreshed each time.

options.text: Store rows in the last 5 years, and refresh rows in the last 5 years.
options.explanation: Refreshing 5 years of data at each refresh would not reduce the refresh time.

options.text: Store rows in the last 10 years, and refresh rows in the last 10 years.
options.explanation: This keeps more history than needed and refreshes everything, which does not reduce the refresh time.

options.text: Store rows in the last 10 days, and refresh rows in the last 5 years.
options.explanation: This would keep only 10 days of history and refresh 5 years of data, which is the opposite of the requirement.

questions.stem:
The Sales table has the columns Quantity and UnitPrice. You need a measure that returns the weighted average unit price, in which each price is weighted by the quantity sold.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: AVERAGE(Sales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: AVERAGE returns the simple average of the prices without weighting by quantity.

options.text: AVERAGEX(Sales, Sales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: AVERAGEX over the unit price returns the same simple average.

options.text: DIVIDE(SUMX(Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice]), COUNTROWS(Sales))
options.explanation: Dividing revenue by the number of rows returns the average revenue per order line.

options.text: DIVIDE(SUMX(Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice]), SUM(Sales[Quantity]))
options.explanation: The numerator is the total revenue and the denominator is the total quantity, which is the quantity-weighted average price.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
Executives want to type natural language questions such as total sales by region this year directly on a dashboard and get an immediate answer, and they want to pin useful answers as tiles.
What should you use?

options.text: The Q&A question box on the dashboard
options.explanation: The Q&A box on a dashboard answers natural language questions with visuals that can be pinned as tiles.

options.text: A drillthrough page that opens from a data point
options.explanation: A drillthrough page is a navigation target inside a report.

options.text: A paginated report with a parameter for the question
options.explanation: A paginated report is a fixed layout document and does not answer ad-hoc questions.

options.text: A bookmark navigator that switches between saved views
options.explanation: A bookmark navigator switches between saved report states.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
The tables Customers and CustomerDetails have a one-to-one relationship on CustomerID, and both tables are small. You must simplify the model.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a calculated table that combines both tables, and hide the original tables.
options.explanation: A calculated table duplicates the data and increases the model size.

options.text: Keep both tables, and change the cross-filter direction to Single.
options.explanation: One-to-one relationships filter in both directions, and the Single direction option is not available.

options.text: Change the relationship to many-to-many.
options.explanation: Many-to-many is less precise than one-to-one and adds ambiguity.

options.text: Merge the two tables into a single Customers table.
options.explanation: A one-to-one relationship usually indicates attributes of the same entity that were split across tables. Combining them gives a simpler model with no relationship to maintain.

questions.stem:
You publish a semantic model whose queries use a Power Query parameter named ServerName. The database server is later renamed. You need to update the parameter value without opening Power BI Desktop.
Where should you make the change?

options.text: The Endorsement and discovery section of the semantic model settings
options.explanation: Endorsement and discovery lets you promote or certify the semantic model. It has nothing to do with query parameters.

options.text: The Data source credentials section of the semantic model settings in the service
options.explanation: The data source credentials section stores how Power BI authenticates to a source. It does not hold parameter values.

options.text: The Scheduled refresh section of the semantic model settings
options.explanation: The scheduled refresh section controls when refreshes run, not the values that queries use.

options.text: The Parameters section of the semantic model settings in the Power BI service
options.explanation: Parameter values for a published semantic model can be edited in the Parameters section of its settings in the service.

questions.reference: Manage semantic model parameters in the Power BI service

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
You published a workspace app last month. Yesterday you fixed a calculation in a report in the workspace and republished it from Power BI Desktop. App users still see the old calculation.
What should you do?

options.text: Update the workspace app.
options.explanation: App users see the version of the content that was published in the app. After changing the workspace content, you must update the app so that the changes are released.

options.text: Create a new workspace.
options.explanation: A new workspace would require recreating the content and the app and is not needed.

options.text: Reassign the users to the Viewer role.
options.explanation: Users of an app are not assigned workspace roles, and their access does not decide which version they see.

options.text: Ask the users to clear their browser cache.
options.explanation: The app does not show the new version of the report, so clearing the cache does not help.

questions.reference: Configure and update a workspace app

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
The 120 salespeople of the West region are members of a Microsoft Entra security group. People join and leave the group every month. You need the RLS role West to always match the group membership with the least administrative effort.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a role for each salesperson, and add each person to a role
options.explanation: A role for each person would multiply the administration.

options.text: Add the group as a Contributor in the workspace of the semantic model that has the role
options.explanation: A Contributor would not be restricted by the role, and workspace roles do not set RLS membership.

options.text: Add the security group as a member of the RLS role in the Power BI service.
options.explanation: When a group is a member of the role, changes in the group membership are picked up automatically, so no one needs to maintain the role.

options.text: Add each salesperson individually to the role every month.
options.explanation: Adding every user individually requires manual maintenance each month.

questions.stem:
Your organization has a brand color palette. You need every new report to use the same colors and font styles without formatting each visual manually.
What should you do?

options.text: Set the default color of each data series in the Model view.
options.explanation: Model view does not control the colors of visuals.

options.text: Create a field parameter that contains the colors.
options.explanation: A field parameter lets users switch fields in a visual. It does not store formatting.

options.text: Format one visual, and copy it to every report.
options.explanation: Copying one visual does not apply the formatting to the other visuals and reports automatically.

options.text: Create a theme JSON file, and import it in each report.
options.explanation: A theme file defines colors, fonts, and default visual formatting, and it can be imported into any report.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A DirectQuery report shows live order data. The visuals must refresh only when new orders arrive, and not at every interval. A measure that returns the highest OrderID is available.
What should you configure?

options.text: Scheduled refresh in the Power BI service every few minutes of the day
options.explanation: Scheduled refresh updates imported data in the semantic model and does not apply to a DirectQuery page.

options.text: Automatic page refresh with the change detection type that uses the measure
options.explanation: Change detection checks a measure at an interval and refreshes the visuals only when the measure value changes, for example when MAX(OrderID) increases.

options.text: Automatic page refresh with the fixed interval type set to one minute
options.explanation: A fixed interval refreshes the visuals at every interval, even if no new data has arrived.

options.text: A subscription on the report that is sent every time that a new order arrives
options.explanation: A subscription sends a snapshot of the report by email and does not refresh the visuals.

questions.stem:
An Orders query includes a column named Items. Each cell contains a nested list of product names. You need a table in which every product from each list has its own row, and the other Orders columns are repeated on those rows.
Which transformation should you use on the Items column?

options.text: Expand to New Rows
options.explanation: Expand to New Rows creates a new row for every list item and repeats the values of the other columns on those rows.

options.text: Extract Values
options.explanation: Extract Values converts each list into a single delimited text value, so the products stay in one row.

options.text: Pivot Column
options.explanation: Pivot Column turns row values into columns. It does not expand lists.

options.text: Convert to Table
options.explanation: Convert to Table applies to a list value, not to a column of lists, and it does not repeat the other order columns.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to TOTALYTD([Total Sales], 'Date'[Date])?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESYTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: TOTALYTD is a shortcut that evaluates the expression over the dates returned by DATESYTD.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESQTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: DATESQTD returns the dates from the start of the quarter.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR returns the same dates one year earlier and does not accumulate from the start of the year.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESMTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: DATESMTD returns the dates from the start of the month.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns Low when Total Sales is less than 1000, Medium when it is less than 5000, and High in all other cases.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: SWITCH(TRUE(), [Total Sales] < 1000, "Low", [Total Sales] < 5000, "Medium", "High")
options.explanation: SWITCH(TRUE()) evaluates the conditions in order and returns the result of the first condition that is true. Testing the smaller threshold first gives the correct bands.

options.text: SWITCH(TRUE(), [Total Sales] >= 5000, "High", [Total Sales] < 1000, "Medium", "Low")
options.explanation: The labels are assigned incorrectly because values below 1000 return Medium and values between 1000 and 5000 return Low.

options.text: SWITCH([Total Sales], < 1000, "Low", < 5000, "Medium", "High")
options.explanation: SWITCH cannot compare an expression to a partial comparison such as less than 1000, so this syntax is not valid.

options.text: SWITCH(TRUE(), [Total Sales] < 5000, "Medium", [Total Sales] < 1000, "Low", "High")
options.explanation: Values below 1000 also satisfy the first condition, so they are labeled Medium and Low is never returned.

questions.stem:
You open the Data source settings dialog in Power BI Desktop.
Which two tasks can you perform from this dialog? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Configure the scheduled refresh frequency
options.explanation: Refresh schedules are configured in the Power BI service.

options.text: Change the server name of a data source for all queries that use it
options.explanation: Change Source lets you modify the data source location, such as the server name, for the queries that use it.

options.text: Create a relationship between two tables
options.explanation: Relationships are created in Model view or through the Manage relationships dialog.

options.text: Change the storage mode of a table
options.explanation: Storage mode is a table property configured in Model view, not in Data source settings.

options.text: Edit the credentials and privacy level of a data source
options.explanation: Edit Permissions lets you update the credentials and the privacy level for a data source.

questions.reference: Manage data source settings in Power BI Desktop

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A manager wants a static snapshot of the pages of a report to include in a board presentation. The manager does not need the slicers or interactivity.
What should the manager do in the Power BI service?

options.text: Publish the report to the web and embed the link in the presentation
options.explanation: Publish to web makes the data public and is not appropriate for a board document.

options.text: Create a subscription with a data alert that is sent to the board members
options.explanation: A subscription sends snapshots by email on a schedule, which is not what is needed for a one-time presentation.

options.text: Use the Export option to create a PowerPoint file or a PDF file of the report
options.explanation: Export creates a PowerPoint or PDF file with a snapshot of the report pages, which is suitable for a presentation.

options.text: Create a paginated report for each page and export each report separately
options.explanation: Creating a paginated report for each page is unnecessary effort.

questions.stem:
A calculated column named Profit in a 200-million-row Sales table is defined as Sales[Amount] - Sales[Cost]. Reports only use the sum of profit in visuals.
You need to reduce the model size without changing the report results.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a second calculated column that rounds the profit to fewer digits and hide the first
options.explanation: Another calculated column adds more stored data.

options.text: Hide the calculated column so that it is not loaded into the model
options.explanation: Hiding the column does not remove the stored data.

options.text: Remove the calculated column and create the measure SUM(Sales[Amount]) - SUM(Sales[Cost])
options.explanation: A measure is calculated only when it is needed, and it stores no per-row data. The result of the sum is the same as the sum of the row-level difference.

options.text: Change the data type of the calculated column to Text so that the column is compressed better
options.explanation: Text columns are usually stored less efficiently than numeric columns.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A team of five report authors needs a gateway to refresh several semantic models from the same on-premises data source, and some of those reports use DirectQuery. The gateway must be managed centrally by the IT department and not by an individual user's computer.
Which gateway should you install?

options.text: No gateway, because Power BI Desktop includes one
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop connects to local sources when it is run, but it does not refresh semantic models in the service.

options.text: An on-premises data gateway in standard mode
options.explanation: The standard mode gateway supports multiple users and data sources, DirectQuery, and Import, and it can be administered centrally.

options.text: An on-premises data gateway in personal mode
options.explanation: The personal mode is meant for one user and supports only scheduled refresh of imported data. It does not support DirectQuery.

options.text: Both gateways on the same computer
options.explanation: Installing both modes on the same computer does not remove the limits of the personal mode.

questions.stem:
Refresh of your Power BI Desktop file is slow. The file loads 30 tables from different sources one after another. The sources can handle several simultaneous requests.
Which option should you configure to reduce the refresh time?

options.text: Enable Parallel loading of tables
options.explanation: Parallel loading lets Power BI Desktop evaluate and load several tables at the same time, which shortens the refresh.

options.text: Disable Auto date/time
options.explanation: Auto date/time reduces the model size but does not change how tables are loaded.

options.text: Set all tables to Dual storage mode
options.explanation: Storage mode determines how the data is stored, not how tables are loaded during a refresh.

options.text: Enable Never detect column types
options.explanation: Type detection is performed while you author queries and does not parallelize loading.

questions.stem:
You maintain a scorecard with a Revenue metric. The current value of the metric must update automatically from the Total Sales measure in an existing Power BI report, and users must not enter it manually.
What should you do?

options.text: Connect the metric to the visual in the report that displays Total Sales.
options.explanation: A connected metric takes its current value, and optionally the target, from a report visual, and it updates when the data in the model refreshes.

options.text: Add a subscription to the report.
options.explanation: A subscription sends the report by email and does not feed a metric.

options.text: Set the current value of the metric manually every month by editing the metric.
options.explanation: A manual value requires a person to type the value each time.

options.text: Export the report to Excel and import the file in the scorecard.
options.explanation: Importing an exported file creates a static copy of the data.

questions.stem:
Your report has 15 queries that all use the SQL Server instance SQLDEV01 and the same database. You need to repoint the report to SQLPROD01 with the least administrative effort.
What should you do?

options.text: Duplicate each query and change its Source step.
options.explanation: Duplicating queries leaves the old queries in place and makes the model harder to maintain.

options.text: Delete the tables, re-import them from SQLPROD01, and recreate the relationships.
options.explanation: Deleting tables removes relationships and measures that depend on them.

options.text: Open the Advanced Editor of each query and edit the server name.
options.explanation: Editing 15 queries individually works but takes more effort and risks mistakes.

options.text: Open Data source settings and use Change Source for the data source.
options.explanation: The Change Source option in Data source settings updates the server name for all queries that use that source in one step.

questions.reference: Manage data source settings in Power BI Desktop

questions.stem:
In a Sales query that has 50 million rows, you merged the Products query to expand the ProductCategory column. Refresh is slow, and the model is large. You must keep a star schema.
What should you do instead?

options.text: Merge each dimension into Sales so that the model has a single wide table of all the columns
options.explanation: A single wide table stores the repeated attributes on every row, which increases the model size.

options.text: Switch the Products query to DirectQuery storage mode
options.explanation: Changing the storage mode of a dimension does not remove the cause of the large merge and does not reduce the model.

options.text: Duplicate the Sales query to calculate the category.
options.explanation: Duplicating a 50-million-row query adds work and size.

options.text: Keep Sales narrow, load Products as a dimension, and relate the two tables
options.explanation: A star schema keeps descriptive attributes in dimension tables and relates them to a narrow fact table. This avoids repeating text values across 50 million rows and removes an expensive merge.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
A table visual lists products. You need a measure that ranks each product by Total Sales so that the product with the highest sales has rank 1. The ranking must be calculated across all products, and it must not be affected by the product in each row.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: RANKX(Products, [Total Sales])
options.explanation: Products is filtered to the product in each row, so each product is ranked against only itself and gets rank 1.

options.text: RANKX(ALL(Products[ProductName]), [Total Sales])
options.explanation: ALL returns every product regardless of the row filter. RANKX compares the current product's sales with all products, and the default order is descending.

options.text: RANKX(VALUES(Products[ProductName]), [Total Sales])
options.explanation: VALUES returns only the visible product in each row, so the result is the same as for RANKX over the Products table.

options.text: RANKX(ALL(Products[ProductName]), [Total Sales], , ASC)
options.explanation: ASC ranks the lowest sales as 1, which is the opposite of the requirement.

questions.stem:
You create a query that merges an HR table from an internal SQL Server database with a public currency-rate file downloaded from a website. HR data is confidential and must never be sent to any other data source, including other internal sources, while queries are evaluated.
Which privacy level should you assign to the SQL Server data source?

options.text: Public
options.explanation: A Public source can share data with any other source.

options.text: Ignore privacy levels
options.explanation: Ignoring privacy levels disables the checks, so data could be sent to any source.

options.text: Organizational
options.explanation: An Organizational source is isolated from Public sources but can still share data with other Organizational sources. That does not meet the requirement for all other sources.

options.text: Private
options.explanation: A Private source is isolated from all other sources, so its data is never sent to them.

questions.stem:
A text column named Notes contains cells that appear blank but actually contain only spaces. Column quality reports 0% empty values. You need these cells to be treated as null.
Which two transformations should you apply, in order? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Replace Values to replace empty text with null
options.explanation: After trimming, the cells hold empty text. Replacing empty text with null converts them to true null values.

options.text: Trim
options.explanation: Trim removes leading and trailing spaces, turning cells that contain only spaces into empty text.

options.text: Remove Errors
options.explanation: There are no errors in the column, so Remove Errors has no effect.

options.text: Capitalize Each Word
options.explanation: Capitalize Each Word changes letter case only.

options.text: Clean
options.explanation: Clean removes non-printable characters. It does not remove ordinary spaces.

questions.reference: Transform text columns in Power Query

questions.stem:
An Orders query has the date columns OrderDate and ShipDate. You need a custom column that returns the number of days between the two dates as a number.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: [ShipDate] + [OrderDate]
options.explanation: Adding two dates is not a valid operation.

options.text: Date.DaysInMonth([ShipDate])
options.explanation: Date.DaysInMonth returns the number of days in the month of a single date.

options.text: DAYS([ShipDate], [OrderDate])
options.explanation: DAYS is not a Power Query M function. Date subtraction and the Duration functions are used in M instead.

options.text: Duration.Days([ShipDate] - [OrderDate])
options.explanation: Subtracting two dates returns a duration, and Duration.Days returns the days of that duration as a number.

questions.reference: Duration functions in Power Query M

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
A measure named Profit Margin returns values such as 0.2534. Report authors need the measure to appear as 25.3% in all visuals.
What should you configure?

options.text: A sort by column for the measure, based on the margin value
options.explanation: Sort by column applies to columns and does not format values.

options.text: The format of the measure, set to Percentage with one decimal place
options.explanation: The format of a measure controls how its value is displayed in all visuals that use it.

options.text: The data category of the measure, set to Percentage in Model view
options.explanation: Data category is for hints such as URL or geography. It is not used to format numbers as percentages.

options.text: The Summarize by property of the measure, set to Average
options.explanation: Summarize by applies to columns, not to measures, which already define their own aggregation.

questions.stem: You try to create a one-to-many relationship from a Customer table to a Sales table on CustomerID, but Power BI reports that the column on the one side contains duplicate values. Profiling shows that each CustomerID appears in several rows of the Customer table, and the rows are otherwise identical. What should you do?

options.text: Remove duplicates on the CustomerID column in Power Query
options.explanation: The one side of a one-to-many relationship must contain unique values. Removing duplicate CustomerID rows in the dimension query fixes the cause.

options.text: Hide the CustomerID column in the Customer table of the model
options.explanation: Hiding a column only affects its visibility in report view. It does not change its values.

options.text: Change the data type of CustomerID to Text and reload the data
options.explanation: Changing the data type does not remove duplicate values.

options.text: Change the relationship to bidirectional cross-filtering
options.explanation: Cross-filter direction does not remove duplicates, and it does not make a duplicated column valid for the one side.

questions.reference: Remove duplicates and keys in dimension tables

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem: You need to enable users to open the Product Detail page from any product in the Summary page. What should you do?

options.text: On the Summary page, create a bookmark for each product.
options.explanation: Bookmarks for each product would be hard to maintain and would not use the product that the user right-clicked.

options.text: On the Product Detail page, add ProductName to the drillthrough filters.
options.explanation: Fields in the drillthrough well make the page a drillthrough target. Users right-click a product value and navigate to the page, with the product passed as a filter.

options.text: On the Product Detail page, add a page-level filter on Product[ProductName].
options.explanation: A page-level filter applies a fixed filter selection to the page, and it does not create a navigation path from other pages.

options.text: On the Product Detail page, add Product[Category] to the drillthrough filters.
options.explanation: With Category as the drillthrough field, the page would be filtered to a category and not to a single product, and users could drill through only from category values.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
You need to make the Summary page easy to read for the regional managers who use phones in portrait orientation. The desktop layout must not change.
What should you do?

options.text: Change the page size of the Summary page to 4:3 so that it fits the phone screens better.
options.explanation: Changing the page size would change the page for all users and would not produce a portrait layout for phones.

options.text: Duplicate the report and delete the visuals that are not needed on phones.
options.explanation: A duplicate report doubles the maintenance, and the requirement is to use the same report.

options.text: Create a mobile layout for the page in Mobile layout view of Power BI Desktop.
options.explanation: The mobile layout is a separate portrait layout that you design for the same page. Desktop and browser users keep the original layout.

options.text: Reduce the font size of all visuals on the page.
options.explanation: Smaller fonts make the content harder to read on a small screen, and they also change the desktop layout.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
You need to make the report easier to use for people who depend on screen readers.
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Configure the Region slicer to use a dropdown style.
options.explanation: The style of a slicer does not provide information to a screen reader.

options.text: Add alternative text to each visual.
options.explanation: Alt text gives a screen reader a description of what each visual shows.

options.text: Disable the Filters pane.
options.explanation: Hiding the Filters pane removes a way for users to interact with the report, and it does not improve accessibility.

options.text: Create a bookmark for each visual.
options.explanation: Bookmarks capture report states for navigation and do not describe visuals to a screen reader.

options.text: Set a logical tab order for the visuals on each page.
options.explanation: The tab order controls the order in which keyboard and screen reader users move through the visuals, so it should follow the logical reading order.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
You need to show the monthly Total Sales of a product when users hover over that product in the bar chart.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a line chart beside the bar chart, and set the interaction between the two visuals to hover
options.explanation: The Edit interactions options are filter, highlight, and none. There is no hover option.

options.text: Create a drillthrough page for the product, and enable hover for the drillthrough on the bar chart so that it appears
options.explanation: Drillthrough requires a user action such as a right-click, and it has no hover option.

options.text: Create a tooltip page that has the line chart, turn on Allow use as tooltip, and set the bar chart to use the page
options.explanation: A report page tooltip can contain any visuals. The page that has the tooltip option enabled is selected as the tooltip of the visual, and it is filtered to the item under the pointer.

options.text: Add the Month field to the Tooltips field well of the bar chart, so that the tooltip lists the months
options.explanation: The Tooltips well adds fields to the default tooltip, which shows text values, and it does not display a chart.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
You need to make sure that the Region selected in the slicer on the Summary page is also applied on the Product Detail page.
What should you use?

options.text: A report-level filter on Region
options.explanation: A report-level filter is a fixed filter and does not follow the user's slicer selection.

options.text: Edit interactions
options.explanation: Edit interactions controls how visuals on one page affect each other, and it does not affect other pages.

options.text: Sync slicers
options.explanation: Sync slicers lets one slicer control the same field on several pages, and the user's selection carries over.

options.text: A drillthrough filter on Region
options.explanation: A drillthrough filter applies only when a user navigates through drillthrough.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem: You are creating a workspace app that contains four reports. When users open the app, they must see the Executive Overview report first, and a report named Test Version must not appear in the navigation. What should you configure?

options.text: A sensitivity label on the app and on each report
options.explanation: A sensitivity label classifies content and does not change the order or visibility of items.

options.text: A bookmark in every report that the app contains
options.explanation: Bookmarks are inside reports and do not control app navigation.

options.text: The app navigation, with the order of the items and Test Version hidden
options.explanation: The app navigation lets you control the order of the items and which items are visible to users.

options.text: A row-level security role on the semantic model of the app
options.explanation: RLS restricts rows of data and does not change navigation.

questions.stem:
You connect Power BI Desktop to a certified semantic model in the Power BI service by using a live connection.
Which two actions can you NOT perform on the model from this report? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Add conditional formatting to a table visual
options.explanation: Conditional formatting is a visual formatting feature and is allowed.

options.text: Apply a theme to the report
options.explanation: Report formatting such as themes is supported because it belongs to the report, not the model.

options.text: Create a report-level measure
options.explanation: Report-level measures are supported over a live connection. They exist only in the report.

options.text: Create a relationship between two tables
options.explanation: With a live connection the model is read-only, so you cannot create or edit relationships in the report.

options.text: Add transformation steps in Power Query
options.explanation: Power Query is not available because the data is not loaded or shaped by the report.

questions.reference: Live connection to Power BI semantic models

questions.stem:
A report has a report-level filter Region is West. A visual on one page has a visual-level filter Region is East.
What does the visual show?

options.text: Data for West only, because the report-level filter overrides the visual-level filter
options.explanation: A report-level filter does not override visual-level filters. They are applied together.

options.text: Data for East only, because the visual-level filter overrides the report-level filter
options.explanation: A visual-level filter does not override a report-level filter. They are applied together.

options.text: No data, because the filters are combined and no row satisfies both
options.explanation: Filters at different levels are combined with AND logic. No row can have both West and East values in the Region column, so the visual is empty.

options.text: Data for both West and East
options.explanation: Combining the filters would give OR logic only if they were part of one filter that selects both values.

questions.reference: Filter levels in Power BI reports

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You are deciding between calculated columns and measures.
Which two statements are true? Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: A measure is evaluated at query time in the current filter context.
options.explanation: Measures are calculated when a visual is rendered and respond to the filter context, so their values change with slicers and visual layout.

options.text: A measure is stored for each row and increases the size of the model like a column.
options.explanation: Measures are not stored per row. Only their definition is stored.

options.text: A calculated column can be used only in the Values area of a visual.
options.explanation: A calculated column can be used on axes, in slicers, and in filters, in addition to values.

options.text: A calculated column changes its values when users select a slicer.
options.explanation: A calculated column is calculated per row at refresh time and does not react to slicer selections.

options.text: A calculated column is computed during data refresh and stored in the model.
options.explanation: Calculated columns are calculated when the model is refreshed. Their values are stored, so they increase the model size.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A drillthrough page named Order Detail ignores the Year slicer on the source page when users drill through from a table. The Keep all filters option on the drillthrough page is turned off, and Year is not one of the drillthrough fields.
What should you do?

options.text: Convert the drillthrough page to a tooltip page.
options.explanation: A tooltip page appears on hover and is not a drillthrough destination.

options.text: Turn on Keep all filters on the Order Detail page.
options.explanation: With Keep all filters turned on, the filters from the source page, including slicers, are passed to the drillthrough page together with the drillthrough field.

options.text: Add a page-level filter on Year to the source page.
options.explanation: A page-level filter on the source page does not change what is passed when Keep all filters is off, and the slicer is the existing filter.

options.text: Disable cross-filtering on the table.
options.explanation: Disabling cross-filtering changes how visuals interact on the source page, and it does not pass the slicer to another page.

questions.stem:
You change the data type of a Quantity column from Text to Whole Number. Some source rows contain the text N/A, so the conversion produces errors. The business requires that these rows are kept and treated as a quantity of 0.
What should you do after the type conversion step?

options.text: Use Replace Errors with a value of 0 on the Quantity column.
options.explanation: Replace Errors substitutes the specified value for error cells while keeping the rows.

options.text: Use Remove Errors on the Quantity column to clean the rows
options.explanation: Remove Errors deletes the rows that contain errors, which violates the requirement to keep them.

options.text: Use Keep Errors on the Quantity column and replace them later
options.explanation: Keep Errors keeps only the rows that have errors and removes all the other rows.

options.text: Use Replace Values to replace null with 0 on the Quantity column
options.explanation: The cells contain errors, not null values, so replacing null does not affect them.

questions.stem:
You need to reduce the size of a Power BI Import model without changing the reports.
Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Remove historical rows that no report requires.
options.explanation: Removing rows that are never used reduces the amount of data that is stored.

options.text: Convert datetime columns to dates when the time part is not needed.
options.explanation: Dropping the time part reduces the number of distinct values, which improves compression.

options.text: Hide the unused columns in report view.
options.explanation: Hiding a column only removes it from the field list. The data is still loaded and uses memory.

options.text: Add a calculated column for every metric that the reports use.
options.explanation: Calculated columns are stored in the model, so adding them increases the size.

options.text: Remove columns that no report, measure, or relationship uses.
options.explanation: Columns that are not needed use memory. Removing them in Power Query reduces the size.

questions.reference: Reduce the size of a semantic model

questions.stem: You need a visual that shows the relationship between Total Sales (horizontal axis) and Total Profit (vertical axis) for each product. The size of each marker must represent the quantity sold. Which visual should you use?

options.text: Scatter chart
options.explanation: A scatter chart plots two numeric values on its axes and can use the size of the markers for a third measure.

options.text: Funnel chart
options.explanation: A funnel chart shows stages of a process and cannot plot two measures on axes.

options.text: Treemap
options.explanation: A treemap shows the size of categories as rectangles but does not plot two measures against each other.

options.text: Line and clustered column chart
options.explanation: A combo chart shows measures against a shared categorical axis and does not plot the relationship between two measures.

questions.stem:
A bar chart shows Total Sales by Country. Management uses a custom division of the countries into sales territories that is not in the data source. You need to show the sales by territory without changing the source or the model queries.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a bin with a size of 10 on the Country column, and use the bin in the chart
options.explanation: Binning applies to numeric and date fields to create equal-sized ranges, and it does not combine specific text values.

options.text: Create a cluster on the Country column, and use the cluster in the chart
options.explanation: Clustering groups data points by their similarity on numeric measures and cannot reproduce a management-defined list.

options.text: Add a trend line from the Analytics pane to the bar chart of the countries
options.explanation: A trend line draws a regression line on a numeric chart and does not group values.

options.text: Select the countries in the visual, group them with a manual group, and use the group
options.explanation: Grouping lets you combine selected values of a field in a group that you name, such as a territory, and use the group in visuals.

questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the year-over-year growth percentage of Total Sales. A positive value must mean that sales increased compared with the same period last year.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: VAR LY = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) RETURN [Total Sales] - LY
options.explanation: This returns the absolute difference and not a percentage.

options.text: VAR LY = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) RETURN DIVIDE([Total Sales] - LY, LY)
options.explanation: The change is the current sales minus last year's sales, divided by last year's sales. A positive result means growth.

options.text: VAR LY = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) RETURN DIVIDE([Total Sales], LY)
options.explanation: This returns the ratio of current to last year's sales. A value of 1.1 would mean a 10 percent increase, not 10 percent growth.

options.text: VAR LY = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) RETURN DIVIDE(LY - [Total Sales], LY)
options.explanation: The numerator is reversed, so growth appears as a negative percentage.

questions.stem:
You need to author a paginated report.
Which tool should you use?

options.text: DAX query view
options.explanation: DAX query view runs DAX queries against a model.

options.text: Power BI Desktop
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop is used to create interactive reports and semantic models.

options.text: Power BI Report Builder
options.explanation: Power BI Report Builder is the authoring tool for paginated reports.

options.text: Power Query Editor
options.explanation: Power Query Editor shapes data. It does not author reports.

questions.stem:
A DirectQuery Sales table has 2 billion rows. Most reports show totals by month and product, and they are slow. You want the most common queries to be answered from memory, while detailed queries still reach the source.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a calculated table with SUMMARIZE over Sales and relate it to the dimensions
options.explanation: A calculated table over a DirectQuery table would not be mapped as an aggregation, and the visuals would not use it automatically.

options.text: Add an Import aggregation table grouped by month and product, and use Manage aggregations
options.explanation: User-defined aggregations let Power BI answer queries at the aggregated grain from the Import table, and send detailed queries to the DirectQuery detail table.

options.text: Set all relationships to bidirectional so that queries use fewer joins
options.explanation: Relationship direction does not reduce the amount of data that is scanned.

options.text: Change the Sales table to Dual storage mode so that it is cached in memory for all queries
options.explanation: A Dual table can be cached, but a 2-billion-row fact table is not suited to caching in memory.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
The Sales table has a ProductID column. The Prices table has the columns ProductID and ListPrice, and no relationship exists between the two tables. You need a calculated column in Sales that returns the ListPrice for each product.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: RELATEDTABLE(Prices)
options.explanation: RELATEDTABLE returns a table and also requires a relationship.

options.text: SELECTEDVALUE(Prices[ListPrice])
options.explanation: SELECTEDVALUE depends on the filter context, which is empty in a calculated column row, so it returns a blank unless there is exactly one price in the table.

options.text: LOOKUPVALUE(Prices[ListPrice], Prices[ProductID], Sales[ProductID])
options.explanation: LOOKUPVALUE searches the Prices table for the row where ProductID equals the current Sales row's ProductID and returns its ListPrice. It does not need a relationship.

options.text: RELATED(Prices[ListPrice])
options.explanation: RELATED needs an existing relationship between the tables.

questions.stem:
An Employees table has a Skills column that contains values such as SQL;DAX;M in a single cell. You need a table that has one row per employee and skill, with the other columns repeated.
What should you do?

options.text: Split the column by delimiter (semicolon) and choose to split into rows
options.explanation: Splitting by delimiter into rows creates a new row for each skill and repeats the other column values.

options.text: Unpivot the Skills column
options.explanation: Unpivot works on multiple columns. The skills are in a single column.

options.text: Use Extract > Text Before Delimiter
options.explanation: Text Before Delimiter returns only the first skill and discards the rest.

options.text: Split the column by delimiter (semicolon) and choose to split into columns
options.explanation: Splitting into columns creates Skills.1, Skills.2, and so on, which keeps all skills in one row.

questions.stem:
A Contacts table contains the email addresses Anna@Contoso.com and anna@contoso.com for the same person. When you apply Remove Duplicates to the Email column, both rows remain.
You need to remove duplicate contacts regardless of letter case.
What should you do?

options.text: Apply Trim to the Email column and then Remove Duplicates.
options.explanation: Trim removes spaces, not differences in letter case.

options.text: Change the data type of the Email column to Any, and then remove duplicates
options.explanation: The Any data type does not change the case-sensitive comparison.

options.text: Apply Remove Duplicates twice, and then sort the Email column
options.explanation: Running the command twice does not change how comparisons are made.

options.text: Convert the Email column to lowercase and then apply Remove Duplicates.
options.explanation: Remove Duplicates compares values case-sensitively, so you must standardize the case first. Lowercasing makes both values identical.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
You administer a workspace for the finance department, whose 40 staff change often. You want to manage who has access to the workspace with the least effort.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a workspace for each user and copy the reports to every workspace
options.explanation: Creating a workspace for each user is not a manageable design.

options.text: Assign a Microsoft Entra security group to the workspace role and maintain the group
options.explanation: Assigning a group to a role applies the role to all of its members, and changes in the group are picked up without changing the workspace.

options.text: Share each report individually with each of the users in the department
options.explanation: Sharing each item with each person is the most laborious option.

options.text: Add each of the 40 users individually to the workspace and remove them one by one
options.explanation: Individual assignments require updating the workspace for each joiner and leaver.

questions.stem:
A column chart shows Total Sales values such as 1,250,000. The data labels are too long. You need them to display 1.25M without changing the data in the model.
What should you configure?

options.text: The display units of the data labels, set to Millions
options.explanation: Display units change how numbers are shown, for example in thousands or millions, and the underlying data is not changed.

options.text: The Summarize by property of the column in the model
options.explanation: Summarize by controls how a column is aggregated, not how a value is displayed.

options.text: The data type of the column, set to Text in Power Query
options.explanation: Converting to text would change the data and stop it from being summed.

options.text: The sort order of the visual, set to descending
options.explanation: Sort order changes the order of the categories.

questions.stem:
The Customer table has a numeric Age column. You need a column chart that shows the number of customers in each 10-year age range.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a calculated column that returns the average age of the customers
options.explanation: An average age is a single value, and it does not create age ranges.

options.text: Create a Bin group on Age with a bin size of 10, use the bin on the axis, and count customers
options.explanation: A bin groups numeric values into ranges of the size that you set. Used on the axis with a count of customers, it shows the distribution.

options.text: Create a new group on the Age column of the type List, and select all ages in the list
options.explanation: A list group combines specific values in named groups, so every 10-year range would have to be defined manually.

options.text: Change the summarization of Age to Average and use Age on the axis of the chart
options.explanation: The summarization of Age changes how the values are aggregated, and it does not create ranges.

questions.stem:
A Country column contains the values US, USA, Australia, and Russia. You want to replace only the exact value US with United States. When you try Replace Values with US and United States, the value USA changes to United StatesA.
What should you do?

options.text: Replace the value again and select Match entire cell contents.
options.explanation: Match entire cell contents limits the replacement to cells whose whole value equals US, so USA remains unchanged.

options.text: Use the Clean transformation on the column before replacing
options.explanation: Clean removes non-printable characters, and it does not replace values.

options.text: Replace the value by using Replace Errors on the column
options.explanation: Replace Errors substitutes error cells only. These cells do not contain errors.

options.text: Convert the column to Uppercase and replace the value again
options.explanation: Uppercasing does not stop partial matches. Values such as USA would still be changed.

questions.stem:
A page filter selects March 1 to March 10, 2025. You need a measure that returns the sales of the entire month of March 2024.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR returns the same days one year earlier (March 1 to March 10, 2024).

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], PREVIOUSYEAR('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: PREVIOUSYEAR returns all of 2024 and not only March.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATEADD('Date'[Date], -1, YEAR))
options.explanation: DATEADD also shifts the same set of days, so the result is March 1 to March 10, 2024.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], PARALLELPERIOD('Date'[Date], -12, MONTH))
options.explanation: PARALLELPERIOD shifts the selected dates and fills partial months out to complete months, so a selection of 10 days returns the complete month 12 months earlier.

questions.stem:
A 100-million-row fact table uses a text GUID column as the key to a dimension table. Refresh is slow, the model is large, and relationships are slow.
What should you do?

options.text: Hide the GUID column in Report view so that it is not stored
options.explanation: Hiding a column does not reduce the memory that it uses.

options.text: Replace the GUID with an integer surrogate key in both tables.
options.explanation: Integer keys have fewer bytes and compress better than long text values, which reduces the model size and speeds up relationship lookups.

options.text: Change the relationship to many-to-many to avoid the key comparison
options.explanation: Many-to-many relationships are generally slower.

options.text: Change the data type of the GUID column to Any in Power Query
options.explanation: The Any type does not change how the values are stored in the model.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You want a role to hide all but the West region from users, and the Region slicer on reports must list only the West region as well. The model has a Region dimension table with a one-to-many single-direction relationship to the Sales fact table.
On which table should the role filter be defined?

options.text: The Sales table, with the filter [Region] = "West"
options.explanation: A filter on the Sales table restricts the fact rows, but with a single-direction relationship it does not filter the Region table, so the slicer would still list all regions.

options.text: The Region table, with the filter [Region] = "West"
options.explanation: A filter on the dimension table limits the dimension rows, and it then filters the fact table through the relationship, so the slicer and the sales both show only West.

options.text: The Date table, with the filter [Region] = "West"
options.explanation: The Date table has no Region column and is not related in a way that would filter the regions.

options.text: No table, because the relationship will apply the filter automatically
options.explanation: A role needs an explicit DAX filter. Relationships only propagate it.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You are writing a measure that uses variables (VAR and RETURN).
Which two statements about DAX variables are true? Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: A variable can be redefined after the RETURN keyword.
options.explanation: Variables are defined before RETURN, and they cannot be redefined after it.

options.text: A variable can store only scalar values.
options.explanation: Variables can hold tables as well as scalar values.

options.text: A variable is evaluated once, and the result is reused wherever the variable is referenced.
options.explanation: A variable is calculated once, which can improve performance when the same expression is needed several times.

options.text: A variable is evaluated in the filter context where it is defined, not where it is used.
options.explanation: The value of a variable is determined in the context in which the variable is defined. Later changes to the filter context, for example by CALCULATE, do not change it.

options.text: A variable is evaluated every time that it is referenced.
options.explanation: This is the behavior of a repeated expression and not of a variable. A variable is not recalculated at each reference.

questions.stem:
A model has two calculation groups: Time Intelligence and Currency Conversion. Both apply to the same measure, and the order in which they are evaluated matters for the result.
Which calculation group property controls this order?

options.text: Format string expression
options.explanation: The format string expression changes how results are formatted, not the order of evaluation.

options.text: Ordinal
options.explanation: Ordinal controls the display order of the items inside a calculation group.

options.text: Name
options.explanation: The name identifies the calculation group and has no effect on evaluation.

options.text: Precedence
options.explanation: Precedence defines the order in which multiple calculation groups are applied to a measure. The group that has the higher value is evaluated first.

questions.stem: A matrix has two measures in the Values area. They appear as side-by-side columns under each year. You need the measures to appear as rows under each product instead, and the years to remain as columns. What should you configure?

options.text: The Row subtotals option for the matrix visual
options.explanation: Row subtotals turn the subtotals of row groups on or off.

options.text: The Show on rows option for the values
options.explanation: Show on rows moves the measures from the column headers to the rows of the matrix.

options.text: The Repeat row headers option for the row fields
options.explanation: Repeat row headers repeats the labels of the row headers in each row.

options.text: The Stepped layout option for the rows of the matrix
options.explanation: Stepped layout controls how row hierarchy levels are indented.

questions.stem: You create an aggregation table named SalesAgg that has the columns ProductKey, MonthKey, and SalesAmount. In the Manage aggregations dialog, you map the columns to the detail table named Sales. Which summarization should you select for the ProductKey and MonthKey columns?

options.text: Sum
options.explanation: Sum is used for numeric measure columns such as SalesAmount, not for key columns.

options.text: GroupBy
options.explanation: ProductKey and MonthKey define the grain of the aggregation, so they are mapped with the GroupBy summarization.

options.text: Max
options.explanation: Max is used for columns that store a maximum value.

options.text: Count
options.explanation: Count is used when the aggregation column stores the number of non-blank values of a detail column.

questions.stem:
You build a composite model. A large Sales fact table uses DirectQuery. Several small dimension tables (Product, Customer, Date) are used for slicers and are related to Sales.
You need to improve query performance for visuals that filter Sales by using the dimension tables. Which storage mode should you configure for the dimension tables?

options.text: Live
options.explanation: Live is a connection type, not a storage mode that can be set on a table.

options.text: DirectQuery
options.explanation: DirectQuery dimensions would query the source for slicer values, which adds load and slows the slicers.

options.text: Import
options.explanation: Import dimensions are in a different source group from the DirectQuery fact table, which produces limited relationships and weaker performance for those queries.

options.text: Dual
options.explanation: A Dual table can be served from the in-memory cache or pushed to the source, so queries that join it to the DirectQuery fact table avoid limited relationships and perform better.

questions.stem:
A line chart shows monthly Total Sales. Sales dropped sharply in March, and an analyst wants Power BI to suggest the factors that contributed to the decrease.
What should the analyst do?

options.text: Select the March data point, and then select Drill through to another page of the report
options.explanation: Drillthrough sends the filter of the data point to another page, and it does not analyze causes.

options.text: Right-click the March data point, and then select Analyze and Explain the decrease.
options.explanation: The Analyze feature runs a statistical analysis on a data point and shows visuals with factors that explain a change in the value.

options.text: Add a trend line to the visual to show the direction of the sales
options.explanation: A trend line shows the direction of the data, and it does not explain a specific drop.

options.text: Add a decomposition tree to the page, and select March in the tree
options.explanation: A decomposition tree would need to be configured by the analyst, and it does not analyze the change between two points automatically.

questions.reference: Analyze feature: Explain the increase and decrease

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX

options.text: The total sales of all products
options.explanation: The measure applies a filter on Color, so it does not return the total across all colors.

options.text: The total sales of Blue products
options.explanation: The Blue selection is replaced by the filter in CALCULATE, so it does not determine the result.

options.text: The total sales of products that are both Red and Blue, which is blank
options.explanation: A blank result would occur if the filters were intersected, for example by using KEEPFILTERS. A plain Boolean filter does not intersect.

options.text: The total sales of Red products
options.explanation: A Boolean filter in CALCULATE replaces any existing filter on the same column. The Blue selection is overridden, so the measure returns the sales of Red products.

questions.stem:
You need to show only the customers whose name contains the word Corp.
Which filter should you use in the Filters pane?

options.text: Advanced filtering on the Customer Name field with the condition contains
options.explanation: Advanced filtering for text fields supports conditions such as contains, starts with, and is.

options.text: Basic filtering on the Customer Name field with the select all option
options.explanation: Basic filtering lists values to select, and it does not apply a text pattern condition.

options.text: Relative date filtering on the Customer Name field for the last year
options.explanation: Relative date filters apply to date fields and not to text fields.

options.text: Top N filtering on the Customer Name field by the number of orders
options.explanation: Top N keeps the highest or lowest items by a measure, and it does not match text.

questions.reference: Types of filters in Power BI reports

questions.stem:
A single query named Sales loads a flat table that contains order data and product attributes (ProductID, ProductName, Category). You are building a star schema and need a Product dimension.
Changes that you later make to the cleaning steps in the Sales query must automatically apply to the Product dimension. You do not want to repeat those steps.
What should you do?

options.text: Copy the M code of the Sales query into a new blank query and edit the copy
options.explanation: A copy of the M code is also an independent set of steps, so it has the same disadvantage as a duplicate.

options.text: Duplicate the Sales query, keep the product columns, and then remove the duplicate rows
options.explanation: A duplicate copies the steps, so later edits to Sales do not update the copy.

options.text: Create a calculated table that uses DISTINCT over the product columns in DAX
options.explanation: A DAX calculated table is built after the data is loaded and does not reuse the Power Query steps.

options.text: Reference the Sales query, keep the product columns, and remove duplicates
options.explanation: A reference query starts from the output of the original query. Edits to the original query's earlier steps flow into the referenced query.

questions.stem:
A REST API returns 100 records per page. A query that has a Page parameter returns the first page. You need all 20 pages in a single table.
What should you do?

options.text: Convert the query to a function that takes the page number, and invoke it for the numbers 1 to 20
options.explanation: A function that accepts the page number can be invoked for each item in a list of page numbers, and the results are expanded into one table. It is easy to extend.

options.text: Duplicate the query 20 times, edit the page number in each copy, and append all of the copies together
options.explanation: Duplicating 20 queries would work but is hard to maintain, and every change must be repeated 20 times.

options.text: Change the query to DirectQuery so that the pages are read on demand
options.explanation: DirectQuery is not available for a REST API source and does not change how pages are retrieved.

options.text: Pivot the Page column of the first page, and then expand the pages
options.explanation: Pivoting does not retrieve additional pages from the API.

questions.stem:
A scatter chart shows Advertising Spend on the X axis and Revenue on the Y axis for 200 campaigns. You need to show whether the two values have a linear relationship.
What should you add?

options.text: A ribbon chart
options.explanation: A ribbon chart is a different chart type that shows the rank over time.

options.text: A constant line at the average of Revenue
options.explanation: A constant line shows one fixed level and not a relationship between the two axes.

options.text: A KPI visual
options.explanation: A KPI visual compares one value with a target and has no axes.

options.text: A trend line from the Analytics pane
options.explanation: A trend line is a regression line that shows the overall direction and the strength of the relationship between the values.

questions.stem:
You append a query named Online to a query named Store. The Online query has a column named CustomerName. The Store query has a column named Customername. After the append, the result contains both columns, and each has null values for the rows from the other query.
What should you do?

options.text: Merge the queries instead of appending them, joining on OrderID
