options.explanation: A merge adds columns from a second table to matching rows and does not stack rows.

options.text: Use Fill Down on both columns after the append is complete
options.explanation: Fill Down would copy values between unrelated rows and would produce wrong data.

options.text: Rename the columns so the names match exactly, and then append
options.explanation: Append matches columns by name, and the match is case-sensitive. Making the names identical puts the values in a single column.

options.text: Change the data type of both columns to Text before the append
options.explanation: Data types do not affect which columns are matched.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A report in a workspace app is based on a semantic model that has RLS roles. Employees get the report only through the app, and they are members of the RLS roles.
How does RLS affect these employees?

options.text: The roles are applied only if the app has a separate audience for each role
options.explanation: Audiences control content visibility in the app and are not required for RLS.

options.text: The roles are ignored, because content that is consumed through apps bypasses the RLS roles
options.explanation: Apps do not bypass RLS. The restrictions of the model stay in effect.

options.text: The roles are applied, because the employees consume the content without edit permissions
options.explanation: Users who consume content, for example through an app, are not workspace editors, and RLS is enforced for the roles they belong to.

options.text: The roles are applied only if the semantic model uses DirectQuery.
options.explanation: RLS works with Import and with DirectQuery.

questions.stem:
A central BI team publishes a certified semantic model. You create a report in Power BI Desktop connected to it through a live connection. You need a measure that exists only in your report and must not change the shared model.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a calculated table to the semantic model.
options.explanation: Calculated tables are part of the model definition, which you cannot edit through a live connection.

options.text: Create a calculated column in the semantic model.
options.explanation: A live connection does not let you modify the model by adding calculated columns.

options.text: Add a Power Query step that computes the value.
options.explanation: Power Query is unavailable over a live connection, and it would not change the shared model anyway.

options.text: Create a report-level measure.
options.explanation: Report-level measures are stored in your report and can reference the shared model's fields. The shared model is unchanged.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A workspace is assigned to Premium Per User capacity. A colleague has a Power BI Pro license, but no Premium Per User license.
What can the colleague do with the content in the workspace?

options.text: Edit the content, because a Pro license gives edit access in all workspaces
options.explanation: Edit access is granted by the workspace role, and the license requirement for the workspace still applies.

options.text: Nothing, because users need a Premium Per User license to access content in that workspace
options.explanation: Content in a Premium Per User workspace can be consumed only by users who also have a Premium Per User license.

options.text: View the content only through the email subscriptions of the workspace
options.explanation: A subscription does not give a user without the proper license access to the content.

options.text: View the content, because a Pro license is sufficient for any workspace
options.explanation: A Pro license is not sufficient for content in a Premium Per User workspace.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the year selected in a slicer on Date[Year] when exactly one year is selected, and the text Multiple years in all other cases.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: HASONEVALUE('Date'[Year])
options.explanation: HASONEVALUE returns TRUE or FALSE and not the year or the text.

options.text: SELECTEDVALUE('Date'[Year], "Multiple years")
options.explanation: SELECTEDVALUE returns the value when exactly one value is in the filter context, and otherwise returns the alternate result that you specify.

options.text: MAX('Date'[Year])
options.explanation: MAX returns the highest selected year and never returns the text Multiple years.

options.text: VALUES('Date'[Year])
options.explanation: VALUES returns a table, and it causes an error in a measure when more than one year is selected.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A report contains confidential detail data. You need to make sure that users can export from the report only the summarized data that is shown in a visual, and not the underlying data.
What should you do?

options.text: Set the export data option of the report to summarized data only
options.explanation: The report's export setting can allow summarized data only, allow summarized and underlying data, or block data export.

options.text: Turn off personalized visuals for the report in the report settings
options.explanation: Personalized visuals lets users change a visual and has no effect on export permissions.

options.text: Hide the Filters pane so that users cannot see the filtered data
options.explanation: The Filters pane controls filtering and does not influence export.

options.text: Remove the Export option from the Power BI mobile app only
options.explanation: The mobile app is only one of the ways to view the report, and the setting does not control data export from other places.

questions.stem:
You develop a report that uses 12 queries against a SQL Server database. The report is deployed to development, test, and production environments, and each environment uses a different server name. You need to change the server name without editing each query.
What should you create?

options.text: A Power Query parameter that is used in the Source step of each query
options.explanation: A Power Query parameter can supply the server name to the Source step of every query. Changing the parameter value repoints all the queries at once.

options.text: A field parameter that lets users switch between the server names in a slicer
options.explanation: A field parameter lets report users switch the fields shown in a visual. It does not affect the data source.

options.text: A calculated table that stores the server names for each environment
options.explanation: A calculated table is evaluated after data is loaded, so it cannot supply a server name to a query that loads the data.

options.text: A what-if parameter that holds the list of the server names
options.explanation: A what-if parameter creates a DAX table and measure that let report users test scenarios. It cannot control data source connections.

questions.stem:
You add a forecast to a line chart that shows monthly Total Sales for the last four years. The sales have a strong yearly seasonal pattern.
Which two settings can you configure for the forecast? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Sensitivity of anomalies
options.explanation: Sensitivity is a setting of anomaly detection, not of a forecast.

options.text: Confidence interval
options.explanation: The confidence interval sets the width of the shaded band around the forecast.

options.text: A DAX expression for the forecast
options.explanation: A forecast is configured in the Analytics pane and does not use DAX.

options.text: Forecasting algorithm, such as ARIMA
options.explanation: The algorithm is selected by Power BI, and it is not a setting of the forecast.

options.text: Seasonality
options.explanation: Seasonality sets the number of points in a repeating cycle, such as 12 for monthly data with a yearly pattern.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem: A Products-to-Sales relationship has a single cross-filter direction. A slicer that uses Sales[Region] must reduce the items shown in a Product slicer to the products that were sold in the selected region. Which relationship setting should you change?

options.text: Enable Assume referential integrity.
options.explanation: Assume referential integrity affects how DirectQuery generates joins and does not change filter direction.

options.text: Make the relationship inactive.
options.explanation: An inactive relationship propagates no filters.

options.text: Set the cross-filter direction to Both.
options.explanation: With single direction, filters flow from Products to Sales. A bidirectional filter also lets Sales filter Products, so the Product slicer shows only related products.

options.text: Set the cardinality to One to one.
options.explanation: Cardinality does not control filter propagation in this way, and Products to Sales is a one-to-many relationship.

questions.stem: Power BI Desktop runs with English (United States) regional settings. A CSV file stores dates as text in the format 31/12/2025 (day/month/year). When you change the column type to Date, many rows show errors. What should you do?

options.text: Change the type by using Locale, and select English (United Kingdom)
options.explanation: Using Locale tells Power Query how to interpret the text. The day-first format of the UK locale interprets 31/12/2025 correctly.

options.text: Enable Auto date/time in the data load options of the current file
options.explanation: Auto date/time creates hidden date tables in the model. It does not fix parsing errors in Power Query.

options.text: Replace the / character with - and then change the type to Date.
options.explanation: Replacing the separator does not change the order of day and month that the US locale expects.

options.text: Change the type to Text first, and then change the type to Date
options.explanation: Converting to Text keeps the same text, and the second conversion fails in the same way because the US locale still expects month first.

questions.reference: Change data type by using locale

questions.stem: The Inventory table stores a stock snapshot only on some days. You need a monthly measure that returns the latest snapshot that exists in each month, even if the last day of the month has no snapshot. Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Inventory[Units]), DATESMTD('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: DATESMTD returns the dates from the start of the month, so the measure sums all snapshots of the month.

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Inventory[Units]), FIRSTNONBLANK('Date'[Date], CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Inventory))))
options.explanation: FIRSTNONBLANK returns the earliest snapshot of the month, which is the opening balance.

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Inventory[Units]), LASTDATE('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: LASTDATE returns the last calendar date of the month, and it returns a blank value if no snapshot exists on that day.

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Inventory[Units]), LASTNONBLANK('Date'[Date], CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Inventory))))
options.explanation: LASTNONBLANK returns the last date on which the expression is not blank, so it finds the latest day that has a snapshot.

questions.stem:
You need to merge a Sales query with a Targets query. A sales row matches a target row only if both Year and Region are equal.
What should you do in the Merge Queries dialog?

options.text: Select Year and Region in the same order in both tables, and then choose the join kind.
options.explanation: You can select several columns in each table. Power Query matches the columns in the order that you select them, so both columns must be selected in the same order.

options.text: Select only the Year columns, and then filter by Region after the merge
options.explanation: Merging on Year only creates extra matches across regions that you would need to remove, and it is more error-prone.

options.text: Select Region in the first table and Year in the second table, and then choose the join kind
options.explanation: Matching Region to Year compares unrelated columns and returns no useful matches.

options.text: Merge twice, first on Year and then on Region, and append the results.
options.explanation: Two separate merges and an append would not produce a single match on both columns.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You need to implement row-level security so that each regional manager sees only the data of their region, with the least administrative effort when assignments change.
What should you do?

options.text: Create one dynamic role that filters SecurityMap by USERPRINCIPALNAME() and flows to the sales data
options.explanation: A single dynamic role driven by the SecurityMap table needs no change when assignments change. The table is updated, and the role follows it.

options.text: Create a static role for each region, and add the managers to those roles in the service
options.explanation: Static roles work, but every change of assignment requires someone to change the membership of the roles.

options.text: Create a calculated column that contains the region of each manager, and filter the visuals by it.
options.explanation: A calculated column is evaluated at refresh and cannot depend on the user who views the report. Filtering visuals is also not a security feature.

options.text: Filter the data in Power Query by using the account of the person who refreshes the semantic model.
options.explanation: Power Query runs at refresh time with the identity of the refresh, not the identity of the viewer, so it cannot filter per viewer.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You need to make sure that the semantic model refreshes four times a day.
What should you do?

options.text: Change the semantic model to Direct Lake storage mode in Power BI Desktop
options.explanation: Direct Lake does not apply to an on-premises SQL Server data source.

options.text: Install an on-premises data gateway, set the credentials, and schedule four refreshes
options.explanation: The source is on-premises, so a gateway is required. With the credentials set, up to eight scheduled refreshes per day are available in a Pro workspace.

options.text: Configure a data alert on the dashboard that shows the sales data
options.explanation: A data alert notifies users about values and does not refresh data.

options.text: Ask each author to refresh the file in Power BI Desktop and publish it four times a day.
options.explanation: A manual process is error-prone and does not meet the requirement of an automatic refresh.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
You need to distribute the content to the 600 employees. Only executives may see the Executive Summary page.
What should you do?

options.text: Add all the employees as Viewers of the Sales Analytics workspace, and hide the Executive Summary page.
options.explanation: Hiding a page does not secure it, and workspace Viewers would see the in-progress content of the workspace.

options.text: Email the PBIX file to all employees every time that it changes
options.explanation: A PBIX file would copy the data to each employee and would not be refreshed or secured.

options.text: Publish a workspace app with two audiences, and give only Executives the Executive Summary page
options.explanation: An app with audiences lets one app serve different groups, and the content that each audience sees is controlled.

options.text: Publish the report to the web and share the link with the employees
options.explanation: Publish to web makes the report public and violates the confidentiality of the data.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem: You need to make sure that only the data governance team can certify the Sales semantic model. What should the Power BI administrator do?

options.text: Assign the data governance team the Admin role in the Sales Analytics workspace
options.explanation: A workspace role does not give the right to certify. The right comes from the tenant setting.

options.text: Give the data governance team the Build permission on the Sales semantic model
options.explanation: Build permission allows users to create content from the semantic model, and it is not related to certification.

options.text: In the tenant settings, enable certification and specify the data governance group
options.explanation: The tenant setting for certification lets the administrator limit certification to specific security groups.

options.text: Ask the data governance team to promote the semantic model in the workspace
options.explanation: Promotion can be done by any content owner and does not mark the model as certified.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
You need to make sure that new reports that authors create in the service from the Sales semantic model are classified as Confidential, without the authors having to apply the label each time.
What should you do?

options.text: Add the text Confidential to the title of every report that the authors create
options.explanation: A title is only text. It does not classify content or apply protection.

options.text: Apply the Confidential label to the semantic model, and enable downstream label inheritance
options.explanation: When a label is applied to a semantic model, and the setting for downstream inheritance is enabled, new content created from it inherits the label.

options.text: Remove the Build permission from the authors on the Sales semantic model
options.explanation: Removing Build permission would stop authors from creating reports from the model, which breaks the requirement.

options.text: Add a watermark to the report theme that all of the authors must use
options.explanation: A watermark does not apply a sensitivity label.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
Your model has the tables A, B, and C. Active one-to-many relationships exist from A to B and from B to C. You now create a relationship from A to C.
What does Power BI Desktop do with the new relationship?

options.text: It creates the new relationship as inactive, because two active paths would be ambiguous
options.explanation: Power BI does not allow ambiguous active paths between two tables. The new relationship is inactive and can be used with USERELATIONSHIP.

options.text: It converts the new relationship to a many-to-many relationship automatically
options.explanation: The cardinality is determined by the columns and is not changed to resolve ambiguity.

options.text: It creates the relationship as active, and deactivates the relationship from B to C.
options.explanation: Existing relationships are not changed automatically.

options.text: It creates the relationship as active, and both paths are evaluated and their results are added.
options.explanation: Filters do not travel along two paths and add their results. Ambiguity is avoided by keeping only one active path.

questions.stem:
Senior management wants to track company goals such as Revenue, Customer Satisfaction, and Employee Turnover. Each goal must have an owner, a current value, a target, a status, and check-ins that record progress over time.
What should you create in the Power BI service?

options.text: A paginated report
options.explanation: A paginated report is a printable document, and it does not track goals over time.

options.text: A scorecard that contains metrics
options.explanation: A scorecard is designed to track metrics with owners, current value, target, status, and check-ins.

options.text: A Power BI Desktop theme
options.explanation: A theme controls colors and fonts.

options.text: A dashboard that contains KPI tiles
options.explanation: Dashboard tiles show values but do not track owners, targets, status rules, and check-ins as a goal.

questions.stem:
You need a single slicer in which users can select a product category or expand it to select individual subcategories.
What should you do?

options.text: Add a Category slicer and enable cross-highlighting.
options.explanation: Cross-highlighting affects how visuals react to selections and does not create subcategories in the slicer.

options.text: Add a matrix visual that has both fields.
options.explanation: A matrix is not a slicer.

options.text: Add the Category and Subcategory fields to the same slicer.
options.explanation: A slicer that has several fields displays them as a hierarchy that users can expand and collapse.

options.text: Add two slicers, one for Category and one for Subcategory, and sync them
options.explanation: Two slicers are two separate objects, and syncing them shares selections across pages and does not create a hierarchy.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem: The owner of a semantic model built for the marketing team wants colleagues in other departments to find it more easily and to see that the owner recommends it. No formal review of the model is required. Which endorsement should the owner apply?

options.text: Sensitivity label
options.explanation: A sensitivity label classifies and protects content and does not make it more discoverable.

options.text: Master data
options.explanation: Master data is for a single source of truth for a type of data, and it is a different endorsement than a recommendation by an owner.

options.text: Certified
options.explanation: Certification requires an authorized reviewer who is designated by the administrator, and a formal review is not available here.

options.text: Promoted
options.explanation: Promotion lets content owners and users who have write permission highlight content that they consider ready to share, without a formal review.

questions.stem:
A table visual lists the column UnitPrice, and it shows Sum of UnitPrice for each row, which is the same as the original price. You need each row to show its own price without an aggregation label.
What should you do?

options.text: Hide the column in the report view and use it as a filter
options.explanation: Hiding the column removes it from the Fields pane, and it does not change how the visual shows it.

options.text: Create a hierarchy that contains UnitPrice and use the hierarchy
options.explanation: A hierarchy does not change aggregation behavior.

options.text: Change the field in the visual's well to Don't summarize
options.explanation: Selecting Don't summarize shows the raw value for each row instead of an aggregate.

options.text: Change the data type of the column to Text in the model
options.explanation: Text values would no longer be numeric, so the column could not be used in calculations.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the number of customers who purchased in 2024 but did not purchase in 2025.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: COUNTROWS(EXCEPT(CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2024), CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2025)))
options.explanation: EXCEPT returns the rows of the first table that do not appear in the second table, so it returns the customers of 2024 who are not in 2025.

options.text: COUNTROWS(INTERSECT(CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2024), CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2025)))
options.explanation: INTERSECT returns customers who purchased in both years.

options.text: COUNTROWS(EXCEPT(CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2025), CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2024)))
options.explanation: The tables are in the wrong order. This returns customers who purchased in 2025 but not in 2024.

options.text: COUNTROWS(UNION(CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2024), CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(Sales[CustomerKey]), 'Date'[Year] = 2025)))
options.explanation: UNION returns customers who purchased in either year.

questions.stem:
You need to show monthly Total Sales as columns and Profit Margin % as a line. The percentage values are much smaller than the sales values, so they must use a separate axis.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Scatter chart
options.explanation: A scatter chart plots two numeric axes and does not combine columns and a line over time.

options.text: Line and clustered column chart
options.explanation: The line and clustered column chart combines columns and a line, and it supports a secondary axis for the line values.

options.text: Stacked area chart
options.explanation: A stacked area chart stacks series on the same axis, which would make the percentage unreadable.

options.text: Clustered column chart
options.explanation: A clustered column chart has only columns and a single value axis.

questions.stem: An Excel workbook is stored in a SharePoint Online document library. You need to import a single workbook from it so that scheduled refresh in the Power BI service works without a data gateway. Which connector should you use?

options.text: Web, by using the file URL
options.explanation: Using the Web connector with the file's SharePoint URL treats the workbook as a cloud source, so the service can refresh it without a gateway.

options.text: Folder, by using a mapped network drive
options.explanation: A folder on a mapped network drive is also an on-premises path that requires a gateway.

options.text: SharePoint Online list
options.explanation: The SharePoint Online list connector reads list data, not workbooks stored in a document library.

options.text: Excel workbook, by using a locally synced file path
options.explanation: A local file path is not reachable by the service without an on-premises data gateway.

questions.reference: Get data from files in SharePoint Online

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A company has 600 salespeople. Each salesperson must see only the sales of their own accounts. A table named SalesRep has a column named Email with the sign-in address of each salesperson. You must avoid creating a separate role for each salesperson.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a calculated column named IsMine in the Sales table.
options.explanation: A calculated column is evaluated at refresh time and cannot know who views the report.

options.text: Create one role with the filter SalesRep[Email] = "ALL".
options.explanation: A fixed text value does not depend on who is signed in.

options.text: Create one role that filters SalesRep[Email] by USERPRINCIPALNAME()
options.explanation: USERPRINCIPALNAME() returns the sign-in name of the current user, so a single role with a dynamic filter shows each user only the rows that match their email.

options.text: Create 600 roles that each have a hard-coded email address.
options.explanation: This works but creates a role for each person and is very difficult to maintain.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns each product's share of the total sales of all products. The denominator must ignore every filter that is applied to the Products table.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: DIVIDE([Total Sales], [Total Sales])
options.explanation: Dividing a value by itself always returns 1.

options.text: DIVIDE([Total Sales], CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL(Products)))
options.explanation: ALL(Products) removes all filters on the Products table, so the denominator is the total for all products.

options.text: DIVIDE([Total Sales], CALCULATE([Total Sales], VALUES(Products)))
options.explanation: VALUES(Products) returns the products that are currently visible and keeps the existing filters, so the denominator equals the numerator in each row.

options.text: DIVIDE([Total Sales], CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALLSELECTED(Products)))
options.explanation: ALLSELECTED keeps filters that come from outside the visual, such as slicers on Products, so the denominator would not ignore every filter on the table.

questions.stem:
You formatted a chart with a specific font, title style, and border. You need to apply the same formatting to ten other visuals on the page quickly.
What should you use?

options.text: Format painter
options.explanation: Format painter copies the formatting of one visual and applies it to another visual.

options.text: The Selection pane
options.explanation: The Selection pane controls visibility and order of objects and does not copy formatting.

options.text: A drillthrough page
options.explanation: A drillthrough page is a navigation feature.

options.text: A bookmark
options.explanation: A bookmark saves the state of a page, such as filters and visibility, and does not copy visual formatting.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A new analyst wants to build a report from a semantic model that already exists in the organization and that has been certified, instead of importing the source data again.
What should the analyst do in Power BI Desktop?

options.text: Open the semantic model in Power Query and export it to CSV
options.explanation: A semantic model in the service cannot be edited in Power Query that way, and a CSV export would be a static copy.

options.text: Connect to the original source of the data and import it into a new model
options.explanation: Importing the source again duplicates the data and the logic, and the measures of the certified model would not be reused.

options.text: Connect to the Power BI semantic model from the Get data options
options.explanation: Connecting to the shared Power BI semantic model creates a live connection to it, so the analyst reuses the model, measures, and security.

options.text: Use Analyze in Excel and import the workbook
options.explanation: Analyze in Excel connects Excel to the model, and importing a workbook would create a disconnected copy.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
The Sales table contains ProductKey and CustomerKey columns that are used only for relationships. You want report authors not to see these columns in the Fields pane, but they must remain available in the model for relationships and DAX.
What should you do?

options.text: Rename the columns to start with an underscore.
options.explanation: Renaming only changes the column name, and the columns remain visible.

options.text: Remove the columns in Power Query.
options.explanation: Removing the columns breaks the relationships that depend on them.

options.text: Hide the columns in report view.
options.explanation: Hiding a column in report view removes it from the Fields pane for authors, and the model can still use it.

options.text: Set the data category of the columns to Uncategorized.
options.explanation: Data category does not control visibility.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
Your dynamic RLS role must filter by the email address of the user, and it must work both when you test it in Power BI Desktop and after you publish the model to the service.
Which DAX function should you use to get the user's identity?

options.text: USERNAME
options.explanation: USERNAME returns the domain and user name in the DOMAIN\user format in Power BI Desktop, and it returns the UPN in the service. The inconsistent format could cause the filter to fail in one of the environments.

options.text: CUSTOMDATA
options.explanation: CUSTOMDATA depends on a value that is passed in the connection string in specific embedded and Analysis Services scenarios, and it does not return the signed-in user.

options.text: USEROBJECTID
options.explanation: USEROBJECTID returns the object identifier of the user in Microsoft Entra ID, which is a GUID and not an email address.

options.text: USERPRINCIPALNAME
options.explanation: USERPRINCIPALNAME returns the user principal name, which is the sign-in email, in the same format in Desktop and in the service.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem: Which requirement is best met by creating a calculated table in the model?

options.text: Removing blank rows from a table that is loaded from a CSV file
options.explanation: Removing blank rows is a data preparation step that belongs in Power Query.

options.text: Changing the data type of a column from Text to Date in the loaded table
options.explanation: Changing the data type is done in Power Query or in the column properties, and it does not require a table.

options.text: Creating a date table from the minimum and maximum dates of the Sales table
options.explanation: A calculated table is created with DAX from data that is already in the model, so a date table derived from the dates in Sales is a good fit.

options.text: Unpivoting month columns into rows so that each month becomes a row of the table
options.explanation: Unpivoting is a Power Query transformation.

questions.stem:
A slicer on the Customer Name field contains 5,000 names. Users need to find a customer quickly by typing part of the name, and the slicer must take little space on the page.
What should you do?

options.text: Set the slicer style to Tiles, and enable Search
options.explanation: Tiles would try to display thousands of buttons and take a lot of space.

options.text: Set the slicer style to Dropdown, and enable Search
options.explanation: A dropdown slicer uses little space, and the search box lets users type to find a name.

options.text: Replace the slicer with a card visual that shows the selected customer
options.explanation: A card displays a value and does not filter other visuals.

options.text: Set the slicer style to List, and disable Search so that all names are visible
options.explanation: A list slicer with search disabled forces users to scroll through 5,000 names.

questions.stem: A model uses many bidirectional relationships. Report queries are slow, and Power BI Desktop warns about ambiguous filter paths. Only one measure actually needs to filter from the fact table to a dimension. What should you do?

options.text: Convert the fact table to a calculated table to simplify the paths
options.explanation: Converting the table does not change how filters propagate.

options.text: Change all relationships to many-to-many to remove the ambiguity between the paths
options.explanation: Many-to-many relationships are generally slower and can create further ambiguity.

options.text: Use single-direction relationships, and use CROSSFILTER only in that one measure
options.explanation: Single-direction relationships avoid ambiguity and extra filter propagation. CROSSFILTER enables the opposite direction only where a calculation needs it.

options.text: Add more bidirectional relationships so that every path of filters becomes unambiguous
options.explanation: Adding bidirectional relationships increases ambiguity and the cost of filter propagation.

questions.stem: You import a JSON file, and the Power Query Editor shows a single value named List. Each item in the list is a Record that has the fields Id, Name, and Region. You need a table that has these three columns. What should you do?

options.text: Transpose the list, and then promote the first row to headers
options.explanation: Transposing is for tables. A list must first be converted to a table.

options.text: Convert the list to a table, and then expand the record column
options.explanation: Converting the list into a table gives one row per item. Expanding the Record column then creates a column for each field.

options.text: Pivot the list, and then use the first row as headers
options.explanation: A list cannot be pivoted directly, and pivoting needs attribute and value columns.

options.text: Split the list by delimiter into several columns
options.explanation: A list of records is not delimited text, so splitting by delimiter does not apply.

questions.reference: Work with JSON in Power Query

questions.stem: You import many CSV files in Power BI Desktop. Each time, Desktop automatically adds Changed Type steps that detect wrong data types. You want to stop this behavior for all new files that you import. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off Parallel loading of tables.
options.explanation: Parallel loading controls how tables load, not how types are detected.

options.text: In Options, under the Current File Data Load settings, select Never detect column types and headers for unstructured sources.
options.explanation: The Current File setting changes the behavior only for the open file, not for all new files.

options.text: In Options, under the Global Data Load settings, select Never detect column types and headers for unstructured sources.
options.explanation: The global Data Load setting applies to all files that you create or import in Desktop.

options.text: Turn off Auto date/time for new files.
options.explanation: Auto date/time creates hidden date tables and has no effect on type detection.

questions.reference: Type detection settings in Power BI Desktop

questions.stem:
You inherit a Power BI file that has 40 queries. You need to understand which queries use other queries as their source before you make any changes.
What should you use?

options.text: Query Settings pane
options.explanation: The Query Settings pane lists the applied steps of the selected query only.

options.text: Query Dependencies view
options.explanation: Query Dependencies shows a diagram of how queries and data sources are connected.

options.text: Manage Parameters
options.explanation: Manage Parameters lets you create and edit query parameters.

options.text: Column quality
options.explanation: Column quality shows valid, error, and empty percentages of columns.

questions.stem:
You have 300 supplier names in a purchasing table that contain typing errors, such as Contosso Ltd and Contoso Limted. A master list of correct supplier names exists. You need to map each purchasing row to the correct supplier name.
What should you do?

options.text: Group the purchasing rows by supplier name.
options.explanation: Group By summarizes rows by identical values, so every misspelling would form its own group.

options.text: Merge the queries by using an exact match on the supplier name, and then remove the nulls
options.explanation: An exact match returns no match for the names that contain typing errors.

options.text: Append the master list to the purchasing query.
options.explanation: Append stacks rows from two tables. It does not correct names or add a matching column.

options.text: Merge the purchasing query with the master list by using fuzzy matching.
options.explanation: A fuzzy merge matches values that are similar but not identical, so it can map the misspelled names to the master list.

questions.stem:
A column chart shows Total Sales by Month. An analyst selects the column for March and wants to inspect the individual order rows that make up that value in the model.
What should the analyst do?

options.text: Right-click the March column, and then select See records.
options.explanation: See records shows the detailed rows of the underlying data for the selected data point.

options.text: Right-click the March column, and then select Show as a table.
options.explanation: Show as a table displays the data behind the visual as aggregated values in a table, not individual order rows.

options.text: Right-click the March column, and then select Summarize.
options.explanation: Summarize generates a narrative summary of the visual.

options.text: Right-click the March column, and then select Include.
options.explanation: Include and Exclude change which data points the visual keeps, and they do not display the underlying rows.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the profit margin. The measure must return 0 when the denominator is zero, and it must follow DAX best practices.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: IF([Sales] = 0, 0, [Profit] / [Sales])
options.explanation: This formula works, but DIVIDE is the recommended function because it is shorter and optimized for this case.

options.text: [Profit] / [Sales]
options.explanation: The division operator returns an error or infinity value when the denominator is zero.

options.text: DIVIDE([Profit], [Sales])
options.explanation: Without the third argument, DIVIDE returns a blank value when the denominator is zero.

options.text: DIVIDE([Profit], [Sales], 0)
options.explanation: DIVIDE handles division by zero and returns the alternate result that is given as the third argument, in this case 0.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem: An analyst has built a report in My workspace and wants to distribute it to 50 colleagues as an app. What should the analyst do first?

options.text: Request the Premium Per User license for each colleague.
options.explanation: Licenses are not the missing piece. The content must first be in a workspace that can publish an app.

options.text: Create a new workspace and publish the report to it.
options.explanation: Apps are published from workspaces. My workspace is a personal area and cannot be used to publish an app.

options.text: Create an app directly in My workspace.
options.explanation: An app cannot be created in My workspace.

options.text: Export the report to PDF.
options.explanation: A PDF is a static copy. It does not give the colleagues an interactive report.

questions.stem:
Your company stores 1.2 billion rows of sales transactions in an Azure SQL database. Executives require dashboards that show data that is only a few seconds old.
The solution must NOT rely on scheduled refreshes of the semantic model and must NOT copy the transaction data into the model.
Which storage mode should you use for the Sales fact table?

options.text: Dual
options.explanation: A Dual table can behave as Import or DirectQuery depending on the query, but it still caches a copy of the data and needs refreshes. It is meant for dimension tables in composite models.

options.text: Import with incremental refresh
options.explanation: Incremental refresh reduces refresh time, but the data is still imported and only as fresh as the latest scheduled refresh.

options.text: Import
options.explanation: Import copies the data into the in-memory model, so the data is only as fresh as the last refresh.

options.text: DirectQuery
options.explanation: DirectQuery sends queries to the source every time a visual renders, so no data is copied and no refresh schedule is needed for the data itself.

questions.reference: Storage modes in Power BI Desktop (Import, DirectQuery, Dual)

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem:
A matrix shows product categories on the rows. Users also apply a slicer on the Date table. You need a measure that returns each category's share of the total of the categories that are currently selected in the visual and filtered by the slicers.
Which denominator should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALLEXCEPT(Products, Products[Category]))
options.explanation: ALLEXCEPT on Category keeps the category filter, so the result is the category's own total.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL(Date))
options.explanation: ALL(Date) removes the date slicer selection and leaves the category row filter in place, so each row would be divided by its own category total across all dates.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL(Products[Category]))
options.explanation: ALL on Category ignores outside selections on the category as well, so shares are calculated against all categories rather than the selected ones.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALLSELECTED(Products[Category]))
options.explanation: ALLSELECTED removes the filter that comes from the matrix rows but keeps the filters from slicers and other outer selections, so the denominator is the visible total.

questions.stem:
In a table visual, you need to color the Sales column background according to logic that is calculated in a DAX measure. The measure returns a hexadecimal color code such as #FF0000 for each row.
Which conditional formatting format style should you use?

options.text: Gradient
options.explanation: Gradient shades cells on a color scale between a minimum and a maximum value.

options.text: Data bars
options.explanation: Data bars draw a bar inside each cell and are not a way to apply a background color from a measure.

options.text: Field value
options.explanation: Field value uses the color code that a measure or column returns for each cell.

options.text: Rules
options.explanation: Rules apply fixed colors when the value meets ranges that you define, and they do not read a color from a measure.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A team develops reports in a Development workspace, tests them in a Test workspace, and then uses a Production workspace. When content moves between stages, the database server parameter must change automatically from the development server to the production server.
What should you use?

options.text: An email subscription that is sent after deployment
options.explanation: A subscription sends snapshots by email.

options.text: A workspace app with audiences for each stage
options.explanation: Audiences control what users see in an app and do not move content or change parameters.

options.text: A deployment pipeline with deployment rules
options.explanation: Deployment pipelines move content between stages, and deployment rules can change data source or parameter values for each stage.

options.text: A data alert on a tile of the production dashboard
options.explanation: A data alert notifies users about values on a tile.

questions.stem:
A sheet contains attribute names (Name, City, Age) down the first column. Each following column holds the values for one person. You need a table in which every person is one row and each attribute is a column with a proper header.
Which transformations should you apply?

options.text: Pivot Column on the first column, using the second column as values
options.explanation: Pivot Column needs attribute and value columns to exist already. In this layout they do not.

options.text: Group By on the first column with a Count Rows aggregation
options.explanation: Group By summarizes rows by key and does not rotate the table.

options.text: Unpivot Other Columns, and then rename the columns
options.explanation: Unpivot Other Columns would create attribute and value rows, which does not restore a person-per-row layout.

options.text: Transpose, and then use the first row as headers
options.explanation: Transpose swaps rows and columns so that each person becomes a row. The attribute names end up in the first row, which you promote to headers.

questions.topic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.stem:
A page contains a shape, a title, a card, and a line chart that form a panel. You need to move the objects together and to show or hide the whole panel with a single bookmark.
What should you do?

options.text: Put the objects in a hierarchy slicer.
options.explanation: A slicer filters data and does not hold report objects.

options.text: Merge the objects into a custom visual.
options.explanation: Visuals cannot be merged into one custom visual.

options.text: Lock the objects on the page.
options.explanation: Locking prevents objects from being moved or resized, and it does not combine them.

options.text: Group the objects in the Selection pane.
options.explanation: A group in the Selection pane acts as a single object, so it can be moved together and its visibility is controlled by one eye icon, which a bookmark can store.

questions.reference: Group and layer visuals by using the Selection pane

questions.stem: Users need to select a range of order dates by dragging a slider that has a start handle and an end handle. Which slicer style should you use on the OrderDate field?

options.text: Dropdown
options.explanation: Dropdown lists individual values in a collapsible list.

options.text: Between
options.explanation: The Between style shows a slider that has start and end handles for a numeric or date range.

options.text: List
options.explanation: List displays the values as a list of items to select.

options.text: Relative date
options.explanation: Relative date defines a period that is relative to today, such as the last 30 days, and it is not a slider with handles.

questions.topic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.stem: A matrix shows Category and ProductName on the rows. You need a measure that returns the total sales of the category on every product row, so each product row can be compared with its category total. Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], KEEPFILTERS(VALUES(Products[Category])))
options.explanation: KEEPFILTERS does not remove the product filter, so the result is still the product's own sales.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS(Products[Category]))
options.explanation: REMOVEFILTERS on Category removes the category filter but leaves the product filter in place, so the result is the product's own sales.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALLEXCEPT(Products, Products[Category]))
options.explanation: ALLEXCEPT removes all filters from Products except the filter on Category, so each product row returns its category total.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL(Products))
options.explanation: ALL(Products) removes the category filter as well, so every row returns the grand total.

questions.stem:
You need a slicer that always shows only the last 30 days of data, and that updates automatically each day without anyone editing the report.
What should you use?

options.text: A list slicer on the Year column
options.explanation: A year slicer filters entire years and not the last 30 days.

options.text: A relative date slicer set to the last 30 days
options.explanation: A relative date slicer is calculated from the current date, so the last 30 days move forward every day.

options.text: A between slicer with fixed start and end dates
options.explanation: Fixed dates must be changed manually as time passes.

options.text: A dropdown slicer on the Date column
options.explanation: A dropdown slicer on dates lists specific dates that the user must select.

questions.stem:
The Column distribution header for CustomerID in a table of 6 million rows shows 1,000 distinct values and 1,000 unique values. A colleague concludes that CustomerID has no duplicates and can be used as the key on the one side of a relationship.
What should you do before accepting this conclusion?

options.text: Change the column profiling scope to the entire data set
options.explanation: By default, profiling uses only the top 1,000 rows. Switching to the entire data set validates uniqueness across all 6 million rows.

options.text: Change the data type of the column to Text and profile it again
options.explanation: Changing the data type does not change how many rows are profiled.

options.text: Enable the Column quality view and check the Empty percentage
options.explanation: Column quality shows valid, error, and empty percentages. It does not change which rows are profiled.

options.text: Apply Table.Buffer to the query and check the Distinct count
options.explanation: Table.Buffer caches a table in memory. It has no effect on profiling.

questions.reference: Column profiling based on entire data set

questions.stem:
You need a calculated table that has one row per year and a column that contains the total sales of that year.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: GROUPBY('Date', 'Date'[Year], "Total Sales", SUM(Sales[Amount]))
options.explanation: GROUPBY aggregations must use CURRENTGROUP and iterator functions. SUM over a column does not work in GROUPBY.

options.text: DISTINCT('Date'[Year])
options.explanation: DISTINCT returns the unique years but no sales column.

options.text: SUMMARIZE('Date'[Year], "Total Sales", SUM(Sales[Amount]))
options.explanation: The first argument of SUMMARIZE must be a table. A column reference is not valid.

options.text: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS('Date'[Year], "Total Sales", SUM(Sales[Amount]))
options.explanation: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS groups by the Year column and adds a column for the aggregation. The relationship between Date and Sales supplies the filter.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model refresh took 10 minutes last week, and now it fails during the night. You need to see when each recent refresh started and ended, whether it succeeded, and the error message of the failed refresh.
Where should you look?

options.text: The Performance Analyzer pane
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer measures the load time of visuals in Power BI Desktop.

options.text: Refresh history of the semantic model
options.explanation: The refresh history lists the recent scheduled and manual refreshes with their start and end times, status, and error details.

options.text: The lineage view of the workspace
options.explanation: The lineage view shows dependencies between items.

options.text: The usage metrics report
options.explanation: A usage metrics report shows how many people view content.

questions.stem:
A PriceHistory table contains several rows for the same ProductID and EffectiveDate, and the Price value differs between those rows. You need exactly one row per ProductID and EffectiveDate and do not care which price remains.
What should you do?

options.text: Select the Price column, and then apply Remove Duplicates
options.explanation: Selecting only Price would remove rows that share a price, even for different products and dates.

options.text: Apply Keep Duplicates to all columns of the table, and then remove the null rows
options.explanation: Keep Duplicates keeps only the duplicated rows, and the opposite of the requirement.

options.text: Select ProductID and EffectiveDate, and then apply Remove Duplicates
options.explanation: Remove Duplicates considers only the selected columns. Selecting ProductID and EffectiveDate keeps one row for each combination.

options.text: Select all columns, and then apply Remove Duplicates
options.explanation: With all columns selected, rows that differ in Price are not duplicates, so every row remains.

questions.stem:
A report author must combine data from two different Power BI semantic models in a single report. Neither model may be copied or duplicated.
What should the author do?

options.text: Export each semantic model to Excel, import both files into one model, and create relationships between them
options.explanation: Exporting creates copies of the data, which the requirement forbids.

options.text: Create two live connections in the same report, one to each of the semantic models
options.explanation: A report can have only one live connection.

options.text: Create a composite model that uses DirectQuery for Power BI semantic models to connect to both models.
options.explanation: Composite models can use DirectQuery to connect to more than one Power BI semantic model, so the models are combined without copying their data.

options.text: Use Append Queries in Power Query to combine the tables of the two semantic models
options.explanation: Power Query cannot append queries over a live connection to a semantic model.

questions.reference: DirectQuery for Power BI semantic models and Analysis Services

questions.stem:
Your source tables contain tens of millions of rows. Authoring in Power BI Desktop is slow. You want to load only the first 10,000 rows from each table while you develop. After publishing, you want to load all rows by changing one value.
What should you do?

options.text: Apply a visual-level Top N filter to every visual, and remove the filter after publishing
options.explanation: Visual-level filters do not reduce the data that is loaded into the model.

options.text: Create a numeric Power Query parameter and use it as the row count in a Keep Top Rows step of each query.
options.explanation: A parameter-driven Keep Top Rows step limits the rows that are loaded. For SQL sources this step can usually fold into the source query. The parameter can later be changed to a large value, including from the service.

options.text: Create a what-if parameter and use it in a TOPN measure that limits the rows in visuals
options.explanation: A what-if parameter and a measure run after the data is loaded. The full tables would still be loaded into the model.

options.text: Create a calculated table that uses TOPN on each large table, and build the report on the calculated tables
options.explanation: A calculated table is created from data that has already been loaded, so the full tables would still be imported.

questions.reference: Power Query parameters and query folding

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A model has the tables UserRegion (Email, Region), Region (Region), and Sales. UserRegion has a many-to-one relationship to Region, Region has a one-to-many relationship to Sales, and all relationships have single-direction cross-filtering. You define a role with the filter UserRegion[Email] = USERPRINCIPALNAME(). Users in the role still see the sales of all regions.
What should you do?

options.text: Create a calculated table that duplicates UserRegion, and apply the filter to it
options.explanation: A copy of the table has the same problem, and the filter would not reach Region.

options.text: Remove the filter from the UserRegion table, and define the filter on the Region table instead
options.explanation: Without the filter, no restriction would be applied at all.

options.text: Change the Sales to Region relationship to many-to-many, and keep the same role filter
options.explanation: A many-to-many relationship would not solve the direction of the filter and would add ambiguity.

options.text: Enable bidirectional filtering on UserRegion to Region, and apply the security filter both ways
options.explanation: The filter on UserRegion must flow to Region and then to Sales. With a single direction relationship, the filter does not flow from the many side to the one side. Applying the security filter in both directions lets it reach Region.

questions.reference: Dynamic RLS with a security table

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem: Your model contains Sales[OrderDate], which has values from 2022 to 2026, and Employees[BirthDate], which has values from 1955 to 2002. A date table created with CALENDARAUTO() runs from 1955 to 2026. You need a date table that covers only the complete calendar years that are needed for the order dates. Which formula should you use?

options.text: CALENDAR(MIN(Sales[OrderDate]), MAX(Sales[OrderDate]))
options.explanation: CALENDAR with MIN and MAX uses the exact first and last order dates, so the first and last years can be incomplete.

options.text: CALENDARAUTO(1)
options.explanation: CALENDARAUTO still uses every date column in the model, including BirthDate.

options.text: CALENDAR(DATE(YEAR(MIN(Sales[OrderDate])), 1, 1), DATE(YEAR(MAX(Sales[OrderDate])), 12, 31))
options.explanation: CALENDAR with the first day of the first year and the last day of the last year creates complete years that are based only on the OrderDate column.

options.text: CALENDARAUTO(12)
options.explanation: CALENDARAUTO scans all date columns in the model, including BirthDate. The argument only sets the fiscal year end month.

questions.topic: Design and implement a data model
questions.stem:
You need to group customers into the bands Under 30, 30 to 50, and Over 50, based on an Age column. Report authors must use the band on slicers and as a visual axis.
Which model object should you create?

options.text: A measure
options.explanation: A measure returns an aggregated value in the context of a visual. It cannot be placed on an axis or used as a slicer field.

options.text: A calculated column
options.explanation: A calculated column stores a value for each row, so it can be used on an axis or in a slicer.

options.text: A calculation group
options.explanation: A calculation group changes how measures are calculated. It does not categorize rows.

options.text: A what-if parameter
options.explanation: A what-if parameter provides a range of numeric input values and does not categorize customers.

questions.stem:
Your organization wants to use Copilot in Power BI to help create report pages.
What is required to use Copilot in a report?

options.text: The report must contain a Q&A visual on at least one of its pages
options.explanation: A Q&A visual is not a requirement for using Copilot.

options.text: The report must be created as a paginated report in Power BI Report Builder
options.explanation: Copilot features for report pages apply to interactive reports and are not limited to paginated reports.

options.text: The report must use a semantic model in DirectQuery mode that is connected through a gateway
options.explanation: Copilot does not depend on the storage mode of the model.

options.text: The workspace must be assigned to a paid Fabric or Premium capacity that supports Copilot
options.explanation: Copilot in Power BI requires the workspace to be assigned to a capacity that supports Copilot, and tenant settings must also allow it.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
questions.stem:
A user must be able to add Contributors and Viewers to a workspace and publish the workspace app. The user must not be able to delete the workspace or add other Admins.
Which workspace role should you assign?

options.text: Admin
options.explanation: Admins can delete the workspace and add other Admins, which the requirement excludes.

options.text: Member
options.explanation: Members can add people with the same or lower roles, such as Members, Contributors, and Viewers, and can publish the app, but they cannot delete the workspace or add Admins.

options.text: Contributor
options.explanation: Contributors cannot manage access and cannot publish the app.

options.text: Viewer
options.explanation: Viewers can only view and interact with content.

questions.stem:
You have two queries, Customers and Orders, that share the CustomerID column. You need a list of customers who have never placed an order.
Which merge join kind should you use when Customers is the first table and Orders is the second table?

options.text: Inner
options.explanation: An inner join returns only customers who have matching orders.

options.text: Left Anti
options.explanation: A left anti join returns only the rows from the first table that have no match in the second table, which finds customers without orders.

options.text: Left Outer
options.explanation: A left outer join returns all customers, including those that have orders, so you would still need a filter.

options.text: Right Anti
options.explanation: A right anti join returns the rows of the second table that have no match in the first table, which would list orders without customers.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You are configuring incremental refresh for a Sales table that has an OrderDate column of the Date/Time type. In Power Query you create the parameters needed for the filter.
Which parameters should you create?

options.text: IncrementalStart and IncrementalEnd, both of the Date/Time type
options.explanation: The names are reserved and must be exactly RangeStart and RangeEnd.

options.text: StartDate and EndDate, both of the Date type
options.explanation: The parameter names must be RangeStart and RangeEnd, and the type must be Date/Time.

options.text: RangeStart and RangeEnd, both of the Date/Time type
options.explanation: Incremental refresh requires two parameters with the exact reserved names RangeStart and RangeEnd, and the type Date/Time.

options.text: RangeStart and RangeEnd, both of the Text type
options.explanation: Text parameters cannot be used to filter a Date/Time column for incremental refresh.

questions.stem:
You merge two queries in Power Query.
Which two join kinds return all rows from the first table, whether or not a matching row exists in the second table? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Full Outer
options.explanation: A full outer join returns all rows from both tables, so all rows of the first table are included.

options.text: Left Anti
options.explanation: A left anti join returns only the first-table rows that have no match, not all the rows.

options.text: Inner
options.explanation: An inner join returns only rows that have matches in both tables.

options.text: Right Outer
options.explanation: A right outer join returns all rows from the second table and only the matching rows from the first table.

options.text: Left Outer
options.explanation: A left outer join returns every row from the first table and the matching rows from the second table.

questions.stem:
You need to show the current month's sales compared with a monthly sales target, together with a small trend over the previous months, in a single visual.
Which visual should you use?

options.text: Card
options.explanation: A card shows a single value and has no target or trend.

options.text: Gauge
options.explanation: A gauge shows progress between a minimum and a maximum value and has no trend axis.

options.text: Slicer
options.explanation: A slicer filters other visuals and does not display measures.

options.text: KPI
options.explanation: A KPI visual shows the current value against a target and uses a trend axis to show how the value changed over time.

questions.stem:
A line chart shows daily Total Sales over two years. You need Power BI to automatically mark the days with unusual values and suggest possible explanations.
What should you do?

options.text: Convert the line chart to a ribbon chart
options.explanation: A ribbon chart shows rank changes of categories and not anomalies.

options.text: Add a trend line from the Analytics pane
options.explanation: A trend line shows the overall direction and does not mark individual unusual values.

options.text: Add Find anomalies from the Analytics pane
options.explanation: Anomaly detection marks the points that differ significantly from the expected pattern of a time series and can propose explanations.

options.text: Add a constant line at the average value
options.explanation: A constant line marks one fixed level and does not detect anomalies by itself.

questions.stem:
You need a measure that returns the sales of the three months that end at the last date in the current filter context, which is a rolling three-month total.
Which expression should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESINPERIOD('Date'[Date], MAX('Date'[Date]), -3, MONTH))
options.explanation: DATESINPERIOD returns the dates in a period that ends at the specified date and goes back three months, which gives a rolling three-month window.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], PARALLELPERIOD('Date'[Date], -3, MONTH))
options.explanation: PARALLELPERIOD shifts the current period by three months instead of extending it, so the result is the period three months ago.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], PREVIOUSMONTH('Date'[Date]))
options.explanation: PREVIOUSMONTH returns only the previous month, and it excludes the current month.

options.text: CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATEADD('Date'[Date], -3, MONTH))
options.explanation: DATEADD shifts the current dates back three months and returns the shifted period, not a window that ends at the current date.
